127  COUNTY EXECUTIVE   OF   MERU   –   NO.12  REPORT ON THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS  Basis for Qualified   Opinion  294.   Payment   of Undisclosed Legal Fees  The statement of financial performance reflect use of goods and services amount of  Kshs.1,585,636,068 which as disclosed in Note 10 to the financial statements includes  other operating expenses amount of Kshs.310,276,980. The latter amount further,  include s   legal   payments   totalling   Kshs.140,507,214   out   of   which   an   amount   of  Kshs.100,000,000 related to part payment of a contingent liability of Kshs. 756,757,420  disclosed in the previous audit report. However, Management did not retain withholding  tax from the   advocate’s payment as required by law.  Further, payments totalling Kshs.40,507,214 in respect of legal cases were not disclosed  in the financial records. The expenditures were not budgeted for and no explanation was  provided on how such unapproved and   unplanned expenditure was processed and paid.  In addition, details of the court cases, fee requisitions indicating amount, taxed amount,  the amount paid, unpaid balances and status of the cases were not provided for audit.  In the   circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the legal fees amount of  Kshs.140,507,214 could not be confirmed.  295.   Unsupported Transfers to Other Government Entities  The statement of financial performance reflects transfers to other government entities  amount of Kshs.766,771,028 which includes Facility Improvement Fund (FIF) amount of  Kshs.108,648,141   and   transfers   to   other   county   government   entities   amount   of  Kshs.529 ,412,779 as disclosed in Note 11 to the financial statements. The transfers  amount   of   Kshs.529,412,779   further   includes   Donor   (DANIDA)   funds   amount   of  Kshs.29,495,006 also transferred to primary healthcare facilities. However, Authority to  Incur Expenditur e (AIEs), payment vouchers, stores receipts vouchers (S13) and project  implementation status reports were not provided for audit.  Further,   various medical services, key personnel and equipment in the hospitals , the  staffing levels, the equipment at the f acilities as prescribed by the Kenya Quality Model  for Health Policy Guidelines, bank reconciliation statements and reimbursements amount  on claims from Social Health Authority (SHA) and Social Fund Health Insurance (SHIF)  were not provided for audit.  In   the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of   transfers to other government  entities amount of Kshs .138,143,147 could not be confirmed.  296.   Unreconciled Long Outstanding Refund on Borrowing  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 1 5 to the financial statements  reflect receivables from non - exchange transactions balance of Kshs.1,650,794,342 which  excluded   borrowings   by   Meru   Micro - finance   Corporation   totalling   Kshs.1,400,000.

128  Review of   debtors’   records revealed that the amount was borrowed from the County  Executive to facilitate payment of salaries for the Corporation’s employees in March,  2018. However, no satisfactory explanation was given on why the debt was remained  unsettled as at 30 June,   2025.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and regularity of the long outstanding debtors balance  of Kshs.1,400,000 could not be confirmed.  297.   Unsupported Trade and Other Payables  The   statement   of   financial   position   reflects   trade   and   other   payables   balance   of  Kshs.3,415,572,399, as disclosed in Note 17 to the financial statements. However, the  supporting ledgers reflected a balance of Kshs.3,428,210,299 resulting in a variance of  K shs.12,837,900. Further, review of payables records provided for audit revealed that the  County   Executive   submitted   to   the   Controller   of   Budget,   payables   totalling  Kshs.1,741,933,778, resulting in another unreconciled and unexplained variance of  Kshs.1,673 ,638,621.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the trade and other payables  balance of Kshs.3,415,572,399 could not be confirmed.  298.   Unreconciled Kenya Medical Supplies Authority Debt  The   statement   of   financial   position   reflects   trade   and   other   payables   balance   of  Kshs.3,415,572,399. As disclosed in Note 17 to the financial statements, the balance of  trade and other payables includes payables to Kenya Medical Supplies Authority of  Kshs.43,412,108 for the supply of drugs and medical supplie s.   However, the Authority’s  records   reflects   a   balance   of   Kshs. 105,367,569,   resulting   in   an   unreconciled   and  unexplained variance of Kshs .61,955,461.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the trade and other payables  balance of Kshs.3,41 5,572,399 could not be confirmed.  299.   Outstanding Retentions and Deposits Refund  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 18 to the financial statements  reflect refundable deposits and prepayments balance of   Kshs.89,224,553. The balance  is in respect of retention money withheld by the County Executive   which should be  maintained in a designated deposit account. The opening balance reflects a balance of  Kshs.86,843,700   and   the   County   Executive   procured   capital   p rojects   totalling  Kshs.705,357,090 as reflected in the statement of cash flows. However, the movement  in the refundable deposits during the year was not disclosed in the Notes to the financial  statements.   Further,   the   deposit   bank   account   revealed   a   closin g   balance   of  Kshs.40,824,224,   resulting   in   an   unexplained   and   unreconciled   variance   of  Kshs.48,400,329.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of refundable deposits and  retentions balance of Kshs.89,224,553 could not be confirmed.

129  300.   Unexpla ined Voided Transactions  Analysis of the Integrated Financial Management Information System ( IFMIS) payments  indicated   that   four   hundred   and   ninety - six   (496)   transactions   with   a   value   of  Kshs.766,804,548 were voided during the year under review. However,   Management did  not provide a reconciliation to confirm whether the voided transactions were subsequently  paid   and that the Controller of Budget was notified of the voided transactions.  In the circumstances,   the accuracy and regularity of the voided transactions totalling  Kshs.766,804,548 could not be confirmed .  Emphasis of Matter  301.   Budgetary   Control and   Performa nce  The statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts reflects final receipts budget  and   actual   on   comparable   basis   of   Kshs.12,452,916,563   and   Kshs.9,054,751,662  respectively, resulting in an under - funding of Kshs. 3,398,164,901   or 27% of the budget .  However, the County Executive spent an amount of Kshs. 8,241,985,043   against actual  receipts of Kshs. 9,054,751,662   resulting in an under - utilization of Kshs. 812,766,619   or  9% of the actual receipts.  The under - funding affected the planned activities and   may have impacted negatively on  service delivery to the public.  My opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.  Other Matter  302.   Unresolved Prior Year Audit Matters  In the previous year’s audit report, several issues were raised under the   Report on  Financial   Statements,   Report   on   Lawfulness   and   Effectiveness   in   Use   of   Public  Resources, and Report on Effectiveness of Internal Controls, Risk Management and  Governance. Review of the status during audit of the County Executive in 2024/2025  reve aled that thirty - seven matters as listed at the end of this report remained unresolved  as at 30 June, 2025 .  Other Information  There were no material issues relating to Other Information.  REPORT   ON   LAWFULNESS   AND   EFFECTIVENESS   IN   THE   USE   OF   PUBLIC  RESOURCES  Basis for Conclusion  303.   Delayed Passing of the Budget by the County Assembly  Review of the budget process   revealed   that the County Assembly of Meru did not approve  the County Government’s annual budget estimates   within the statutory deadline of

130  30 June, as required under the Public Finance Management Act, 2012. The budget was  instead passed on 13 August, 2024. This was contrary to Section 129(7) of the Public  Finance   Management   Act, 2012, which r equires timely approval of budget estimates to  ensure the smooth commencement of government operations at the start of each financial  year. The County Treasury is also obligated to submit the estimates in good time to  facilitate adequate review and deliber ation.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  304.   Delayed Disbursement of Exchequer Releases  Review of County Revenue Fund (CRF) bank statements revealed receipts totalling  Kshs. 1,640,816,129 were received after 15 June, 2025. This   was contrary to Section  17(6) of the Public Finance Management Act, 2012 which provides among others that;  The National Treasury shall administer the Consolidated Fund in accordance with Article  206 of the Constitution and facilitate payment into that acco unt all monies raised or  received by or on behalf of the National Government, and pay from that National  Exchequer Account without undue delay all amounts that are payable for public services.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  305.   Non - Compliance   with   Fiscal   Responsibility   Principles   on   Development  Expenditure  The statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts reflects total expenditure  amount   of   Kshs.8,241,985,042   comprising   recurrent   and   development   expenditure  amount of Ksh s.7,536,627,953, and Kshs.705,357,090 respectively. The development  expenditure accounted for only 9% of the total expenditure which was below the 30%  threshold stipulated by Regulation 25(1)(g) of the Public Finance Management (County  Governments) Regulat ions, 2015.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  306.   Projects Implementation Status  The statement of comparison of budget and actuals reflects actual receipts amount of  Kshs.8,241,985,042 which includes acquisition of property, plant   and equipment amount  totalling Kshs.705,357,090. However, the following observations were made;  306.1.   Overlapping Scope between Works done by Mechanical Transport Fund  and   Contractors  Review of the development cashbook revealed that an amount of Kshs. 223,000,000 was  paid to the Department of Roads   -   Mechanical Transport Fund (MTF) for gravelling of all -  weather roads and culvert works. Further, the County Executive awarded contracts  totalling   Kshs.493,777,736   to   various   contractors   for   similar   civil   wor ks.   However,  mapping and identification of which works were to be done and details of the roadworks  by the Mechanical Transport Fund and individual contractors was not provided for audit.

131  306.2.   Incomplete Works at Timau Stadium  The County Executive incurred an expenditure amount of Kshs.1,861,445 in respect of  the construction of Timau stadium toilet.   However, physical inspection carried out in  June, 2025 revealed that the toilet had not been constructed. Further, the existing   gates  at the facility had been vandalized and no   dais   was in place.  306.3.   Incomplete Execution of Low Voltage Board Works at Kanyakine   Hospital  The County Executive   through the Department for Health awarded a contract for supply,  installation and commissioning of low voltage board at Kanyakine Sub - County Hospital  to a local contractor through an open national tender. The contract agreement was signed  on 2 May, 2023 fo r a contract sum of Kshs.8,958,007. Two (2) certificates of payment  were raised with the second and final payment of Kshs.1,861,026 paid on 30 September,  2024. However, physical inspection at the Hospital in June, 2025 revealed that the board  had been moun ted but there was no evidence of connection to the power supply system.  Further, test reports and commissioning certificates to confirm that commissioning  activities had been carried out were not provided for audit. This resulted in the Hospital  relying   on outdated electrical infrastructure. In addition, procurement documents were not  provided for audit.  I n the circumstances, the value for money on the expenditure on the above projects could  not be confirmed.  307.   Failure to Utilise   Completed Projects  307.1.   Ablution   Block   and   Laboratory   at   Kenya   Medical   Training   College   -  Miathene   Campus  The   County Executive awarded a tender for construction of an ablution block and  laboratory at Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) Miathene Campus at a cost of  Kshs.8,893,027. The project was to commence in January, 2022 and was scheduled for  completion   in   Au gust,   2022.   The   project   was   inspected   and   accepted   on  30 November, 2023 one year after the intended completion date.   Physical inspection  carried out in June, 2025 revealed that both the ablution blocks (male and female)   and  the laboratory were not in use.   Further, no provision for water supply to these facilities  was incorporated during project planning, which further constrained their utilization and  effective operation hindering their use.  307.2.   Kiguchwa   Dispensary  The   County Executive awarded to a   local contractor a contract at a   cost of Kshs.999,251  for renovation works at Kiguchwa Dispensary, with a scheduled completion date of  30 June, 2023.   However, physical inspection of the dispensary   revealed that several  renovation works were completed on the maternity block in June, 2023 despite the block  having originally been commissioned on 3 August, 2015. Despite the recent renovations,  the maternity block remained underutilized due to persistent   understaffing at the facility.

132  307.3.   Modern Roof Shed at Kinoro Market  The contract for construction of a modern roof shed at Kinoro Market was awarded to   a  local merchant   at a contract sum of Kshs. 1,279,619. The project inspection certificate  was   issued on 15 February, 2024. Physical inspection carried out in June, 2025 revealed  that the works were complete. However, the market was not in use and was instead  occupied   by   boda - boda   riders.   The   responsible   Department   did   not   provide   any  explanation f or the failure to operationalize the project promptly to ensure the intended  economic benefits were realized.  307.4.   Timau Market Roofing  The   County Executive incurred an expenditure of Kshs.6,174,861 in respect of roofing.  However, the market has remained id le for over one year.  307.5.   Grill Fixing at Mari t ati Market  The County Executive incurred an expenditure amount of Kshs.3,120,680 for fixing grills  at Maritati   Market. However, the project has remained unutilized for over one year.  307.6.   Alterations and Installations of Steel Grills at Marimati Perimeter Wall  The   County Executive awarded a contract for alterations and installations of steel grills at  Marimati perimeter wall at a cost of Kshs.3,120,680.   Physical inspection carried out in  June, 2025 revealed that although the works were completed, the project remain ed as it  had not been put into use for over one year.  In the circumstances, the value for money spent on projects and delivery of the intended  economic and social benefits to the public could not be confirmed.  308.   Delayed Proposed Construction of County Ag gregation and Industrial Park  The State Department for Industry invited bids for construction of the proposed County  Aggregation and Industrial Park (CAIP). Seven (7) bidders submitted their documents and  the contract was awarded to a local merchant at a contract sum of Kshs.492,212,74 1.  Review of the project file provided for audit revealed that one of the unsuccessful bidders  who had quoted a contract sum of Kshs.465,320,261 was disqualified at the mechanical  works evaluation stage for failing to attach sub - contractor details. However , Section 111  on evaluation and qualification criteria provided only mandatory requirements for main  contractor and did not specify mandatory documentations for sub - contractors. It was  therefore, not clear why the bidder who had   submitted   the lowest bid by   Kshs.26,892,480  was disqualified. The County Executive may have prepared skewed or tailored technical  specifications, resulting in unfair competition. This was contrary to Section 149(1) of the  Public Finance Management Act, 2012 which requires an Account ing Officer to ensure  that resources of the entity for which the officer is designated are used in a way that is  effective, efficient, economical and transparent. Further, Management has since paid the  contractor an amount of Kshs.478,499,999. However, th e corresponding bank statement  for the project was not provided for audit.

133  In the circumstances, the value for money for the expenditure on the above project could  not be confirmed.  309.   Non - Compliance with the Public Procurement Capacity Building Levy Order ,  2023  Review of contract records revealed that the County Executive entered into several  procurement contracts. However, but no documentary evidence was provided to confirm  that the County Executive complied with paragraph 3(1) of the Public Procurement  Capacity Building Levy, Order 2023 which provides that there shall be paid a levy by a  supplier on all procurement contracts signed between the supplier and a procuring entity,  at the rate of point zero three per centum (0.03%) of the value of the signed   contract,  exclusive of applicable taxes.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the Levy Order, 2023.  310.   Non - Compliance with Fiscal Responsibility Principles on Wages  The   County   Executive   incurred   an   expenditure on   salaries and   wages amounting  Kshs.4,620,092,462 which translates to 45% of the total revenues during the year under  review   of Kshs.10,217,151,933. This was contrary to Regulation 25(1)(a) and (b) of the  Publi c Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which stipulates  that the County Government’s expenditure on wages and benefits for its public officers,  shall not exceed thirty - five percent (35%) of the County Government’s total revenue.  In the   circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  311.   Irregularities in Human Resource Matters  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 9 to the financial  statements reflects an amount of Kshs.4,620,092,462 in respect of compensatio n of  employees. Review of employees’ records revealed the following unsatisfactory matters:  311.1.   Centralized Budgeting for Staff Costs  Review of employee costs revealed that the budget for staff costs for all departments was  made under the vote Meru   -   Publi c Service Management and Administration (Vote 3569),  yet each Department’s Accounting Officer (the Chief Officer) is responsible for identifying  staffing needs, preparing recruitment requests, and submitting them to the County Public  Service Board (CPSB).   This was contrary to Regulations 119(2) and (3) of the Public  Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which provides that t he  budgetary allocation for personnel costs shall be determined based on a detailed costing  of a human capital plan   of a County Government entity as approved by the responsible  County Department for Public Service Management matters, the County Public Service  Board and County Treasury. Regulation   3 provides that t he Accounting Officer of a  County Government   entity shall ensure that the personnel cost of all appointees, as well  as promotion and salary increase, can be met within the budgetary allocation voted for  the County Government entity.

134  311.2.   Failure to Budget and Pay Gratuity to Contracted   Employees  The County Executive engaged contracted employees but did not honor the terms of the  contracts as gratuity payable upon completion of the contract period was not paid. Further  the terms of the contract kept on changing after every contract renew al. No explanation  was given why the County Executive failed to pay or set aside funds for gratuity to the  contracted employees. This was contrary to Paragraph 6.6.2 of the Employment Contract  Between Meru County Public Service Board which provides that t he employee and the  contracted employee for the provision of services on contract shall upon successful  completion of the contract the employee will be entitled to thirty (30) calendar days’ wages  in lieu of gratuity.  In the circumstances, Management was   in breach of the employment contract.  312.   Irregularities in the Human Resource System  Review of human resources records revealed that the County Executive engaged a local  contractor on Phase 2 of an unknown contract sum for a contract to deliver, install, test,  and commission an Integrated County Human Resource System   (HRIS - Ke). The vendor  initiated the second phase of the works which was being done through data collection.  However, the contract was not provided for audit. Review of the data collection report  revealed the following anomalies;  312.1.   Unverified Workers  Review of the data colle ction report from the Vendor revealed that the County Executive  had a total of six thousand, two hundred and five (6,205) staff members out of which, five  thousand, six hundred and twenty - eight (5,628) employees were verified leaving five  hundred and seven ty - seven (577) staff unaccounted for. Further, review and audit of the  payroll in June, 2025 revealed a workforce of five thousand, eight hundred and fifty - seven  (5,857) resulting in an unreconciled variance of one thousand, three hundred and forty -  eight ( 1,348) between the Vendor staff numbers and the audited staff. The inconsistency  in respect of the staff members' records was not explained.  312.2.   Staff Under Probation for More than the Stipulated Period  Review of the payroll records revealed that an amoun t of Kshs.343,604,330 was paid to  five hundred and ninety - eight (598) staff members who were on probation for more than  one year. This was contrary to   Paragraph   B.16 (1)   of the County Public Service Human  Resource Manual, 2013 which provides that w here vac ancies exist in the pensionable  establishment, candidates recruited to fill such vacancies shall be appointed on probation  for six (6) months. No explanation was provided for the extended period on probation.  312.3.   Salaries Paid to Unknown Staff  Review of sampled human resource records in the County Executive payroll revealed that  an amount of Kshs.9,486,690 was paid to employees who did not offer services to the  County Executive and were subsequently removed from the payroll as detailed below:   -

135  (i)   A Medical Officer was granted a four - year study leave and bonded to serve the  County for four (4) years upon completion. At the time of approval, the officer  had served only two (2) years. There was no evidence that the officer resumed  duty after comple ting the study leave.   Despite the   lack of   resumption , the officer  continued to receive salary, leading to a potential loss of Kshs.9,486,690 for  the four (4) years from the expected date of return date of 21 October, 2021.  (ii)   The Medical   Officer was   posted t o the County Executive by the Transitional  Authority in June, 2015 and acknowledged by then County Chief Officer of  Health. However, job designation remained Medical Officer Intern, Job Group  L since the officer was posted. The officer’s request to pursue   a Masters of  Medicine (Family Medicine) was approved by the County Public Service Board  and released vide a letter ref: 2014005244/TY/(17) dated 29 August, 2017. The  release letter being signed by the then Acting Chief officer Health. The rules  governing t he award of scholarship was signed by the officer on 7 September,  2017 and bonding forms were completed and signed on 25 August, 2017. The  bonding period was four (4) years or Kshs.10,155,150 payable to Chief Officer  for Health on behalf of the County Exec utive in case of breach.   However, as  at the time of audit in June, 2025, there was no evidence in the staff personal  file confirming completion of studies, no evidence that the officer resumed duty  or any payment in lieu of the bond. The last document in   the personal file (data  sheet) was filled and completed on 6 April, 2018. The staff was also not in the  Chief Officer of Health staff returns submitted for audit and did not turn up for  physical count conducted on 12 March, 2025.  In the circumstances, Ma nagement was in breach of the law and value for money  could not be confirmed.  313.   Non - Compliance with the Law Staff Ethnic Composition  Review of personnel records revealed that the County Executive had five thousand, eight  hundred and fifty - seven   (5,857) staff out of which five thousand two hundred and twelve  (5,212) representing 89% were from the dominant ethnic community in the County. This  was contrary to the requirements of Section 7(1) and   (2) of the National Cohesion and  Integration Act, 2008   which states that no public establishment shall have more than one  third of its staff from the same ethnic community.  Further, the dominant community represented 88% of the new recruitment conducted in  2024/2025.   This was contrary to Section 65(1) of th e County Governments Act, 2012,  which provides that in selecting candidates for appointment, the County Public Service  Board shall consider the need to ensure that at least thirty percent (30%) of the vacant  posts at entry level are filled by candidates wh o are not from the dominant ethnic  community in the county.  In the circumstances,   Management was in breach of the law.

136  314.   Irregular Payments for Subscription  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 10 to the financial  statements reflect use of goods and services amount of Kshs.1,585,636,068 which  includes other operating expenses amount of Kshs.310,276,980 out of which amounts of  Kshs.6,000,000 and Kshs.300,000   were paid to   the Council of Governors and   County  Public Ser vice Board National Consultative Forum, respectively .   However, supporting  documents   such as   legal framework,   invoices and contract agreements   for the   basis of  the payment were not provided for audit. This was contrary to   Section 37 of the  Intergovernmenta l Relations Act, 2012 which provides that the operational expenses in  respect of the structures and institutions established by the Act shall be provided for in  the annual estimates of the revenue and expenditure of the National Government to cater  for; th e Summit, the Council of County Governors, the Technical Committee, Secretariat,  and the sectoral working group established by the Technical Committee and the sectoral  working groups established by the Council.  In the circumstances, Management was in brea ch of the law.  315.   Failure to Establish Sub - County (Level 4) Hospitals  The County Executive had nine (9) established Sub - counties. However, the County  Executive had only established seven (7) sub – county hospitals. Further, there was no  evidence to prove tha t the County Executive established a County Health Management  Team, a Health Quality and Assurance Unit, a Health Facility Improvement Board and a  Policy on transfer of unutilized pharmaceutical and non   –   pharmaceuticals from one  health facility to another   to ensure efficient stock management. This was contrary to  Section 8 (1) of the Meru County Health Services Act, 2016 which provides that there  shall be at least one county hospital, at least one sub – county hospital in each sub – county,  and at least one he alth center in each ward.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  316.   Failure to Enact County Finance Act  Review   of   the   County   Executive’s   legislative   framework   revealed   that   the   County  Executive continued to rely on the Finance Act of 2019 for the imposition of taxes, fees,  and charges for services. The Act, which was passed in line with the 2019/2020 financial  year's budget proposals was no t revised to reflect subsequent annual budgets and  prevailing economic realities. As a result ,   the current rates for various County services do  not align with inflation and the increased cost of service delivery.  In the circumstances, Management was in   breach of the law .

137  REPORT ON EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROLS, RISK MANAGEMENT  AND GOVERNANCE  Basis for Conclusion  317.   Weaknesses in the Management of Fixed Asset  Review of the County Executive’s assets register revealed that Management   did not  update   its fixed assets register in year under review. Review of sampled procurement  records and physical inspection revealed that assets acquired over several financial  years, including   some identified in the year under review   totalling Kshs.3,959,399 had not  b een recorded in the assets register.  Further, Regulation 136(1) of the (County Governments), Public Finance Management  Regulations, 2015 requires County Governments to maintain an updated asset register  that records all fixed and movable assets. This   includes tagging assets and keeping  detailed records such as the cost of acquisition, asset location, and condition.   Physical  inspection of sampled office desks, chairs and desktops revealed that the assets were  not tagged.  In the circumstances, the effec tiveness of internal controls on management and safe  custody of fixed assets could not be confirmed.  318.   Lack of Approved Training Policy, Needs Assessment, and Annual Training  Plan  The County Executive did not have in place an approved Training Policy, an approved  Annual Training Plan, or evidence of a Training Needs Assessment (TNA). Additionally,  the County's Human Resource Manual was still in draft form, which contributed to the   lack  of formalized training and development procedures and frameworks. This was contrary  to   Section H 2   (3) of the   Human Resource Policies and Procedures Manual for Public  Service, 2016, which requires that   nomination and selection for individual and group  training shall be based on prioritized training projections. The policy also requires that the  approved programmes should address National, Organizational and individual goals.  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of training programmes in the County   Executive  could not be confirmed.
