Irregular Operation of a Commercial Bank Account  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 21 to the financial statements,  reflects cash and cash equivalents balance of Kshs.334,439,455. Review of bank  documents revealed that the Count y Executive operated a commercial bank account  under the name of Machakos County National Agri Value Chain which had a balance of  Kshs.77,687,164.   However, payments from this account were not processed through  Integrated Financial Management Information Sy stem (IFMIS) contrary to the donor’s  requirement that all payments must be processed through IFMIS.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the donor requirements.  403.   Completion of Early Childhood Development Education Centres  The contract for construction of Kitooni, Nguluni AIC and Kangundo   Early Childhood  Development Education Centres   (ECDE) classes Lot 1 was awarded at a contract sum  of Kshs.4,405,819. However, the contract was terminated after issuance of certificate  number   1 valued at Kshs.2,633,831. The amount was paid and another firm was awarded  the contract to complete the ECDE classrooms at a contract sum of Kshs.3,047,459 which  increased the total cost of the project from the initial amount of Kshs.4,405,819 to  Kshs.5 ,681,290. However, the valuation report of the remaining works after termination

171  of the first contract and engineers estimates for the new Bill of Quantities were not  provided for audit review. Although Management   explained that   the increase was due to  inc lusion of   floor   tiles which were not in the first contract and due to fluctuation of prices,  no documents were provided for audit in support of this explanation.  In the circumstances, value for money on the above project could not be confirmed.  404.   Stalled Construction of Twin Workshops at Matuu   Vocational Training Centre  The contract for construction of two (2) twin workshops at Matuu   Vocational Training  Centre ( VTC )   was awarded at a contract sum of Kshs.17,393,550. However, the contract  agreement signed on 26 June, 2023 did not indicate the contract period. Further, although  the first valuation certificate was raised on 6 March, 2024 for payment of Kshs.6,506,239,  no   payment had been made as at the time of audit in June, 2025 and the contractor was  not on site.  In the circumstances, value for money on the project amounting to Kshs.17,393,550 could  not be confirmed.  405.   Non - Operationalization   of   a   Twin   Workshop   at   Kamwa nyani   Vocational  Training Centre  The contract   for the proposed construction of a twin workshop at Kamwanyani Vocational  Training Centre   was awarded   at a contract sum of Kshs.12,556,200. However, the  workshop was completed but lacked adequate   equipment and essential tools required for  effective delivery of tertiary courses offered which included carpentry, tailoring and hair  dressing among others.  In the circumstances, value for money on the project amounting to Kshs.12,556,200 could  not be co nfirmed.  406.   Irregular Supply and Delivery of Milk for Early Childhood Development and  Education Centers  The contract for supply and delivery of 629,000 (200ml) packets of milk was awarded at a  contract sum of Kshs.38 per packet as per evaluation report date d 28 December, 2023  with   implementation   period   of   ninety   (90)   days   under   framework   agreement   which  involved seven (7) suppliers. However, the firm signed a contract of one year dated  12 January, 2 024 despite the tender document stating ninety (90) days implementation  period. During the year under review, the firm was paid an amount of Kshs.51,769,612 for  supply and delivery of 1,362,346 (200ml) packets of milk for ECDE Centers. Further, the  firm co ntinued to supply milk to the County Executive even after supplying the total of  629,000 packets of milk stated in the tender documents. Although Management explained  that the contract was extended for one (1)   year, there   were no call - off orders, or any other  mini competition done to give chance to the other six (6) firms having framework  agreements with the County Executive.  In the circumstances, the regularity and value for money on the expenditure incurred on  the   programme could not be confirmed.

172  407.   Non -   Renewal of Performance Bond and Insurance  The contract   for construction of phased development of ultra - modern - multi - purpose and  discipline sports complex in Machakos New   City was awarded at   a contract sum of  Kshs.1 ,107,250,003. As   at the time of audit the   performance bond and insurance for  material damage and third - party liability had expired on 10 May, 2025 and 9 July, 2025  respectively. However, no renewal had been done. Further, valuation certificate number 2  val ued the swimming pool works at an amount of Kshs.21,052,820. However, the amount  did not have a detailed   breakdown   of specific works which were done by the contractor.  In the circumstances, assurance and continued performance by the contractor and  eventual completion of the project could not be confirmed.  408.   Failure to Retain   Facilities Improvement Funds   at the Hospitals  Review of revenue records obtained from Level 4 and Level 5 health facilities in   Machakos  County revealed that   eleven   ( 11 ) health facilities collected a total Kshs. 605,516,224  towards   the   Health   Facilities   Improvement.   Out   of   this   amount,   a   total   of  Kshs.1 92,379,722   was transferred to County Revenue Fund. However, the County  Treasury reimburse d a total of Kshs.1 00,618,500   to the health facilities resulting in a  deficit of Kshs. 91,761,222 .   This was contrary to Section 5(1) of the Facilities Improvement  Financing Act, 2023 which requires that all monies raised or received by or on behalf of  all P ublic Health Facilities be retained in the Hospital Facilities Improvement Financing  Account. In addition, failure to reimburse the total amount transferred by the facilities  impacted negatively on service delivery by the health facilities.  In the circum stances, Management was in breach of the law .  REPORT ON EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROLS, RISK MANAGEMENT  AND GOVERNANCE  Conclusion  409.   There   were no material issues relating to effectiveness of internal controls, risk  management and governance.

173  COUNTY EXECUTIVE OF   MAKUENI   –   NO.17  REPORT ON THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS  Unmodified Opinion  410.   There were no material issues noted during the   audit of the financial statements of  the County.  Emphasis of Matter  411.   Budgetary Control and Performance  The statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts reflects final revenue budget  and   actual   on   comparable   basis   amounts   of   Kshs.10,742,471,512   an d  Kshs.8,872,507,510 respectively resulting in under - funding of Kshs.1,869,964,002 or  17%   of   the   budget.   However,   the   County   Executive   spent   an   amount   of  Kshs.8,710,124,639 against the actual receipts of Kshs.   8,872,507,510   resulting in a  underspending of   Kshs.162,382,871 or 2% of the actual receipts.  The under - funding affected the planned activities and may have impacted negatively on  service delivery to the public.  412.   Long Outstanding Trade and Other Payables  The   statement   of   financial   position   and   as   disclosed   in   Note   32   to   the   financial  statements   reflects   trade   and   other   payables   balance   of   Kshs.773,724,216   which  includes balances of Kshs.265,420,905, Kshs.374,948,836 and Kshs.133,354,475 in  respect of trade payables, emplo yee payables and deposits and retentions respectively.  Review of the supporting documents and ageing analysis revealed that trade and other  payables amounting   to Kshs .138,604,174 have been outstanding for a period of more  than one (1) year. Management did   not provide measures put in place to settle the long  outstanding trade and other payables.  Further, failure to settle bills during the year to which they relate distorts the financial  statements and adversely affects the budgetary provisions for the   subsequent year as  they form the first charge.  My opinion is not modified in respect of these matters.  Other Information  413.   There were no material issues relating to Other Information.

174  REPORT   ON   LAWFULNESS   AND   EFFECTIVENESS   IN   THE   USE   OF   PUBLIC  RESOURCES  Basis for Conclusion  414.   Non - Compliance with Fiscal Responsibility Principles on Wages  As previously reported, the statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note  9 to the financial statements reflects employees’ costs totalling Kshs.4,426,652,436 which  represents approximately 51% of the total revenue amount of Kshs.8,674,598,10 7. This  was contrary to Regulation 25(1)(a) and (b) of the Public Finance Management (County  Governments)   Regulations,   2015   and   Section   107(2)(c)   of   the   Public   Finance  Management Act, 2012 which require that the County Government’s expenditure on  wages   and   benefits   for   its   public   officers   shall   not   exceed   35%   of   the   County  Government’s total revenue.  Although Management indicated that the increase in wage bill was as a result of various  policies and legal requirements such as   mandatory wage inc rease as per the Salaries  and   Remuneration   Commission   (SRC)   circulars   and   implementation   of   the   Health  Workers' Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA), no measures have been put in place  to address the matter.  In the circumstances, Management was in breac h of the law.  415.   Non - Compliance with Law on Staff Ethnic Composition  As previously reported , r eview of master roll and other staff records revealed that the  County Executive had three thousand eight hundred and sixty - three (3,863) employees  out of which three thousand five hundred and eighty - five (3,585) or approximately 93% of  the total workforce   were from the dominant ethnic community in the County.   This was  contrary to   Section 7(1) and (2) of the National Cohesion and Integration Act, 2008 states  that, all public   offices shall seek to represent the diversity of the people of Kenya in the  employme nt of staff and that no public Institution shall have more than one - third of its  staff establishment from the same ethnic community.  Further, one hundred and six (106) employees were recruited during the year under  review out of which   ninety - four (94) or   approximately 89% of the newly recruited staff  were from the dominant ethnic community in the County.   This was contrary to Section  65(1)(e) of the County Governments Act, 2012 which requires that at least thirty percent  of the vacant posts at entry level a re filled by candidates who are not from the dominant  ethnic community in the   County.   Although   Management   indicated   that   they made  deliberate effort to have a wider circulation of the advertisements for the posts and  encouraged other community members to a pply, the outcome was not positive.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

175  416.   Non - Compliance with Persons with Disabilities Act, 2025  As previously reported, during the year under review, the County Executive recruited a  total of   one   hundred and six (106) employees , out of which three (3) were persons with  disabilities, which translates to approximately 3% of the new staff. No explanation was  provided for failure to meet the threshold of 5% as stipulated in   Section 5(1)(e) of the  Pers ons with Disabilities Act, 2025   which states that every county government   shall  promote the inclusion of persons with disabilities in the county public service by putting in  place measures to ensure that at least five per centum of the employment positions are  filled by persons with disabilities.  Further,   among   the   one   hundred   and   twenty - three   (123)   employees   in   senior  management positions, only two (2) are persons with disabilities. This indicates under -  representation of persons with disabilities in both general workforce and in governance  and leadership roles within the Coun ty Executive .  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  417.   Failure to Operationalize   Completed   Projects  417.1.   Kathambalani   Drift and Sump  The County Executive through the Department for Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries  and   Cooperative   Development   entered   into   a   contract   for   the   construction  of   Kathambalani   Irrigation Project on 30   May,   2024 at a contract sum of   Kshs.6,390,017.  The projec t was inspected on 4   September,   2024 and full payment was made on  27 January, 2025. However, physical verification revealed that the Project had not been  fully operationalized, despite the County   Executive   having paid the entire contract sum  of   Kshs.6,390,017.  417.2.   Makueni Child Protection and Development Center  The Coun ty Executive through the   Department of Gender, Children, Youth, Sports  and Social services entered into a contract for the construction of a   manager’s   house  at   Makueni   Child   Protection   and   Development   Center   (MCCPDC)   (Phase   V)  on   17   April,   2024   at   a   contract   sum   of   Kshs.2,913,165   and   was   completed   on  10 February, 2025.  Further, the Department awarded a contract on 14 March, 2025 for the installation of Solar  System for the operationalization of the   Center at a contract sum of Kshs.2,782,010. The  project was completed on 7   April, 2025. Project   inspection   revealed that the two (2)  projects were complete. However, despite having in place a committee composed of  members from the State Department for Soc ial Protection and the County Government  of   Makueni   to   fast - track   operationalization   process,   the   center   had   not   been  operationalized.  In the circumstances,   the   value for money from the   above non - operational   projects  completed could not be confirmed.

176  418.   Dela y   in   Completion of Project   -   Mulima Earth Dam Project  The County Executive entered into a contract   for the construction of Mulima Water project  P hase II on 9 January, 2025 at a contract sum of Kshs.34,470,879   for a period of five (5)  months with expected   completion date of 30 June, 2025.   Review of   m inutes of site visit  revealed that the project was ongoing and the pump house was approximately 60%  complete while the stilling well and chemical dosing channel was at approximately 70%  complete .  Further,   review of the project file revealed that   there was a land dispute   at   the dam  construction site . In addition, the County Executive   had   not obtain ed the necessary  permits from the Kenya Forest Service for the use of the forest land prior to project  implement ation.  In the circumstances,   the   value for money from the incomplete project could not be  confirmed.  419.   Non - Implementation   of Approved   Project s  The   County   Executive   planned   to   implement   seven   hundred   and   sixty - one   (761)  projects   with   a budgeted expenditu re   totalling Kshs.3,438,686,936 for the year ended 30  June, 2025. Review of the County’s Annual Progress Report revealed that   one hundred  and two (102) projects with a budgeted cost of Kshs.865,777,653 were   ongoing,   twenty -  four   (24) projects   budgeted at Ks hs.82,066,179 had not started, while   one   (1) project  costing   Kshs. 500,000 had stalled.   Management did not provide measures put in place to  complete the projects as   listed at the end of this report .  In the circumstances,   the public did not get   value for money   in respect of stalled or  projects not started.  REPORT ON EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROLS, RISK MANAGEMENT  AND GOVERNANCE  Basis for Conclusion  420.   Under - Staffing of Internal Audit Unit  As previously reported, the a pproved County Executive staff establishment provides for  the Internal Audit Department headed by a   director . The Directorate has two (2) divisions,  including Internal Audit and Internal Control, Policies and Systems Divisions, each  headed by a Deputy Dire ctor. However, review of the staff establishment revealed that  the Directorate had an approved staff establishment of twenty - eight (28) employees  whereas the actual number in position is six (6), resulting in under - staffing by twenty - two  (22) officers.  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of Internal Audit Unit could not be confirmed.

177  COUNTY EXECUTIVE OF NYANDARUA   –   NO.18  REPORT ON THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS  Basis for Qualified   Opinion  421.   Unexplained Voided Transactions  Review of the financial records revealed that one thousand nine hundred and ninety -   eight  (1998) transactions amounting to Kshs.1,191,206,248 were v oided during the financial  year under review. However, supporting documents such as voided payment vouchers,  requests to void payments, The National Treasury approval and Exchequer requisitions  from the Controller of Budget were not provided for audit rev iew.   Further, the voided  payments   were   not disclosed as pending accounts payable s   and the utilization of funds  meant for voided transactions was not confirmed.  In the circumstances, the accuracy, completeness and regularity of voided   transactions  amounting to Kshs.1,191,206,248 could not be confirmed.  422.   Unreconciled   Receivables from Non - Exchange Transactions  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 23 to financial statements  reflects receivables from non - exchange tr ansactions balance of Kshs.1,627,082,389  which relates to receipts that were due from County Revenue Fund. However, the balance  differs with the corresponding payables balance from County Revenue Fund financial  statements amounting to Kshs.1,646,579,968, r esulting in an un - reconciled variance of  Kshs.19,497,579.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the receivables from non -  exchange transactions balance of Kshs.1,627,082,389 could not be confirmed.  Emphasis of Matter  423.   Budgetary Control and Performance  The statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts - recurrent and development  combined reflects final receipts budget and actual on comparable basis amounts of  Kshs.8,779,773,471 and Kshs.4,790,756,342 respectively , resulting in an under - funding  of Kshs.3,989,017,129 or 45% of the budget. However, the County Executive spent an  amount   of   Kshs.4,592,860,887   against   the   actual   receipts   of   Kshs.4,790,756,342  resulting in a underspending of Kshs.197,895,455 or 4% of the   actual receipts.  The under - funding of the budget may have impacted negatively on the delivery of goods  and services to the public.

178  424.   Late Exchequer Releases  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 6 to the financial  statements   reflects   transfers   from   County   Revenue   Fund   amounting   to  Kshs.6,297,330,369. Included in the balance is an amount of Kshs.1,527,255,673 that  was received in July after the end of the financial year.  Late disbursement of Exchequer releases   to the County Re venue Fund may have  impacted negatively   on implementation of County Executive’s programmes for the year  under review.  425.   Long Outstanding Payables  The statement of financial position and as disclosed Note 32 to financial statements  reflect trade and other payables balance of Kshs.5,024,674,774. Included in the balance  is an outstanding amount of Kshs.2,746,515,943 that remained unsettled for over a y ear  comprising payables balance of Kshs.77,727,236 aged 1 - 2 years, Kshs.35,046,274 aged  2 - 3 years and Kshs.2,633,742,433 aged over three (3) years.  Failure to settle bills during the year in which they relate distorts the financial statements  and   adversely affects the budgetary provisions for the subsequent year to which they  have to be charged.  [  My opinion is not modified in respect of these matters.  Othe r Matter  426.   Unresolved Prior Year Matters  In the prior year audit report, several issues were raised under the Report on Financial  Statements and Lawfulness and Effectiveness in Use of Public Resources. Review of the  status during audit of the County   Executive in 2024/2025 revealed that twenty - three (23)  matters as listed at the end of this report   remained unresolved as at 30 June, 2025.  Other Information  427.   There were no material issues relating to Other Information.  REPORT   ON   LAWFULNESS   AND   EFFECTIV ENESS   IN   USE   OF   PUBLIC  RESOURCES  Basis for Conclusion  428.   Payment of Salary Outside Integrated Payroll and Personnel Database and  Human Resource   Integrated System  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 9 to the financial  statements reflect employee costs amount of Kshs.2,486,839,933 which includes an  amount of Kshs.2,483.292,033 paid as basic salaries of permanent   employees.   However,

179  an amount of Kshs.93,005,874 was paid outside the Integrated Payroll and Personnel  Database (IPPD) system and the Human Resource Integrated System (HRIS) through  manual payrolls.   This was contrary to The National Treasury Circular No.16 /2020 which  requires personnel   emoluments to be controlled in the public personnel database and  supported by IPPD. Management did not demonstrate efforts undertaken to rectify this  anomaly.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  429.   Non - Compliance with   Law on   Staff   Ethnic Diversity  Review of human resource records revealed that the County Executive had two thousand  four   hundred   and   twenty - nine   (2,429)   staff   on   contractual   a nd   permanent   and  pensionable   terms. However, out of this number, two thousand three hundred and twenty -  two (2,322) members of staff, which translates to 96%, were from the dominant ethnic  community in the County. Further, officers in Job Group P and above   were a total of one  hundred and twenty -   three (123) employees out of which one hundred and ten (110) which  translate to 89%, were from the dominant ethnic community.  This was contrary to provisions of Section 7(1) and (2) of the National Cohesion and  Inte gration Act, 2008 which states that no public establishment shall have more than one  third of its staff from the same ethnic community.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  430.   Non - Compliance with   One - Third   Rule on   Basic Salary  The payroll for the year under audit revealed that four hundred and fourteen (414) staff  members earned net pay less than a third (1/3) of their basic salary. This was contrary to  Section 19 (3) of the Employment Act, 2007 which states   that   the total amount of all  deductions which may be made by an   employer from the wages of his employee at any  one time shall not exceed   two - thirds of such wages .  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  431.   Non - Compliance with the   Persons with Disabilities   Act, 2025  Out of two thousand four hundred and twenty - nine (2,429) employees of the County  Executive only   twenty - two   (22) are   persons with   disabilities, representing 1% of the  workforce which was below the 5% threshold recommend ed by Section 5(1)(e) of the  Persons with Disabilities Act, 2025. The law   states that every county government shall  promote the inclusion of persons with disabilities in the county public service by putting in  place measures to ensure that at least five pe r centum of the employment positions are  filled by persons with disabilities.   Furthermore, among the one hundred and   twenty - three  (123)   employees   in   senior   management   positions,   only   two   (2)   are   persons   with  disabilities.  In the   circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

180  432.   Irregular Staff Recruitment  The County Executive recruited   forty   three (43) officers in various positions. However,  there was no approved staff establishment as prescribed by Section B.2(1) of the Huma n  Resource Policies and Procedures Manual for the Public Service, 2016 which requires  every public entity to prepare Human Resource Plans based on comprehensive job  analysis to support achievement of goals and objectives in their Strategic Plans.   The  hirin g of the officers was also contrary to Section B.3 (1) of the Public Service Commission  Human Resource Policy, 2016 which states that an Authorized Officer shall declare all  vacant posts to the Public Service Commission in accordance with the procedures se t out  in the Commission’s regulations.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  433.   Casuals Engaged Beyond Stipulated Period  The County Executive engaged twenty (20) casual workers continuously for periods  exceeding three (3) consecutive months incurring an amount of Kshs.1,792,800. This was  contrary to Section 37 of the Employment Act, 2007   which requires the employer to  formal ize the employment relationship and extend all the rights and benefits due under  the law, including leave entitlements, notice period, and statutory deductions.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  434.   Non - Compliance with Law on   Fiscal Responsibility Principles on Wages  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 9 to the financial  statements reflects employee costs amount of Kshs.2,486,839,933 equivalent to 39% of  the total revenue of Kshs.6,297,330,369. The   amount exceeded the statutory limit of 35%  set   out   under   Regulation   25(1)(b)   of   the   Public   Finance   Management   (County  Governments) Regulations, 2015.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  435.   Procurement from Non - Prequalified Suppliers  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 10 to the financial  statements reflects use of goods and services amount of Kshs.1,689,204,344 which  includes office general supplies amount of Kshs.32,804,015. Included in the expenditure  is   an amount of Kshs.7,685,896 procured from suppliers who were not included in the  approved framework agreement list of suppliers. This was contrary to Regulation 106 (1)  of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Regulations, 2020 which states that a  proc uring entity is not required to advertise or invite quotations from persons not  shortlisted under the framework agreement where a framework agreement has been  entered into by the procuring entity.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law .

181  436.   Failure to Retain   Facilities Improvement Funds   at the Hospitals  Review of revenue records obtained from Level 4 and Level 5 health facilities in the  County revealed that two (2) health facilities collected a total Kshs.236,054,105 towards  the   health improvement Funds (FIF) which was transferred to the County Revenue Fund.  However, the Fund reimbursed a total of Kshs.234,811,127 to the health facilities  resulting in a deficit of Kshs.1,242,978. Further, the County Executive owes the   two (2)  heal th facilities a cumulative amount of Kshs.111,299,334 from prior years.   This was  contrary to Section 5(1) of the Facilities Improvement Financing Act, 2023 which requires  that all monies raised or received by or on behalf of all public health facilities be   retained  in the Hospital Facilities Improvement Financing account. Failure to reimburse the total  amount transferred by the facilities impacted negatively on service delivery to the public.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  437.   Irregular Insurance Premium Paid for Undelivered Motor   Vehicles  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 10 to the financial  statements reflects use of goods and services amount of Kshs.1,689,204,344 which  includes insurance cost of Kshs.157,554,605. Included in the expenditure is an amount  of Ks hs.437,406 paid as insurance premium for two (2) vehicles purchased in February,  2025 which had not been delivered to the County Executive.   Further, the   logbooks had  not been processed at the time of audit.  In the circumstances, value for money on expendi ture amounting to Kshs.437,406 paid  as insurance premium for the two (2) vehicles could not be confirmed.  438.   Irregular Limits of Liability and Premiums   Payments   in   Group   Medical  Scheme  Review of the County Executive Group Medical Scheme revealed that staff   in Job group  G to   J were offered an inpatient cover limit of Kshs.1,750,000 instead of the approved  limit of Kshs.1,000,000 set by Salaries and Renumeration Commission.   Further, the  County Executive provided optical cover for staff in Job Group K to P of   Kshs.30,000  instead of Kshs.25,000 and optical cover of Kshs.30,000 for officers in Job Group R to T  instead of the prescribed limit of Kshs.35,000 set by SRC. This contravenes the Salaries  and Remuneration Commission Circular No.   SRC/TS/CGOVT/3/61 dated1 9 December,  2014 which requires all public entities to adhere to renumeration and benefit rates set by  the Commission.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  439.   Irregular Payment of Subscription  The statement financial   performance and as disclosed in Note 10 to the financial  statements reflects use of goods and services amount of Kshs.1,689,204,344 which  includes other operating expenses amount of Kshs.454,853,639 which further includes  an amount of Kshs.2,000,000 paid t o the Council of Governors. This was contrary to  Section 37(b) of the Intergovernmental Relations Act, 2012 which provides that the  operational expenses in respect of the Council of Governors should be provided for in the  annual estimates of the revenue an d expenditure of the National Government.

182  In the circumstances ,   Management was in breach of the law.  440.   Delays in Project Implementation  440.1.   Proposed   Construction   of   Medical   Complex   at   JM   Memorial   County  Referral   Hospital  The construction of the   Medical Complex at JM Memorial County Referral Hospital project  was awarded to a contractor at a contract sum of Kshs.1,468,740,156 for a contract period  of one hundred and fifty - six (156) weeks commencing 7 July, 2021. The estimated  completion date was 7   July, 2024 which was later revised to 1 July, 2026 while the  contract price was varied to Kshs.1,597,161,937 or 8% of the initial contract sum.  Although the County Executive entered into a termination agreement with the contractor  on 4 August, 2025 to pave   way for completion of the project through the Department for  Defense following a Presidential directive, physical inspection revealed that minimal work  was ongoing at the construction site.  440.2.   Delayed Construction of Nyandarua County Headquarters at Ol   Kalou  As   previously   reported,   the   construction   of   Nyandarua   County   Headquarters   was  awarded at a contract sum of Kshs.617,644,564 for a period of one hundred and four  (104) weeks commencing16 March, 2017 with an estimated completion date of 15 March,  2019. The completion date was revised to 30 June, 2019 and again   to 30 June, 2021 and  later to 31 December, 2022. In the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) entered into  with the State Department for Public Works in January, 2021, the County Executive was  to fund 30% of the cost of the project and National Government was   to provide the  balance   of 70%. According   to   payment   records,   the   County   Executive had made  payments amounting   to Kshs .60,617,658 while the National Government had paid an  amount   of   Kshs.279,218,554   which   contract   translates   to   total   payments   of  Kshs.339,8 36,212 or 45% of the contract sum. Available   information provided   indicates  that there was a variation order of Kshs.142,293,606 to the contract sum resulting in a  revised   contract   sum   of   Kshs.756,938,171.   However,   the   contract   was   mutually  terminated on 1 4 October, 2022.  Further, the County Executive awarded the contract to another contractor on 29 May,  2023 for a contract sum of Kshs.449,097,570 for a period of one hundred and two (102)  weeks commencing 9 June, 2023 and estimated completion date on 23 Ma y, 2025. The  contract was extended for a further   fifty - two   (52) weeks with a new completion date of  22 May, 2026. Project brief dated 2 September, 2025 and physical inspection conducted  in October, 2025   revealed s lowdown   in progress of works during the period under review.  As a result, the likelihood of achieving the expected completion date is doubtful.  440.3.   Stalled Construction of County Aggregation and Industrial Park  As previously reported, Management awarded a   contract for construction of the County  Aggregation and Industrial Park (CAIP) at Njabini Agricultural Training College (ATC) on  4 October, 2023 at a contract sum of Kshs.464,360,410 with a contract period of twenty -  eight (28) weeks commencing on 29 Janua ry, 2024 and ending on 11 August, 2024.

183  The   County   Executive   was   to   fund   50%   of   the   cost   of   the   project   and   National  Government was to provide the balance of 50%.   T he County Executive had so far made  payments amounting to Kshs.47,026,100 whereas the   National Government did not  release any payments. This translates to total payments of Kshs.47,026,100 or 10% of  the contract sum, for 17% of the work completed and time elapsed was seventy (70)  weeks or 250% of the completion period.  Physical inspection   of the project revealed that the project stalled at substructure works  level (back filling and making up, hardcore filling and compaction, anti - termite treatment  and reinforcement work level) at aggregation warehouses and cold storage level and  substructur e works level (blinding, reinforcement, form - work fixing and concerting to  foundation footing and column base level) at value addition warehouses level. Further,  the contractor was not on site and there was no evidence of project extension after the  previo us thirteen (13) extensions.  440.4.   Stalled Construction of Pharmacy and Laboratory at Manunga Health  Centre  Management entered into a contract for the proposed construction and completion of a  pharmacy   and   laboratory   unit   at   Manunga   health   center   at   a   contract   sum   of  Kshs.8,074,615. The project commenced on 6 May, 2024 with a scheduled contract  period of fifty - t hree (53) weeks, ending on 6 May, 2025.  However, as at the time of audit in June, 2025, after the agreed project completion date,  only the first interim payment of Kshs.2,007,000 dated 31 January, 2025 had been made.  The project remained incomplete and ha d stalled at the foundation level. No revised  completion date and approval for project extension was provided for audit review.  440.5.   Stalled Construction of a Radiology Unit at Bamboo Health Centre  Management entered into a contract for   the   proposed construction and completion of  radiology   unit at Bamboo   Health Center   at a contract sum of Kshs.11,496,972. The  project commenced on 6 May, 2024 with a contract period of   fifty - three   ( 53 )   weeks  scheduled   to be completed on 6 May, 2025.  As at the time of audit in May, 2025, after the lapse of the project completion deadline  had lapsed, only the first interim payment of Kshs.2,395,215 dated 31 January, 2025 had  been made. Physical inspection further reveale d that the project was incomplete and  stalled at the foundation level and the contractor was not on site.  No revised completion date or approval for project extension was provided for audit  review. Further, the performance security for the project expired   on 15 May, 2025 and no  evidence was provided for the renewal.  440.6.   Stalled Construction of Chamuka Dispensary  Management entered into a contract for the proposed construction and completion of  Chamuka Dispensary on 15 May, 2024 for a contract sum of Kshs.28,342,801. The

184  project commenced on 29 May, 2024 with a contract period of fifty - two (52)   weeks,  scheduled   to   be completed on 27 May, 2025.  As at the time of audit in June, 2025 after the project completion deadline, two (2 ) payment  certificates   totalling   Kshs.15,000,000   had   been   made.   However,   the   project   was  incomplete with finishing works yet to be done.  However, revised completion date and approval for project extension as well as the  performance security were not provided for audit review. In addition, physical   inspection  done   in the month of June, 2025 revealed that the project had stalled and the contr actor  was not on site.  440.7.   Construction of Governor’s Official Residence  Contract   for   construction   of   the   Governor's   residence   at   a   contract   sum   of  Kshs.43,415,636 was awarded on 18 April, 2024. The contract period was thirty - two (32)  weeks   with   expected   completion   date   of   24   December,   2024.   Physical   inspection  revealed   that th e project had stalled and the contractor was not on site. No revised  completion date or approval for project extension was provided for audit review.  In the circumstances, value for money on the stalled projects could not be confirmed.  441.   Outstanding Legal   Fees  The statement of financial performance reflects use of goods and services amount of  Kshs.1,689,204,344 which as disclosed in Note 10 to financial statements includes other  operating expenses amount of Kshs.454,853,639. The operating expenses includes an  am ount of Kshs.15,861,118 owed to various law firms for services rendered and not paid.  The County Executive may incur expenditure which could have been avoided if the  County Executive had honoured its financial obligations promptly.  In the circumstances, d elay in settlement of the fee notes exposed the County Executive  to the risks of fines, penalties, interest and further legal suits and value for money on the  expenditure could not be confirmed.  442.   Failure to Pay Court Awards  The Employment and Labour Relations Court of Kenya at Nakuru ordered the County  Executive to pay a total of Kshs.25,286,532 to three (3) petitioners as compensation and  damages for unlawful termination on 26 October, 2021. However, as at the time of audit,  the County Executive had not complied with the court order. Failure to comply with the  court order exposes the County Executive to additional costs in form of fines and penalties  as well as the risk of further litigation.  In the circumstances,   Management   was in breach of the law.

185  443.   Irregularities in Planning and Budgeting  443.1.   Lack   of   Effective   Citizen Participation in Planning and Budgeting  Review of the budget - making process revealed that the County Executive did not   comply  with   Articles 201 and 232(1)(d) of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, due to failure to adhere  to the prescribed guidelines for effective public participation. Further, Man agement did  not develop criteria for identifying the stakeholders to participate in the budget process.  443.2.   Non - Compliance with Budgetary Limits and Reporting Requirements  The approved revenue budget for the Nyandarua County Government (County Executive  a nd   Assembly)   amounted   to   Kshs.9,652,691,719,   which   includes   an   amount   of  Kshs.872,918,248 allocated to the County Assembly. The approved budget for the  County Assembly translates to 9% of the total County Government revenue exceeding  the fiscal limit by 2%   set under Regulation 25(1)(f) of the Public Finance Management  (County Governments) Regulations, 2015.  Further,   the   County   Executive   Committee   Member   for   Finance   did   not   submit   a  responsibility statement to the County Assembly explaining the reasons for   the deviation  and outlining a plan to ensure annual actual expenditure out turns as well as medium  term allocations comply with the provisions of Section 107(2)(a) of the Public Finance  Management Act, 2012 and the regulations in the subsequent years as re quired by  Regulation   25(1)(h)   of   the   Public   Finance   Management   (County   Governments)  Regulations, 2015.  443.3.   Non - Compliance with Debt - to - Revenue Ratio Limits  The approved revenue budget for the County Executive for the year under review  amounted   to   Kshs.8,779,773,471   against   certified   pending   accounts   payables   of  Kshs.2,965,410,323.   This   resulted   in   thirty - four   percent   (34%)   of   the   County  Government’s total revenue. The amount exceeds the required set limit of twenty percent  (20%) stipulated under Re gulation 25(1)(d) of the Public Finance Management (County  Governments) Regulations, 2015.  443.4.   Delay in Insurance Compensation  The County   Executive   lost   twenty - six   ( 26 )   motor vehicles to fire during the Gen - Z  demonstrations on 25 June, 2025 at the Ol Kalou Sub - County yard and at the District  Officer’s office.   The motor vehicles were insured and the matter was reported to the  insurance company.   However,   from   review   of   cor respondence between   M anagement and  the   insurance companies ,   it   was not clear how or when the County   Executive   would be  compensated for the loss.  In   the   circumstances,   the   delay   in   insurance   claims,   financial   strain   and   loss   of  compensation for the loss of   twenty - six   ( 26 )   motor vehicles   could not be confirmed.

186  REPORT ON EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROLS, RISK MANAGEMENT  AND GOVERNANCE  Basis for Conclusion  444.   Ineffective Management of Property, Plant and Equipment  The statement of financial position and as disclosed   in   Note 26 to financial statements  reflects   a balance of   Kshs.1,560,955,311   relating to   property, plant and equipment.  However, during the audi t the following issues were noted;  444.1.   Lack of Logbooks  Review of assets records revealed that the   County   Executive   owns two hundred and  twelve (212) motor vehicles and one hundred and sixty - two (162) motorcycles. However,  only ninety - three (93)   motor vehicle   logbooks and forty (40) motorcycles   logbooks   were  provided for audit review.   The remaining one hundred and nine teen (119) motor vehicle  logbooks and one hundred and twenty - two (122) motorcycle logbooks were not provided  for audit review .  444.2.   Grounded Motor Vehicles  Out of the total fleet of two hundred   and twelve (212) , th e County   Executive   has eighty  (80) grounde d motor vehicles out of the total fleet of two hundred   and twelve   vehicles,  and seventy - eight (78) grounded motorcycles out of one hundred and sixty - two (162)  motorcycles. However,   motor vehicle   records provided did not indicate the duration these  vehicles   and motorcycles have been grounded   nor did they provide   any maintenance,  disposal, or reactivation plans , to ensure effective asset management.  444.3.   Lack of   Updated   Asset s   Register  The County   Executive   did not maintain an updated fixed asset s   register for   its assets   and  assets   procured   during   the   year   were   neither   recorded   nor   tagged   for   ease   of  identification   and verification .  In the circumstances, the existence   of   effective assets management   mechanisms   could  not be confirmed.  445.   Lack of an Off - site   Data Recovery Centre  Review of the County Executive’s ICT disaster preparedness and business continuity  arrangements revealed that the County Executive had not established an off - site data  recovery centre. As a result, critical systems and data are not se curely backed up or  protected against loss in the event of unforeseen occurrences such as system failures,  cyber - attacks   or fires.  In the circumstances, existence of effective mechanisms to safeguard the County  Executive’s ICT systems and information cou ld not be confirmed.

187  List of Unresolved Prior Years Matters  No.   Audit Issue s for 2023/2024  1   Variances in the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts   –  Recurrent and Development Combined  2   Variances Between Financial Statements Balances and Integrated Financial  Management   S ystem   (IFMIS)  3   Variance Between Appropriation Account and Payment Details,  4 -   Unreconciled Pending Bills  5 -   Unexplained Voided Transactions,  6 -   Budgetary Control and Performance  7   Non - Compliance with Law on Ethnic Composition,  8   Non - Compliance with the Law on Fiscal Responsibility - Wage Bill,  9   Payment of Salary Outside IPPD System,  10   Irregular Engagement of Consultants for Legal   Services,  11   Irregular Payments of Subscription to the Council of Governors,  12   Non - Compliance with the Law on Pending Bills,  13   Irregular Expenditure on Designated Departments,  14   Incomplete and Low Absorption in Projects Implementation Status   Report,  15   Stalled Construction of the Nyandarua County Headquarters at Ol   -   Kalou,  16   Proposed Construction of County Aggregation and Industrial Parks,  17   Proposed Construction of Medical Complex at JM Memorial County Referral  Hospital,  18   Governor's Official Residence,  19   Lack of Risk Management Policy,  20   Weaknesses in the Legal Department,  21   Lack of Logbooks and Vehicle Status  22   Failure to   Adhere to Vote Control Guidelines on Subsistence Allowance and  23   Summary of Non - C urrent Assets Register.

188  COUNTY EXECUTIVE   OF   NYERI   –   NO.19  REPORT ON THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS  Basis for Qualified   Opinion  446.   Lack of Land Ownership Documents  446.1.   Official Residence of the Governor  The statement of financial position   and as disclosed in Note 26 to the financial   statements  reflects   property, plant and equipment balance of Kshs . 506,369,499. Included in   the  amount are additions of   w ork - i n - p rogress   (WIP)   balance   of Kshs. 47,465,613, out of  which,   Kshs.42,449,829   is   in respect of the construction of official residence for the  Governor.   However, no land ownership documents in the form of title deed, certificate of  title or certificate of lease for the parcel of land measuring 1.8 acres on which the  r esidence is being constructed were provided for audit   review .  446.2.   Undisclosed   Property, Plant and Equipment  The statement of financial performance reflects other grants and subsides amount of  Kshs.687,166,800 as disclosed in Note 13 to the financial statemen ts. The amount  includes other capital grants and transfers amount of Kshs.666,786,484 out of which an  amount of Kshs.42,224,555 was in respect of Nyeri County Aggregated and Industrial  Park project. However, the amount of Kshs.93,164,980 was not included i n the property,  plant and equipment balance of Kshs.506,369,499 as Work - in progress and the project  was started without a certificate of lease or title deed.  In the circumstances, the   ownership,   accuracy   and   completeness of   p roperty, plant and  equipment   balance   of Kshs . 506,369,499 could not be confirmed.  447.   Unsupported   Voided Payments  Analysis of the Integrated Financial Management System (IFMIS) payments indicated  that two hundred and eighty - three (283) transactions   totallin g   Kshs.230,423,834 were  voided during the year   under review . However, no evidence was provided to confirm that  the Controller of Budget was   notified   of the voiding of the payments to make necessary  adjustments and approval.  In the circumstances, the accu racy and regularity of the voided transactions   amounting  to   Kshs.230,423,834 could not be confirmed.  Other Matter  448.   Unresolved Prior Year Audit Issues  In the prior year ’ s audit report, several issues were raised under the Report on Financial  Statements, Lawfulness and Effectiveness in Use of Public Resources, and Effectiveness  of Internal Controls, Risk Management and Governance. Review of the   status during audit  of the C ounty Executive in 2024/2025 revealed that the   seventeen (17)   matters   as listed  at the end of this report   remained unresolved   as   at 30 June, 2025 report.

189  Other Information  449.   There were no material issues relating to   Other Information .  REPORT   ON   LAWFULNESS   AND   EFFECTIVENESS   IN   THE   USE   OF   PUBLIC  RESOURCES  Basis for Conclusion  450.   Long Outstanding Employee   Payables  The   statement   of   financial   position   reflects   trade   and   other   payables   balance   of  Kshs . 34 2 , 359 , 626   and   as disclosed in Note   32 to the financial statements. The balance  incudes   employee payables amounting to   K shs .110,483,849 .   R eview of the   payable’s  ledger revealed that public officers at the   County Executive undertook official activities  using private funds and later claimed the same. This   was   contrary to   Regulation 93(4)(d)  of the   Public Finance Management (County Government s )   Regulations,   2015 which  require s   that   before   making   official   journey   the   Accounting   Officer   should   ensure  adequate funds are available against the relevant items of expenditure to meet the  proposed expenditure. Further, some employee payables date back to   the financial year  2019/2020 , Management did not explain   why they were not cleared as the first charge in  the subsequent financial year.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the   l aw.  451.   Irr egularit ies   in   Human Resource Management   Practices  451.1.   Lack of Annual Recruitment Plans  R eview of positions filled during the   year under review   revealed   that two hundred and  fifty - six (256) persons were recruited for various positions. However, the corresponding  annual recruitment plans were not   provid ed for audit. Management did not   also   provide  evidence on implementation of internal controls with refere nce to the provision of  approved annual recruitment plans in accordance with Public Service Commission  requirements.  Although   Management explained   that   all County Departments   had   been directed to  submit their Human Resource Plans by 30 June of each financ ial year to allow timely  preparation and approval of the consolidated Annual Recruitment Plan, there was no  evidence   provided   for audit to indicate   that this was followed in the year under review.  In   the   circumstances,   compliance   with   annual   recruitment   p lanning   could   not   be  confirmed.  451.2.   Salaries   Paid Outside Integrated Person nel and Payroll Database   System  Analysis of sampled payroll   data between   July ,   2024 and December ,   2024 revealed that  two hundred and ninety - six ( 296 )   persons in the Finance and Health Departments were  paid   an amount of   Kshs . 19,213,386 through manual payment vouchers outside the  Government   recommended   Integrated   Personnel   and   Payroll   Database   (IPPD)  Management System. This   wa s contrary   to   The National T reasury Circular No.16/2020

190  which requires personnel emoluments to be controlled in the Public Personnel Database  and supported by IPPD.   Management did not illustrate efforts undertaken to regularize  this anomaly during the six - month period.  451.3.   Retention of Employees Beyond Retirement Age  Analysis of   Integrated   Payroll   and   Personnel   Database   (IPPD )   payroll data   as   at  30 June, 2025 revealed that there were   fifteen ( 15 )   employees who had attained the  retirement age of 60   years, but were still in the payroll.   This   was   contrary to   Regulation  70(1)(a), (b), (c) of the Public Service Commission Regulation, 2020 which states that the  mandatory   retirement age in the Public Service shall be sixty (60) years and/or as may  be pre scribed by the Government from time to time .  451.4.   Non - Alignment of   Integrated Personnel and Payroll Database System to  Approved Staff Establishment  R eview of   the   Integrated   Personnel   and   Payroll   Database ( IPPD )   system   revealed   that  four hundred and two (402) designations were configured as at   30   June, 2025. However,  out of the   four hundred and two   ( 402 )   configured designations, three hundred and twenty -  three (323) were not aligned with the designations in the approved staff est ablishment.  Further, two thousand nine hundred and eighty - seven (2,987) employees were placed in  these   three hundred and twenty - three   ( 323 )   designations ; thus there was no   alignment of  IPPD system to the approved establishment.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the   law.  452.   Non - Compliance with   Persons with Disabilities   Act, 2025  The County Public Service Board recruited ninety (90) employees during the year  under review. However, no persons living with   disabilities   were recruited contrary to  Section 5(e) of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2025 which states that every co unty  government shall promote the inclusion of persons with disabilities in the county public  service by putting in place measures to ensure that at least five per centum of the  employment position are filled by persons with disabilities .  In the circumsta nce s , Management was in breach of the law.  453.   Non - Compliance with Law on Staff Ethnic Composition  Review of employee records for the County Executive provided for audit   revealed   that,  the dominant ethnic community   in the County   constituted 9 4 %   or three thousand, four  hundred and   forty - three   (3,443) out of the total population   of   three   thousand six hundred  and seventy - five ( 3,675 )   employees. This   was   contrary to Section 7(2) of the National  Cohesion and Integration Act, 2008 whic h provides that no public establishment shall  have more than one third of its staff from the same ethnic community.  Further,   review   of payroll records and a list of new recruitments conducted   in   the year  under review , revealed that the County Public Servi ce Board recruited ninety (90)  employees. However, eighty - five (85) or 94% were from the dominant ethnic community .  That was contrary to   Section 65(1)(e) of the County Governments Act, 2012, which

191  requires at least thirty percent   (30%)   of the vacant posts   at entry level to be filled by  candidates who are not from the dominant ethnic community in the County.  In the circumstance s , Management was in breach of law.  454.   Non - Compliance with Fiscal Responsibilities Principles on Wages  The statement of financial performance and   as disclosed in   Note 9 to the   financial  statements reflects employee cost amount of Kshs . 4,493,693,474 out of the budgeted  revenue   amount   of Kshs.9,004,034,684 translating to 50% of the revenues.   This   wa s  contrary   to Regulation 25(1)(a) and (b) of the Public Finance Management (County  Governments)   Regulations,   2015   which   provides   that   the   County   Government’s  expenditure on wages and benefits for its public officers, shall not exceed thirty - five  percent (35 % ) of the   County Government’s total revenue.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  455.   Excessive Budget Allocation  The approved budget for the County   Executive   for the financial year 2024/2025 was  K shs . 8,750,998,795   while   t he   County   Assembly’s   budget   was   Kshs . 796,625,715  translating to 9%   of the total County revenue. As a result, the approved budget allocated  exceeded the allowable amount by   Kshs . 184,055,800.   This   wa s contrary to Regulation  25(1)(f) of the Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015  which   provides   that the approved expenditures of a County Assembly shall not exceed  seven percent (7%) of the total revenues of the County Government   or twice the  personnel emoluments of that County Assembly, whichever is lower.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  456.   Failure to Retain Facilities Improvement Funds at the Hospitals  Review of revenue records obtained from Level 4 an d Level 5 health facilities in the  County   revealed   that   seven   (7)   health   facilities   collected   a   total   amount   of  Kshs.722,201,876 towards the   Health   Facilities Improvement which was transferred to  Nyeri   County   Health   Services   Fund.   However,   the   Fund   reimbursed   a   total   of  Kshs.572,160,313 to the health facilities resulting in a deficit of Kshs.150,041,563.   This  was contrary to Section 5(1) of the Facili ties Improvement Financing Act, 2023 which  requires that all monies raised or received by or on behalf of all public health facilities be  retained in the Hospital Facilities Improvement Financing Account.   Further , failure to  reimburse the total amount tran sferred by the facilities impacted negatively on service  delivery by the health facilities.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  457.   Stalled Nyeri County Aggregation and Industrial Park  The statement of financial performance reflects   other grants and subsidies balance  of Kshs.687,166,890 which as further disclosed in Note 13 to the financial statements  includes other capital grants and transfers amount of Kshs.656,756,484 out of which an  amount of Kshs.42,224,555 was   in respect of Nyeri County Aggregated and Industrial

192  Park   project.   A   contractor   was   awarded   a   contract   for   the   project   at   cost   of  Kshs.589,292,137.   As   at   the   time   of   audit   in   September,   2025,   an   amount   of  Kshs.93,164,980   had   been   incurred   on   the   project.   Further,   physical   inspection  conducted in May and September, 2025 revealed that the construction   stalled in May,  2025,   at lintel and walling levels with warehouse structures having no roof .  REPORT ON EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROLS, RISK   MANAGEMENT  AND GOVERNANCE  Conclusion  458.   There were no material issues relating to effectiveness of internal controls, risk  management   and governance.

194  COUNTY EXECUTIVE   OF   KIRINYAGA   –   NO.20  REPORT ON THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS  Basis for Qualified   Opinion  459.   Inaccuracies   in   Transfers to Other Government Entities  The   statement   of   financial   performance   and   as   disclosed   in   Note   11   to   financial  statements reflects an amount of Kshs. 855,601,727 in respect of transfers to other  Government   entities   which   includes   an   amount   of   Kshs. 99,775,086   transferred   to  Kirinyaga   Coun ty   Climate   Change   Fund.   However,   review   of   the   Fund’s   financial  statements revealed that only an amount of Kshs.64,667,859 was received resulting in  an unexplained variance of Kshs.35,107,227.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of transf ers to other Government  entities amount of Kshs.99,775,086 could not be confirmed.  460.   Inaccuracies in Cash and Cash Equivalents  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 21 to the financial statements  reflects   a   balance   of   Kshs.149,920,5 43   in   respect   of   cash   and   cash   equivalents.  However, review of bank accounts revealed that an amount of Kshs.101,969,935 in one  bank account was not disclosed in the financial statements.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the cash and cash equivalents  balance of Kshs.149,920,543 could not be confirmed.  461.   Unsupported Refundable Deposits and Prepayments  The   statement   of   financial   position   and   as   disclosed   in   Note   33   to   the   financial  statements reflects a balance of Kshs.70,296,409 in respect of refundable deposits.  However, Management did not provide relevant supporting documents including invoices  and schedules showing amount retained from payments to vario us suppliers to support  the balance.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of refundable deposits and  prepayments balance of Kshs. 70,296,409   could not be confirmed.  462.   Lack of Land Ownership Documents  The statement of financial   position and as disclosed in Note 26 to the financial statements  reflects a balance of Ksh s .879,898,225 in respect of property, plant and equipment. The  balance includes addition to assets amounting to Kshs.548,017,450 out of which an  amount of Kshs.28,40 0,000 relates to additions to land during the year under review.  However, Management did not provide land ownership documents in respect of the land  acquired.  In the circumstances, the ownership, existence and completeness of property, plant and  equipmen t balance of Kshs.28,400,000 could not be confirmed.

195  463.   Overstatements   of Property, Plant and Equipment  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 26 to the financial statements  reflects a balance of Kshs.879,898,225 in respect of proper ty, plant and equipment. The  balance includes additions to assets amount of Kshs.548,017,450 out of which an amount  of Kshs.246,156,189 relates to additions for infrastructure assets which further includes  an amount of Kshs.14,543,835 paid to a firm in res pect of construction   of a   fire station  whose contract price was Kshs.50,663,036. However, the amount of Kshs.50,663,036  was also recognized in the financial statements of Kerugoya - Kutus Municipality where  the entire cost of the fire station was disclosed as the Municipality’s asset under property,  plant and equipment. Management did not provide explanation why the asset was  recognized by the two (2) entities in their respective fin ancial statements.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of property, plant and equipment  balance of Kshs.50,663,036 could not be confirmed.  464.   Non - Compliance with   the   International Public Sector Accounting Standards  Reporting Requirements  During the year under review, the   County Executive prepared its financial statements in  accordance with accrual basis of accounting under the International Public Sector  Accounting Standards (IPSAS). This was a shift from cash basis of accounting. As  discl osed in Note 2 to the financial statements, Management indicated that the entity had  taken advantage of the transition provisions under IPSAS 33 for a three - year transition  period.   IPSAS 33 explicitly requires an entity that utilizes any transition exempt ions to  clearly disclose the transition provisions that it has applied. However, the County  Executive did not disclose the specific transitional provisions and measures being taken  towards full compliance with IPSAS Accrual.  In the circumstances, the pres entation and disclosure if the financial statements could not  be confirmed.  Emphasis of Matter  465.   Budgetary Control and Performance  The statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts reflects total final revenue  budget   and   actual   on   comparable   basis   amounts   of   Kshs.7,118,221,601   and  Kshs.5,873,579,553 respectively, resulting in under - funding of Kshs.1,244,642,048 or  17%   of   the   budget.   Similarly,   the   County   Executive   spent   an   amount   of  Kshs.5,793,955,419 out of the actual receipts amou nt of Kshs.5,873,579,553 resulting in  under - expenditure amount of Kshs.79,624,134 or 1% of the actual receipts.  The under - funding affected the planned activities and may have impacted negatively on  service delivery to the public.  My opinion is not modifi ed in respect of this matter.

196  Other Matter  466.   Unresolved Prior Year Audit Issues  In the prior year audit report, several issues were raised under the Report on Financial  Statements, Lawfulness and Effectiveness in Use of Public Resources, and Report on  Effectiveness of Internal Controls, Risk Management and Governance, respectively.  Re view of the status during the audit of the County Executive in 2024/2025 revealed that  the following matters remained unresolved as at 30 June, 2025.  No.   Audit Issues for 2023/2024  1   Variances Between Financial Statements Balances and   Integrated Financial  Management Information System (IFMIS) Report.  2   Long Outstanding Pending Bills  3   Non - Adherence to Fiscal Responsibility Principle on Wage Bill.  4   Non - Compliance with the Law on Staff Ethnic Diversity  5   Lack of Internal Audit   Reports  6   Lack of Valuation Report and Ownership Documents  Other Information  467.   There were no material issues relating to Other Information.  REPORT   ON   LAWFULNESS   AND   EFFECTIVENESS   IN   THE   USE   OF   PUBLIC  RESOURCES  Basis for Conclusion  468.   Non - Compliance   with   Fiscal   Responsibility   Principles   on   County  Assemblies’ Allocation  Review of the County Executive budget for the financial year 2024 - 2025 revealed that an  amount of Kshs.807,492,795 was allocated to County Assembly of Kirinyaga. The  allocation was equivalent to 10% of the total County’s revenue budget for the year of  Kshs .7,925,714,395. This was contrary to Regulation 25(1)(f) of the Public Finance  Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which provides that the approved  expenditures of a County Assembly shall not exceed seven percent (7%) of the total  revenues of   the County Government or twice the personnel emoluments of that County  Assembly, whichever is lower.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  469.   Incomplete Construction of Mathia Dispensary  The construction of Mathia Dispensary had a t otal project cost amount of Kshs.8,871,455.  During the year under review, an amount of Kshs.5,262,250, was paid to the contractor.  However, physical inspection conducted in September, 2025 revealed that the dispensary  was incomplete. There was no budgetary   estimates provision for the balance in the FY

197  2025/2026 County Executive Budget. Without this allocation, the project risks stalling  indefinitely.  In the circumstances, value for money from the incomplete project could not confirmed.  470.   Non - Compliant with Fiscal Responsibility Principles on Wages  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 9 to the financial  statements   reflects an amount of Kshs.2,506,567,818 in respect of employee costs which  translates to forty - three percent (43%) of the total revenue of Kshs.5,873,579,553. This  was contrary to Regulation 25(1)(a) and (b) of the Public Finance Management (County  Govern ments)   Regulations,   2015   which   provides   that   the   County   Government’s  expenditure on wages and benefits for its public officers, shall not exceed thirty - five  percent (35%) of the County Government’s total revenue.  In the circumstances, Management was in br each of the law.  471.   Non - Compliance with Law on Staff Ethnic Composition  Review of human resource records revealed that ninety - two percent (92%) of the   County  Executive   employees were from the dominant ethnic community in the County contrary  to   S ection 7(2) of the National Cohesion and Integration Act, 2008 which provides that no  public establishment shall have more than one third of its staff from the same ethnic  communi ty. Further, out of ninety - seven (97) staff members recruited during the year  under review, eighty - five (85) or eighty - seven percent (87 %) were   from the dominant  ethnic community. This was contrary to Section 65(1) of the County Governments Act,  2012 which   provides that   the County Public Service Board is required to consider, in  selecting candidates for appointment, the need to ensure that at least thirty percent (30%)  of the vacant posts at entry level are filled by candidates who are not from the dominant  ethnic community in the County.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  472.   Non - Compliance with Persons with Disabilities Act, 2025  Further, Management did not provide evidence that   p ersons with   d isabilities   were given  employment opport unities   contrary to Section 5(e) of the Persons with Disabilities Act,  2025 which requires that every county government shall provide the inclusion of persons  with disabilities in the county public service by putting in place measures to ensure at  least fi ve per   centum   of the employment position are filled by persons with   disabilities .  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  473.   Unutilized   Gender - Based Violence Rehabilitation   Center at Kirinyaga  A firm was awarded a tender to   convert two (2) residential houses at Kerugoya Referral  Houses to a Gender - Based Violence Rehabilitation (GBVR) Center - Kirinyaga. However,  physical inspection conducted in September, 2025 revealed that the houses were

198  renovat ed but not labelled and were abandoned with notable broken windows and  neglected background.  In the circumstances, value for money on the project could not be confirmed.  474.   Non - Remittance of Capacity Building Levy  Procurement   records   provided   for   audit   revealed   that   in   the   period   between  1 September, 2024 and 30 June, 2025, the County Executive awarded tenders totalling  Kshs.613,055,017.   However,   Management   did   not   provide   evidence   that   capacity  building levy was deduct ed and the amount remitted to the Authority as per the Public  Procurement Regulatory Authority Circular number 01/2024 (Ref: PPRA/6/5 VOL 11  (224) dated 30 August, 2024. The circular provides that procuring entities are expected  to collect the capacity bu ilding levy at the rate of 0.03% of the contract sum from suppliers  on all procurement contracts signed between the suppliers and procuring entity and remit  to the authority through the e - citizen platform.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of   the law.  475.   Long Outstanding Trade and Other Payables  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 32 to the financial statements  reflects a total balance of Kshs.589,845,766 in respect of trade and other payables which  includes an amount of Kshs.286,650,940 which has been outstanding from fin ancial year  2013/2014. It was not clear why Management did not prioritize paying prior pending  payables on first come first paid basis. This was contrary to   Regulation 41(2) of the Public  Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which req uires that debt  service payments shall be a first charge on the County   Revenue Fund and the Accounting  Officer shall ensure this is done to   the extent possible that the County Government does  not default on debt   obligations.  In the circumstances, Manageme nt was in breach of the law.  476.   Irregular   Engagement of Casual Workers  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 9 to the financial  statements reflects an amount of Kshs.2,506,567,818 in respect of employee costs which  includes   an   amount   of   Kshs.80,399,461   in   respect   of   basic   wages   of   temporary  employees   paid as casual workers. Employees records revealed that during the year  under review, the County Executive engaged nine hundred and twenty - eight (928) casual  workers. However, requisition from respective departments to the County Public Service  Board indi cating the number of casuals and duration required were not provided for audit  review contrary to Section 63 of the County Governments Act, 2012 which provides  exclusive powers   to the County Public Service Board   to make appointments, promotions,  and re - app ointments within the County Public Service.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

199  REPORT ON EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROLS, RISK MANAGEMENT  AND GOVERNANCE  Basis for Conclusion  477.   Lack of an Approved Staff   Establishment  Review of the human resource documents revealed that the County Executive did not  have an approved staff establishment in the year under review . This was contrary to  Section B.2(1) of the Human Resource Policies and Procedures Manual for the   Public  Service, 2016 which requires every public entity to prepare Human Resource Plans based  on comprehensive job analysis to support achievement of goals and objectives in their  strategic plans.   Further, the County Executive may not operate at optimum s taffing level  which may impact negatively on service delivery to the public.  In the circumstances, existence of an effective human resource tool to prevent against  understaffing or overstaffing to ensure optimum staff levels could not be   confirmed.  478.   Weakness in the Internal Audit Unit  During the year under review, the Internal Audit Unit had four (4) staff members. However,  the internal audit department did not produce any report to confirm that the Unit was  functional. Further, there was   no approved internal audit workplan for the year under  review. In addition, there was no evidence that the audit committee met during the year.  In the circumstances, the assurance to Management on the systems of internal controls,  risk management and gov ernance could not be confirmed.  479.   Weaknesses in Asset Management  479.1.   Failure to Tag Assets  During the year under review, t he County   Executive   acquired furniture   and Information  Communication   and   Technology   (ICT)   equipment   valued   at   Kshs . 28,366,140   and  Kshs . 68,198,500, respectively . However, at the time of audit, these assets had not been  tagged for ease of tracing as required under Regulation 132 of the Public Fin ance  Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015.  479.2.   Failure to   Board and   Dispose Grounded Unserviceable Motor Vehicles  Review of a list of motor vehicles provided for audit revealed that a total of one hundred  and eight (108) motor vehicles and motor cycles were classified as grounded and  unserviceable. However, Management did not provide a disposal plan as required under  Section 53 ( 4 )   of the Public Procurement   and   Asset Disposal Act ,   2015 .  Further, there were no   mechanical reports to justify classification of the grounded units  as obsolete or   unserviceable.  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of County Executive as set management and  internal controls could not be confirmed.

200  480.   Lack of a   Risk Management   Policy  The County Executive did not have in place a   Risk Management Policy to provide a  framework for detecting   and preventing fraud during the year under review. Further, t here  was no formal documented process to guide   in   timely   detection and prevention of fraud  contrary to Regulation 158 of the Public Fin ance Management (County Governments)  Regulations, 2015.  In the circumstances, risk management and the internal controls built within the financial  and operational systems could not be confirmed.

201  COUNTY EXECUTIVE   OF   MURANG'A   –   NO.21  REPORT ON THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS  Basis for Qualified   Opinion  481.   Non - Compliance with the Reporting Requirements  Review   of   the   financial   statements   revealed   that,   the   Statement   of   Management  Responsibilities and Note 2 to the financial statement under the statement of compliance  and basis of preparation did not indicate   that these were transitional financial statements.  Further, Management did not disclose the elements in the financial   statements   not  recognized due to transitional reporting.  In the circumstances, the presentation and disclosure of the financial statements could  not be   confirmed .  482.   Trade and Other Payables  482.1.   Unreconciled   Trade and Other Payables  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 32 to the financial statements  reflects a balance of Kshs.3,228,256,308 in respect of trade and other payables, out of  which, a balance of   Kshs.695,112,289   is in respect of trade payables. Howeve r, the O ffice  of the Controller of Budget (COB)   –   County Governments budget implementation review  report   showed that as at 30 June, 2025, the County Executive of Murang’a had pending  bills   balance   of   Kshs.1,834,879,792   resulting   in   an   unexplained   and   unrec onciled  variance of Kshs .1,139,767,503 .  482.2.   Failure to Reconciled Account Payables on Utilities  Further, creditors’ circularization made to service providers revealed that The Kenya  Power and Lighting Company (KPLC) is owed by the County Executive a total   of  Kshs.74,941,039 on electricity supply while records submitted by the County Executive  indicated that the Company’s payables balance of Kshs.38,878,148 resulting in an  unreconciled and unexplained variance of Kshs.36,062,891.  In the circumstances, the a ccuracy, existence and completeness of outstanding utilities  payables balance of   Kshs. 38,878,148 could not be confirmed.  483.   Misstatement of Cash and Cash Equivalents Balance  The statement of financial position reflects cash and cash equivalents balance of  Kshs.248,892,510, as disclosed in Note 21 to the financial statements. However, the  amount included a balance of Kshs.8,505,361 relating to Murang’a County Climate  Change Fund as disclosed in the Murang’a County Climate Change Fund financial

202  statements for   the year ended 30 June, 2025. The Fund is   self - reporting   entity, and its  transactions and balances should therefore be accounted for   separately from   those of the  County Executive.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the cash and cash   equivalents  balance   of Kshs.248,892,510 could not be confirmed.  484.   Unreconciled   Receivables   from Non - Exchange Transactions  The statement of financial position and as   disclosed in Note 23 to the financial statements  reflects a balance of Kshs.1,310,755,577 in respect of other debtors in respect of  transfers from the County Revenue Fund. However, the County Revenue Fund financial  statements reflects a balance of Kshs.1,3 06,767,577 as outstanding payables to the  County   Executive   resulting   in   an   unexplained   and   unreconciled   variance   of  Kshs.3,988,000.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of receivables from non - exchange  transactions balance of Kshs.1,310,755 ,577 could not be confirmed.  Emphasis of Matter  485.   Budgetary Control and Performance  The statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts (recurrent and development  combined)   reflects   final   receipts   budget   and   actual   on   comparable   basis   of  Kshs.9,877, 836,251 and Kshs.8,494,766,810 respectively, resulting in under -   funding of  Kshs.1,383,069,441 or 14% of the budget.   Similarly, the County Executive spent an  amount of Kshs.8,243,969,936   against   actual receipts amount of Kshs.8,494,766,810  resulting in und er - expenditure amount of Kshs.250,796,874 or 3% of the actual receipts.  The under - funding affected the planned activities and may have impacted negatively on  service delivery to the public.  My opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.  Other Matter  486.   Unresolved Prior Year Audit Issues  In the   previous   year audit report, several issues were raised under the Report on Financial  Statements, Lawfulness and Effectiveness in Use of Public Resources, and Effectiveness  of Internal Controls, Risk   Management and Governance. Review of the status during audit  of the County Executive in 2024/2025 revealed that sixteen (16) matters remained  unresolved as at 30 June, 2025 as listed at the end of this report.

203  Other Information  487.   There were no material issues relating to Other Information.  REPORT   ON   LAWFULNESS   AND   EFFECTIVENESS   IN   THE   USE   OF   PUBLIC  RESOURCES  Basis for Conclusion  488.
