424  COUNTY EXECUTIVE OF KAJIADO   –   NO.34  REPORT ON THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS  Basis for Qualified   Opinion  871.   Unsupported Receivables from Non - Exchange Transactions  The   statement   of   financial   position   and   as   disclosed   in   Note   23   to   the   financial  statements reflects receivables from non - exchange transactions opening balance of  Kshs.2,501,193,082. However, the supporting ledgers of the balance were not prov ided  for audit.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the receivables from non -  exchange transactions opening balance of Kshs.2,501,193,082 could not be confirmed.  872.   Unsupported Adjustments in the   Statement of Changes in Net Assets  The st atement of changes in net assets reflects adjustments (to recognize assets and  liabilities) balance of Kshs.133,287,878. Further, the statement reflects capital fund  additions negative balance of Kshs.2,854,609,720. However, supporting documents for  the ad justments were not provided for audit.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the statement of changes in net  assets could not be confirmed.  873.   Inaccuracies   in the Statement of Cash Flows  The statement of   cash flows   reflects cash   outflows from operating activities amounting to  Kshs.107,526,229 in respect of use of goods and services. The amount is reflected as  negative balance which implies that there was an overpayment for goods and services  which was not justified. Further, the s tatement reflects net cash flows from operating  activities   amount   of   Kshs.1,388,581,400   which   includes   an   adjustment   of  Kshs.340,983,877 as disclosed in Note 40 to the financial statements in relation to  increase in inventories. However, no disclosure note   was included in the financial  statements to explain the adjustment.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the statement of cash flows  could not be confirmed.  874.   Unconfirmed   Trade and Other Payables  The statement of financial position reflects a balance of Kshs.4,174,866,983 in respect of  trade and other payables as disclosed in Note 32 to the financial statements. However,  the payables schedule provided for audit did not provide a movement schedule f or the  pending payables during the year indicating the balance brought forward from previous  years, additions during the year, bills paid during the year and outstanding trade and other  payables as at 30 June, 2025.

425  In addition, payables totalling Kshs.8 12,164,056 or approximately 19% of the total  payables had been outstanding for over three (3) years, an indication that the payables  were not treated as a first charge on the County Revenue Fund in the succeeding years.  No explanation was provided for not   settling the debts or the measures put in place to  settle the bills.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the trade and other payables  balance of Kshs.4,174,866,983 could not be confirmed.  875.   Unsupported   Property, Plant and Equipment Balan ce  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 26 to the financial statements  reflects property, plant and equipment balance of Kshs.1,357,867,605. However, the  balance was not supported by a fixed assets register. Further, the   depreciation charge  for the year amount of Kshs.218,499,332 was not supported by an accounting policy to  guide on the depreciation of various classes of assets as required by the Accounting  Standards.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness o f property, plant and equipment  balance of Kshs.1,357,867,605 could not be confirmed.  Emphasis of Matter  876.   Budgetary   Control   and Performance  The statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts reflects final receipts b udget  and   actual   on   comparable   basis   amounts   of   Kshs.13,018,989,469   and  Kshs.7,345,726,037 respectively, resulting in under - funding of Kshs.5,673,263,431 or  44%   of   the   budget.   However,   the   County   Executive   spent   an   amount   of  Kshs.5,744,336,822 against actu al receipts amount of Kshs.7,345,726,037 resulting in  under - utilization of Kshs.1,601,389,208 or 22% of the actual receipts.  The under - funding and under - utilization affected the planned activities and may have  impacted negatively on service delivery to th e public.  My opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.  Other Matter  877.   Unresolved   Prior   Year Matters  In the audit report of the previous year, several issues were raised under the Report on  Financial   Statements,   Report   on   Lawfulness   and   Effectiveness   in   Use   of   Public  Resources . Review of the status during audit of the County Executive in the financial year  2024/2025 revealed that the following matters remained unresolved;

426  Audit Issues for 2023/2024  1   Incomplete Projects  2   Non - Operationalization of Municipalities of Kajiado, Ngong and Kitengela  3   Legal Expenses  4   Staff Ethnic, Gender and Persons Living with   disabilities   Composition  5   Lack of an Approved Staff Establishment  6   Non - Compliance with the One - Third Basic Salary Rule  Other Information  878.   There were no   material issues relating to Other Information.  REPORT   ON   LAWFULNESS   AND   EFFECTIVENESS   IN   THE   USE   OF   PUBLIC  RESOURCES  Basis for Conclusion  879.   Non - Compliance   with the Development Expenditure Threshold  The statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts reflects total expenditure  amounting to Kshs.7,320,703,769 comprising of amounts of Kshs.5,744,336,832 and  Kshs.1,576,366,937 for recurrent expenditure and development expenditure respectively.  The d evelopment expenditure of Kshs.1,576,366,936 was approximately 22% of the total  expenditure. This was contrary to Regulation 25(1)(g) of the Public Finance Management  (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 that stipulates that   pursuant to Section 107(5)  of   the Act, the County Executive actual expenditure on development shall be at least thirty  percent (30%) in conformity with the requirement under Section 107(2)(a) of the Act.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  880.   Irregular   Engagement   of Casual Workers  The statement of financial performance reflects an amount of Kshs.4,650,645,574 in  respect of employee costs which, as disclosed in Note 9 to the financial statements  includes an expenditure of Kshs.9,650,000 paid to casual workers acro ss different  Departments. However, review of the human resource records revealed that payment  vouchers provided for audit were not supported by daily attendance registers or job cards  approved by the responsible supervisors. Further, there was no evidence   provided to  confirm that the County Public Service Board was involved in recruitment of casuals or  approved their engagement. This was contrary to   Section 74 of the County Governments  Act, 2012 that requires the County Public Service Board to regulate the   engagement of  persons on contract, volunteer and casual workers in its public bodies and offices.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

427  881.   Unsatisfactory   Implementation   of   Projects  The   County   Executive   through   various   Departments   entered   into   contracts   for  implementation of various projects across the County. However, review of sampled  projects files and physical inspection of nine (9) projects valued at Kshs.116,797,538  revealed   var ious discrepancies leading to unsatisfactory   mplementation   of the projects.  In the circumstances, value for money spent on the above projects could not be  confirmed.  882.   Stalled Project for the Construction of County Aggregation and Industrial  Park  The   County Executive through the Department for Trade, initiated construction of County  Aggregation Industrial Park in the financial year 2023/2024, to be funded at a cost of  Kshs.500,000,000 which was a joint contribution of Kshs.250,000,000 each by the Count y  Government and the National Government. However, the County Executive budgeted for  an amount of Kshs.250,000,000 which was revised downwards to Kshs.30,000,000 in the  supplementary budget.  Review of procurement records revealed that, the contract was aw arded to a contractor  at a sum of Kshs.487,548,670 as per the contract agreement signed on 19 September,  2023 to be implemented within a period of ten (10) months. Further, an invoice dated 14  February, 2024 revealed that the contractor requested payment o f Kshs.25,702,571 for  Certificate No.1, being payment of 16% of work completed. However, payment records  to the contractor were not provided.  Further,   the   site   meeting   and   Inspection   Committee   Report   held   and   issued   on  20 February, 20 24 and Progress Report indicated that there was slow execution of the  project. In addition, physical inspection carried out in October, 2025 revealed that the  contractor had abandoned the project. The graded, graveled roadworks, office control  room and gen erator room were overgrown with grass and various materials like block of  stones meant for foundation works were still at the site, exposed to risk of theft as the  larger part of the land remained unfenced or uncontrolled.  Although Management had explaine d that the delay was occasioned by failure by the  National Government to release its part of the contribution towards the project which  affected the implementation of the project as required, no measures were put in place to  ensure completion of the projec t.  In the circumstances, final implementation of the project and value for money could not  be confirmed.  883.   Failure   to Prepare and Submit Quarterly Reports.  Review of the County Executive quarterly re ports for the period ending   31 March, 2025  revealed that the statement of receipts and disbursements, and a statement of arrears of

428  revenue were not prepared and submitted to the County Treasury. This was contrary to  Regulation 64(1) and (4) of the Public Finance Management (County G overnments)  Regulations, 2015   which require the Accounting Officer or receiver   of revenue   or collector  of revenue shall prepare and submit the quarterly reports to the County Treasury not later  than the fifteenth day after the end of each quarter.  In th e circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  884.   Irregular   Payment to Council of Governors and Maa Regional Economic Block  Review of payment details and other supporting documents revealed that Management  paid amounts of Kshs.1,000,000 and Kshs.500,000 to the Council of Governors and Maa  Regional Economic   Blocs   respectively.   This   was   contrary to   Section   37(b) of   the  Intergover nmental Relations Act, 2012 which requires that the operational expenses in  respect of the structures and institutions established in this Act shall be provided for in  the annual estimates of the revenue and expenditure of the National Government.  In the   circumstances, Management was in breach of the regulations.  885.   Irregularities in Procurement Planning and Reporting  Review of documents in respect of the procurement process revealed that, there was no  evidence   of   preparation   of   quarterly   reports   on   the   implementation   of   the   Annual  Procurement Plan and submission to the County Committee Member for Finance. This  was   contrary   to   Regulation   40(6)   of   the   Public   Procurement   and   Asset   Disposal  Regulations, 2020 which requires   a n   A ccounting   O fficer of a procurin g entity to prepare  quarterly report s   on the implementation of the   A nnual   P rocurement   P lan and submit it to  the Cabinet Secretary or County Executive Committee Member for Finance or   person  responsible for the procuring entity or the governing body, as the   case may be.  Further, there was no evidence to confirm that preparation of the Annual Procurement  Plan was preceded by an undertaking of a market survey. This was contrary to Regulation  71(3) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal   Regulations, 2020 which requires  that when   estimating the value of the goods, works or services, the   A ccounting   O fficer  should ensure that the estimate is realistic and based on up - to - date information on  economic and market conditions.  In the circumstance s, Management was in breach of the law.  886.   Irregular   Funding   of Project Under the National Government Function  The County Executive through the Department for Education, Vocational Training, Youth  and Sports entered into a contract for the   fencing of Ilikus hin and Oloilalei Primary  Schools in Imaroro at a contract sum of Kshs.5,909,736   and   construction of Oloolaiser  High School gate at a contract sum of Kshs.1,911,573. However, the projects fall under  the functions   of the National Government. This was contrary to the   fourth schedule of the

429  Constitution of Kenya, which places Primary and Secondary Schools under the f unctions  of the National Government.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  887.   Supply of   Medical   Equipment to Non - Operational Dispensary  The County Executive through Kitengela Municipality procured medical equipment at a  cost of Kshs.2 ,936,600 for   Sholinke Dispensary   vide contract agreement dated 28  February, 2025 which was paid in   May, 2025. Physical inspection carried out on   28 May,  2025 revealed that the structure was incomplete. Although Management explained that  the   medical   equipme nt   was   held   in   safe   custody   in   another   facility   awaiting  operationalization of the Dispensary, no explanation was provided as to why the medical  equipment was procured for a facility that was not complete. This was contrary to Section  153(1) of the Public   Finance Management Act, 2012 that requires the Accounting Officer  to manage assets in such a way as to ensure that the County Government entity achieves  value for money in acquiring, using or disposing of those assets.  In the circumstances,   Management was in breach of the law and value for money on the  expenditure of Kshs.2,936,600 could not be confirmed.  888.   Delay in   Construction   of County Government Headquarters Complex  The County Executive awarded a contract for the construction of the Coun ty Government  of K ajiado Headquarters Complex at a contract sum of Kshs.492,646,852. The contract  agreement was signed on 20 June, 2024 and the contract was to be implemented  within   one   hundred   and   four   (104)   weeks   commencing   15   November,   2024   to  15 November, 2026. Review of records provided for audit revealed that the contractor  was paid an amount of Kshs.98,529,370 being an advance amount paid at the rate of  twenty percent (20%) of the contract sum.  Further, the   project consultant through a letter raised concerns in relation to delayed  works. The letter noted that as   of 13 February, 2025 with four (4) months of the contract  period lapse, only two percent (2%) of the total works had been accomplished signalling  del ayed works and the need for revision of the workplan.   However,   audit inspection  carried out in May, 2025 revealed that there were no works going on as the contractor  had abandoned the site. Further, the foundation works were not completed and heaps of  meta llic materials for blinding works and erection of pillars were left lying at the project  site .  In the circumstances, value for money on the expenditure   for   Kshs.98,529,370 could not  be confirmed.  889.   Failure to Retain   Facilities Improvement Funds   at the Hospitals  Review of revenue records obtained from Level 4 and Level 5 health facilities revealed  that seven (7) health facilities collected a total amount of Kshs.253,680,164 towards the

430  Health Facilities Improvement (FIF). Out of this amount, a t otal of Kshs.190,325,503 was  transferred to County Revenue Fund. However, the County Treasury reimbursed a total  of Kshs.177,163,167 to the health facilities resulting in a deficit of Kshs.13,162,336.   This  was contrary to Section 5(1) of the Facilities Imp rovement Financing Act, 2023 which  requires that all monies raised or received by or on behalf of all Public Health Facilities  be retained in the Hospital Facilities Improvement Financing Account. In addition, failure  to reimburse the total amount transfer red by the facilities negatively impacted on service  delivery by the health facilities.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  REPORT ON EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROLS, RISK MANAGEMENT  AND GOVERNANCE  Basis for Conclusion  890.   Lack of Audit Committee and Ineffective Internal Audit Function  Review of the Internal Audit Work Plan revealed that, although the Internal Audit Function  had planned to carry out thirteen (13) audits during the financial year under review, the  Unit man aged to complete five (5) of the planned audits.   Further, there was no Audit  Committee   in   place.   This   was   contrary   to   Section   155(5)   of   the   Public   Finance  Management Act, 2012 which provides that a County Government entity shall establish  an internal audi ting committee whose composition and functions are to be prescribed by  the regulations.  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of the Internal Audit Function in carrying out  oversight role in the County Executive could not be confirmed.  891.   Lack of Risk   Management Policy and Disaster Recovery plan  Review of records and information provided by Management in relation to internal controls  revealed that the County Executive lacked an approved Risk Management Policy.  Further, the County Executive did not   have a   Disaster Recovery   and   Business Continuity  Plan contrary to the provisions of Regulation 158(b)(1) of the Public Finance Management  (County Governments) Regulations, 2015.   In addition, there was no evidence that a  formal risk assessment was conducted   during the year under review.  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of Management   in addressing emerging risks and  assure continuity of business operations in case of a disaster could not be confirmed.  892.   Weakness in Information Technology   Control Environment  Review of the County’s Information Communication Technology (IC T) environment  revealed that the County Executive lacked a formal approved ICT Policy.   Management  explained that the Policy had already been formulated but was yet to be approved by the  Executive Committee. Further, the County Executive was operating with out an IT Steering  Committee and an up - to - date approved IT Strategic Plan.

431  In the circumstances, the efficiency and effectiveness of Information Communication  Technology Controls could not be confirmed.  893.   Unsatisfactory Sectoral Report  Review of records provided by the County Executive Climate Change Unit for audit  indicated that Management was yet to establish measurement reporting and verification  (MRV+) system that will be able to gather data and reports on sectoral greenhouse ga s  emissions for the National Inventory. This implies that the Climate Change Unit has not  been able to file the required reports on mitigation, adaptation actions and benefits with  the National Council. Further, no annual reports had been submitted to the   National  Council on status and progress of performance and implementation of assigned Climate  Change duties.  In the circumstances, the efficiency and effectiveness of the Unit in measurement and  providing timely reports on sectoral greenhouse gas emission s for the National inventory  could not be confirmed.

432  COUNTY EXECUTIVE   OF   KERICHO   –   NO.35  REPORT ON THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS  Basis for Adverse   Opinion  894.   Unsupported Opening Balances  The statement of financial position reflects total assets and total liabilities opening  balances   of   Kshs.606,588,886   and   Kshs.1,211,995,248 ,   respectively,   resulting   in  negative net assets opening balance of Kshs.605,406,362. However, the balances were  not supported by the Transition Project   Co - ordination Committee report. Further, the  listing of the assets and liabilities was not provided for   audit review.  In addition, the statement reflects property, plant and equipment opening balance of  Kshs.345,658,601.   However,   the   amount   is   at   variance   with   the   balance   of  Kshs.15,560,830,144 reflected in the summary of non - current assets register for th e  previous year resulting in variance of Kshs.15,215,171,543.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness opening balances could not be  confirmed.  895.   Variance in the Use of Goods and Services Expenditure  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 10 to the financial  statements   reflects   use   of   goods   and   services   amounting   to   Kshs.2,171,715,695.  However, the amount includes various expenditure items totalling Kshs.174,583,661 at  variance   with the supporting general ledgers that had a total amount of Kshs.172,521,661  resulting in   unreconciled   variance of Kshs.2,062,000 .  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of   use of goods and services  amounting to Kshs.2,062,000   could not be confirmed.  896.   Inaccuracies in Employee Costs  The   statement   of   financial   performance   reflects   employee   costs   amounting   to  Kshs.3,388,084,170. However, the corresponding Note 9 to the financi al statements  reflects   an   amount   of   Kshs.3,387,953,221   resulting   unreconciled   variance   of  Kshs.130,949. Further, the payroll and supporting schedules for employee costs reflects  an amount of   Kshs.3,335,801,370 resulting in   unreconciled   variance of Kshs.52, 282,800.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of   employee costs amounting to  Kshs.52,413,749   could not be confirmed.

433  897.   Inaccuracies in Transfers to Bomet Water and Sanitation Company Limited  The statement of financial performance reflects transfer to other Government entities  amounting to Kshs.502,651,539 as disclosed in Note 11 to the financial statements. The  amount includes transfers to Bomet Water and Sanitation Company Limited totalling  K shs.18,433,620. However, review of records revealed that only two (2) payments of  Kshs.7,500,000 each were made on 21 August, 2024 and 21 January, 2025 respectively  all   totalling   Kshs.15,000,000   resulting   in   unreconciled   variance   of   Kshs.3,433,620.  Furthe r, the records of Bomet Water and Sanitation Company Limited reflected receipts  amounting to Kshs.15,000,000 .  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of   transfers to Bomet Water and  Sanitation Company Limited amounting to Kshs.3,433,620 could   not be confirmed.  898.   Inaccuracies in Transfers to National Agricultural Value Chain Development  Project  The statement of financial performance reflects transfer to other Government entities  amounting to Kshs.502,651,539. The amount includes transfers to National Agricultural  Value   Chain   Development   Project   (NAVCDP)   amounting   to   Kshs.144,514,015   as  disclosed   in Note 11 to the financial statements. However, the amount was at variance  with the Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS) payment details  balance of Kshs.89,383,098 resulting in   unreconciled   variance of Kshs.55,130,917.  Further, the   Project’s opening bank balance at 1 July, 2024 was Kshs.134,927,319, while  during the year the Project received an amount of Kshs.144,514,015 and the closing bank  balance was Kshs.413,304 which indicates that the total expenditure for the Project was  Kshs .279,028,030. However, the respective expenditure returns together with the related  accountability supporting documents were not provided for audit review.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and the completeness of the transfers to National  Agricultural   Value Chain Development Project amounting to Kshs.55,130,917 could not  be confirmed.  899.   Unsupported Property, Plant and Equipment Balance  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 26 to the financial statements  reflects property, plant   and equipment balance of Kshs.854,402,767. However, no  depreciation was charged on property, plant and equipment in the year. This was contrary  to Policy 4(d) of the summary of significant accounting policies to the financial statements  which provides that   all property, plant and equipment are stated at cost less accumulated  depreciation and impairment losses. Further, the assets register and listing of assets in  support of the disclosed balance were not provided for audit review.  In addition, the balance   includes an expenditure amounting to Kshs.4,851,724 incurred  on the purchase of 0.5 hectares of land for the construction of a ward office at Kapsurer

434  Ward. However, the title deed for the land was not provided for audit review. Similarly,  the amount of K shs.854,402,767 includes work - in - progress totalling Kshs.137,299,890  whose details of the nature of works, commencement date, expected date of completion,  name of the contractor engaged, contract amount, interim certificates and progress  reports were not p rovided for audit verification.  Further,   the   property,   plant   and   equipment   balance   included   an   amount   of  Kshs.2,100,000 in respect of motor vehicles additions during the year which was at  variance with the respective IFMIS payment details expenditure of   Kshs.6,000,000  resulting in   unreconciled   variance of Kshs.3,900,000.  In the circumstances, the accuracy, completeness and ownership of   property, plant and  equipment balance of Kshs.854,402,767   could not be confirmed.  900.   Unsupported Intangible Assets   Balance  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 27 to the financial statements  reflects intangible assets balance of Kshs.20,316,233 which relates to additions in the  year under review. However, review of payment records   revealed that software items that  were procured during the year amounted to Kshs.13,873,100   resulting in variance of  Kshs.6,443,133. Further, the names of software procured, their purpose or function,  where they operate from and the installation and hand o ver reports were not provided for  audit review. In addition, payment vouchers in support of software payment amounting to  Kshs.1,500,000 made during the year were not provided for audit review.  Similarly, the intangible assets were not amortized as requir ed. This was contrary to  Policy 4(g) of the summary of significant accounting policies to the financial statements  which provides that   the   intangible assets are stated at cost less accumulated amortization  and impairment losses.  In the circumstances, the   ownership, accuracy and completeness of   intangible assets  balance of Kshs.20,316,233   could not be confirmed.  901.   Undisclosed Trade and Other Payables Balance  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 32 to the financial statements  reflec ts trade and other payables balance of Kshs1,884,953,574. However, the amount  excluded twenty - one (21) Court awards made against the County Executive over the  years totalling Kshs.69,083,118 which had not been paid and there was no evidence of  appeal by Ma nagement.   Further, the amount had not been disclosed as a contingent  liability as required.  In addition, the balance of Kshs.1,884,953,514 did not include payables to Kenya Medical  Supplies Authority (KEMSA). However, collaborative evidence from KEMSA re vealed that  the County Executive owed the Authority an amount of Kshs.61,140 for medical supplies  which was not disclosed in the financial statements.

435  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of   trade and other payables  balance of Kshs.69,144, 258   could not be confirmed.  902.   Inaccuracies in Accumulated Surplus  The   statement   of   financial   position   reflects   accumulated   surplus   balance   of  Kshs.188,862,932. The balance includes opening surplus amount of Kshs.173,161,379  as reflected in the   statement of changes in net assets. However, the previous years  audited financial statements reflected surplus amounting to Kshs.229,908,705 resulting  in a variance of Kshs.56,747,326.  Further, the balance includes an unexplained and unsupported negative   adjustment to  recognize assets and liabilities amount of Kshs.778,567,740 as reflected in the statement  of changes in net assets. However, the adjustments amount was at variance with the  negative   net   assets   operating   balance   totalling   Kshs.605,406,362   refl ected   in   the  statement of financial position resulting in variance of Kshs.173,161,378.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the   accumulated surplus  balance of Kshs.188,862,932   could not be confirmed.  903.   Unsupported Printing,   Advertisement and Information Supplies  The statement of financial performance reflects use of goods and services amount of  Kshs.2,171,715,695 as disclosed in Note 10 to the financial statements. The amount  includes printing, advertising and information su pplies and services expenditure of  Kshs.31,258,398.   However,   payment   documents   in   support   of   payments   totalling  Kshs.19,376,766 were not provided for audit review.  In   the   circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of   printing, advertising   and  informatio n supplies and services amounting to Kshs.19,376,766 could not be confirmed.  904.   Unsupported Insurance Costs  The statement of financial performance reflects use of goods and services amounting to  Kshs.2,171,715,695 as disclosed in Note 10 to the financial statements which includes  insurance costs totalling Kshs.82,439,739. The insurance costs includes an amount o f  Kshs. 40,939,739 incurred on   motor vehicle insurance which was not supported by,  valuation reports, signed contract and policy documents for the insured motor vehicles.  Further,   seven   (7)   motor   vehicles   with   GK   registration   numbers   valued   at  Kshs.27,164,0 00   were insured at a   total premium of Kshs.747,000 yet the vehicles   were  not disclosed in the asset register under the respective category, and   no log books were  provided for audit review.  In addition, the insurance costs includes an amount of Kshs.41,500 ,000 in relation to part  payment   to   an   Insurance   Broker   through   not   serialized   payment   voucher   dated  20 June, 2025 for provision of comprehensive medical insurance and group life cover to

436  the County Executive staff at a contract sum of   Kshs.200,000,139 effective 1 May, 2025.  However, the contract agreement signed between the County Executive and the service  provider did not provide the details of the names and number of members of staff covered,  their dependents and the medical cover li mits. No explanation was provided for not  signing the insurance contract with the underwriter and paying the insurance broker  instead of the underwriter. The accrued insurance cost of Kshs.158,500,139 was also not  disclosed as a payable in the financial st atements.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the   insurance costs amounting  to Kshs.82,439,739 could not be confirmed.  905.   Unsupported Transfers to Vocational Training Centers  The statement of financial performance reflects transfer to other Government entities  amounting to Kshs.502,651,539 as disclosed in Note 11 to the financial statements which  includes transfers to Vocational Training Centers totalling Kshs.39,308,107. Howev er,  expenditure returns and acknowledgement from beneficiary Institutions were not provided  for audit review.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of   transfers to Vocational Training  Centers amounting to Kshs.39,308,107   could not be confirm ed.  906.   Unsupported Access Road Expenditure  The statement of financial performance reflects use of goods and services amount of  Kshs.2,171,715,695 as disclosed in Note 10 to the financial statements which includes  access roads expenditure amount of Kshs.653, 436,226. However, Management did not  provide details of the roads repaired or constructed, contract amount for each road done  and payment documents for audit review.  Further,   the   access   road   expenditure   includes   legal   expenses   amounting   to  Kshs.9,897,699.   However, the legal expenses were wrongly charged to access roads and  Management did not explain the anomaly.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of   access roads expenditure  amounting to Kshs.653,436,226   could not be confirmed.  907.   Unsupporte d Cash and Cash Equivalents Balance  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 21 to the financial statements  reflects cash and cash equivalents balance of Kshs.86,230,126. However, the balance  was not supported by certificate of bank ba lances, bank statements, board of survey  reports and bank reconciliation statements.  In the circumstances, the existence, accuracy and completeness of   cash and cash  equivalents balance of Kshs.86,230,126   could not be confirmed.

Review   of   the   respective   ledge rs   and   Integrated   Financial  Management Information System   ( IFMIS) payment details revealed that transactions  amounting to Kshs.3,321,920,045 and Kshs.166,819,466 were made to Kericho County  Government   and   Kericho   Chief   Officer - Finance,   respectively   all   tot alling  Kshs.3,488,739,511. However, the nature of the payments and the ultimate beneficiaries  was not explained or provided for audit review. Unsupported   Kericho   County   Kenya   Urban   Support   Program   Urban  Development Grant  The   statement   of   financial   performance   reflects   total   expenses   amounting   to  Kshs.6,163,967,157. 438  912.   Unsupported Cash Payments  The   statement   of   financial   performance   reflects   total   expenses   amounting   to  Kshs.6,163,967,157. The amount includes a balance of K shs.141,055,481 paid under  cash sub item to suppliers and individuals and Kshs.75,692,646 paid as late duty  allowances   which   were   not   supported   with   payment   vouchers   and   its   related  documentation including lists of beneficiaries among others. Budgetary Control and Performance  The statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts reflects total receipts  budget and actual on comparable basis of Kshs.8,769,871,719 and Kshs.6,042,824,075  respectively resulting in underfunding of Kshs.2,727,047,644 or approximately 31% of the  approved budget. However, Management spent an amount of Kshs.5,932,300,322 out of  the actual receipts amount of Kshs.6,042,824,075 resulting   in   under - expenditure of  Kshs.110,523,753.  The underfunding affected the implementation of planned activities and programmes   and  may have negatively impacted on effective service delivery to the public. However, Management  had not resolved   twenty - eight   (28) the issues or given any explanations for failure to  implement the recommendations.

440  Other Information  919.   There were no material issues relating to Other Information.  REPORT   ON   LAWFULNESS   AND   EFFECTIVENESS   IN   THE   USE   OF   PUBLIC  RESOURCES  Basis for Conclusion  920.   Failure to Prepare and Submit Financial Statements for Kenya Devolution  Support Programme II  The statement of financial performance reflects transfers to other Government entities  amounting to Kshs.502,651,539. The amount includes transfers to Kenya Devolution  Support Programme II (KDSP 2). However, the financial statements for the programme  were   not prepared and submitted to the Auditor - General. This was contrary to Regulation  101(4) of the Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015  which requires   a n   A cc oun ti n g   O ffice r   to   p re p ar e   a n d s u b m i t   fi n a n cia l   state m e n t s   no t  late r   t h a n   t h re e   mon t h s   afte r   t h e   e n d   o f   t h e   fi n a n cia l   y ea r   a n d   s ubm i t   t h e m   to   t h e  Aud it o r - G e n era l   w it h   a   c op y   t o   t h e   Coun t y   T reas u r y ,   t h e   Con tr o lle r   o f   Budg e t   a n d   t h e  N ati on a l   T reas u r y.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  921.   Non - Compliance   with   Guidelines   on   Transition   from   Cash   to   Accrual  Accounting  Review of the transition process revealed that the   County Steering Committee   to oversee  the planning, execution and monitoring of the transition process had not been established.  This was contrary to Guideline 1.5(iii) on Transition from Cash to Accrual Accounting by  Ministries,   Departments,   Agencies   and   County   Governments   in   Kenya,   2024   and  Paragraph 2.1.1 of The National Treasury and Economic Planning Circular Referenced  No.03/2 025 dated 14 April, 2025 which directed that an entity steering committee made  up of officers from relevant Departments be established by the Accounting Officer.  Further, Project   Manager   responsible for leading and coordinating all activities related to  t he transition process had not been appointed.   This was contrary to Paragraph 2.1.2 of  the Guidelines that directed the Accounting Officers to appoint a project manager from  among the service staff to oversee the transition from cash to accrual accounting   project.  In the circumstances, lack of leadership and coordination may delay the transition process  and result in non - achievement of key milestones and deliverables outlined in the transition  roadmap.

441  922.   Irregular Transfer of   Hospitals Revenue to   County Revenue Fund  Review of revenue records obtained from Level 4 and Level 5 health facilities in Kericho  County   revealed   that   seven   (7)   Health   facilities   collected   revenue   amounting   to  Kshs.566,976,183   that   included,   a   total   amount   of   Kshs.62,168,779   which   was  transferred to the County Revenue Fund. This was contrary   to Section 5(1) of the  Facilities Improvement Financing Act, 2023 which requires that all monies raised or  received by or on behalf of all public health facilities be retained in the Hospi tal Facilities  Improvement Financing account.   However, the County Treasury reimbursed a total of  Kshs.65,297,630   to   the   health   facilities   resulting   in   excess   reimbursement   of  Kshs.3,128,807 in respect of Roret Level 4 Hospital.  In the circumstances, Manag ement was in breach of the law.  923.   Long Outstanding Trade and Other Payables Balance  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 32 to the financial statements  reflects trade and other payables balance of Kshs.1,884,953,574. The ageing analysis  provided revealed that an amount of Kshs.533,924,516 or 28% of total payables h as been  outstanding for more than one (1) year. This was contrary to Regulation 41(2) of the Public  Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which provides that   d e b t  ser v ic e   p a y m e n t s   s h al l   b e   a   firs t   c h ar g e   o n   t h e   Coun t y   R e v e nu e   Fun d.   No   reason was  provided for failure by Management to settle the balance of Kshs.533,924,516.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  924.   Unauthorized Over Expenditure  The   statement   of   financial   performance   reflects   total   expenses   amounting   to  Kshs.6,163,967,157. Review of the IFMIS payment details revealed that the amount  includes expenses totalling Kshs. 5,460,167,341. However, this expenditure exceeded   the  corresponding   approved   budget   amount   of   Kshs. 4,718,017,542   resulting   in   an  unauthorized over expenditure of   Kshs.742,149,799.   This was   contrary to Regulation  42(1) of the Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which  requires an Accounting Officer to ensure that public funds entrusted to their care are  pr operly safeguarded and are applied for purpose for only which they were intended and  appropriated by the County Assembly.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  925.   Non - Compliance with Fiscal Responsibility Principles on Wages  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 9 to the financial  statements reflects employee costs amounting to Kshs.3,388,084,170. The amount was  equivalent to forty - nine percent (49%) of the County Executive’s total revenue amounting  t o Kshs.6,958,060,201.   This was contrary to Regulation 25(1)(b) of the Public Finance  Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which   provides that the limit for

442  County Government's expenditure on wages and benefits shall not exceed thirty - five (35)  percent of the County Government's total revenue .  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  926.   Failure to Implement Budgeted Water Projects  Review of Projects Implementation Status report revealed that water and sewerage  infrastructural works under rural schemes budgeted for an amount of Kshs.210,010,917.  However, the respective projects had not been implemented during the year under  review. F urther, no evidence was provided to show that the responsible Authority to Incur  Expenditure (AIE) holder informed the Accounting Officer on the non - performance of the  budgetary provisions by 15 February, 2025. This was contrary to Regulation 116 of the  Pu blic Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which states that;  where an A.I.E holder observes that it will not be possible to   all o cate d   for   a   p a r ti cu la r  project   i n   a   g i v e n   fi n a n cia l   y ear ,   t h e   A I E   ho l d e r   s h al l   i n f o r m   t h e   Acc oun ti n g   O ffice r   no t  late r   t h a n   t h e   15 t h   F e b r u ar y   eac h   y ear .   Th e   A cc oun ti n g   O ffice r   s h al l   t h e n   s u rre nd e r  t h e   res ou rce s   t o   t h e County   Treasury   and   the   County   Treasury   shall   ensure   that   the  f und s   are   re - vo te d   for   the project   in   t h e following   financial   year   in   o r d e r   t o   c on ti nu e  t h e   i mp le m e n tati o n   o f   t h e   p r o ject .  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  927.   Projects Implemented Outside the Approved Procurement Plan  Review of records revealed that an expenditure amounting to   Kshs.230,573,346 was  incurred on construction of roads. However, the roads constructed were not included in  the approved procurement plan. This was contrary to Section 45(3) of the Public  Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015 which requires all procurem ent processes to  align with the approved budget and be undertaken in accordance with an annual  procurement plan developed by the procuring entity.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  928.   Unsupported Strategic Intervention  The County Executive budgetary performance implementation and indicators for the year  under review reflects budgetary provision in respect of strategic intervention phase 1 and  2   amounts   of   Kshs.100,000,000   and   Kshs.134,000,000   respectively,   all   totalling  Kshs.234,000,000.   However, the budget estimate   and   performance   presented   and  approved by the County Assembly did not contain lists of strategic intervention projects  to be financed. This was contrary to Regulation 50(3) of the Public Finance   Management  (Co unty Governments) Regulations, 2015 which requires an   Accounting Officer of a  Government entity to make an expenditure commitment against the procurement plan  approved for that entity in Accordance with the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal  Act and Reg ulations made thereunder.

443  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  929.   Non - Compliance with the Law on Affirmative Action on 30% of Procurement  Opportunities  Review of the procurement plan revealed that enterprises owned by youth, women, and  persons with disabilities were allocated an amount of Kshs.742,304,923 of the planned  annual procurement amounting to Kshs.2,916,301,125, representing twenty five percent  ( 25%) of the annual procurement budget. This was contrary to Regulation   149 of the  Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Regulations, 2020 which requires an Accounting  Officer of a procuring entity to allocate at least thirty percent (30%) of its annual  pro curement budget for the purposes of procuring goods, works and services from  enterprises owned by youth, women and persons with disability.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  930.   Non - Compliance with the One Third Rule on Basic Salary  Review of the monthly payroll records revealed that three hundred and eighty - nine (389)  employees earned a net salary of less than one - third (1/3) of the basic salary in various  months during   the   yea r   under review.   This   was   contrary   to   Section   19(3) of   the  Employment Act, 2007 which requires that deductions made by an employer from the  wages of his employee at any one time shall not exceed two - thirds of such wages.  In the circumstances, Management w as in breach of the law.  931.   Appointment in Acting Capacity Beyond the Stipulated Period  Review of the human resource records revealed that a member of staff had been  appointed in acting capacity for more than six (6) months. This was in contravention of  Paragraph C14(1) of the Human Resource Policies and Procedures Manual for the Public  Se rvice, 2016 which requires that when an officer is eligible for appointment to a higher  post and is called upon to act in that post pending advertisement of the post, he or she is  eligible for payment of acting allowance at the rate of twenty percent (20%)   of his  substantive basic salary and that acting allowance will not be payable to an officer for  more than six (6) months.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the Human Resource Manual.  932.   Nugatory Expenditure on Legal Fees  The statement of financial   performance reflects   use of goods and services amounting to  Kshs.2,171,715,695 as disclosed in Note 10 to the financial statements which   includes  other   operating   expenses amounting   to Kshs.199,605,631. The other operating expense s  further include s   an expenditure of   Kshs.3,278,377 paid to an Advocate on behalf of a  claimant for trespass on his land. Review of records revealed that the payment was in

444  respect of compensation award of Kshs.2,000,000 plus accrued interest which arose f rom  illegal trespass on the claimant’s half an acre of land during road construction by a  contractor hired by the County Executive. The contractor allegedly delineated the marks  on the boundaries of the land and damaged property on the land which Managemen t  claimed was public land lying on a road reserve. No order or notice to vacate the land  was given by the County Executive’s Department for Roads to the residents occupying  the land which resulted to the damage of property. Had the order or notice been giv en to  the residents to vacate the road reserve and public land, there would have been no suit  and the expenditure of Kshs.3,278,375 would not have been incurred.  Further,   the   Environment   and   Lands   Court   in   Kericho   No.   E010   of   2020   dated  6 July,   2023 decree awarded an am ount of Kshs.2,000,000 against the County Executive.  However, the amount was not paid within the required time which attracted an interest of  Kshs.490,000, cost of the case of Kshs.633,233 and interest on cost awarded amounting  to Kshs.155,142 all totallin g to Kshs.1,278,375 which was avoidable.  In the circumstances, value for money on the legal fees and interest paid on the Court  awards totalling Kshs.3,278,375 could not be confirmed.  933.   Irregularities in Procurement of Empowerment Materials  The statemen t of financial performance reflects use of goods and services expenditure  amounting to Kshs.2,171,715,695 as disclosed in Note 10 the financial statements. The  amount includes an expenditure amount of Kshs.7,971,636 which   was   incurred on  procurement of assorted empowerment materials. However, the expenditure was not in  the procurement plan or in the approved budget for the year under review. This was  contrary to Section 44(2)(a) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act,   2015  which provides that in the performance of the responsibility, an Accounting Officer shall  ensure that procurements of goods, works and services of the public entity are within  approved budget of that entity. Further, request for quotations, regret le tters to the  unsuccessful bidders, inspection and acceptance certificates and distribution lists of the  empowerment materials in support of the expenditure were not provided for audit  verification.  In addition, review of Counter Receipt Vouchers (S13) an d Counter Requisition and Issue  Vouchers (S11) revealed that one officer received and issued all the items delivered. This  was contrary to the segregation of duties internal control. The delivery notes not signed  by the suppliers and the officers who recei ved the items at the County Executive.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  934.   Grounded Motor Vehicles  Review of records revealed that forty - seven (47) motor vehicles were grounded during  the year under review. The vehicles comprise   of nineteen (19) serviceable units and  twenty - eight (28) grounded but recommended for disposal. However, no explanation was

445  given on why the unserviceable motor vehicles and transport equipment had not been  bonded and earmarked for disposal. This was contr ary to Regulation 176(1) of the Public  Procurement and Asset Disposal Regulations, 2020 which requires an Accounting Officer  to ensure that an Annual Assets Disposal Plan is prepared for items declared as  unserviceable, surplus or obsolete stores, asset or   equipment.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  935.   Irregular Expenditure on Contracted Borehole Drilling Services  The County Executive outsourced borehole drilling services and paid an amount of  Kshs.15,018,224. However, the   County Executive had its own borehole drilling equipment  which includes a drilling rig, compressor, testing pump, generator and a support truck. No  explanation was provided for outsourcing borehole drilling services. This was contrary to  Regulation   39(1)(a )   of   the   Public   Finance   Management   (County   Governments)  Regulations,   2015   which   requires   an   Accounting   Officer   to   ensure   efficient   and  economical use of budgeted funds and that value for money is achieved in the delivery of  services.  In the circumstances,   public resources were not applied in a prudent and efficient manner.  936.   Irregular Payment of Legal Fees  Legal fees amounting to Kshs.10,338,464 was paid to a legal fi rm on 24 September, 2024  in respect of the amount of decree together with cost execution and Court collection fees  which was outstanding for four (4) years. This amount was at variance with the decree  amount of Kshs.9,106,244 provided in ELC Petition No. E 0003 of 2021 resulting in an  overpayment   of   Kshs.1,232,220.   Further,   the   amount   of   Kshs.9,106,244   was   not  supported by a statement of cost and the respective fee note from the legal firm.  In addition, legal fees amounting to Kshs.12,821,788 and outstandin g compensation on  legal fees of Kshs.48,888,829 all totalling Kshs.61,710,617 was paid in the year under  review.   However,   the   amount   exceeded   the   approved   budgeted   amount   of  Kshs.10,000,000 resulting in an unauthorized expenditure of Kshs.51,710,617.  In   the circumstances, public resources may not have been applied in a prudent and  efficient manner.  937.   Delayed Construction of County Aggregation and Industrial Park  The contract for the construction of County Aggregation and Industrial Park (CAIP) in  Kapso rok was signed on 17 October, 2023 at a contract price of Kshs.541,000,000.  Review of records revealed that the project was to be done under counterpart funding  arrangement between the National Government and the County Executive at amounts of  Kshs.291,000 ,000 and Kshs.250,000,000, respectively. The contract period was to expire  on 21 August, 2025. However, at the time of audit in June, 2025 the contractor had been

446  paid a total of Kshs.72,872,622 equivalent of 14% against estimated physical progress  of 6 %.  Physical verification of the project on 4 June, 2025, revealed that several works included  in the Bills of Quantities totalling Kshs.512,885,072 were yet to be done.  In the circumstances, value for money on the expenditure of   Kshs.72,872,622 incurred  on the project could not be confirmed.  938.   Delayed Completion of Rehabilitation and Construction of Kimologit Water  Supply Project  The contract for the proposed rehabilitation and construction of Kimologit Water Project  at a contract sum of Kshs.186,289,133 for a contract period of twelve (12) months, with  estimated completion date on 11 July, 2020, was signed on 30 May, 2019. Review   of  records revealed that the contract had been extended severally for periods cumulating to  fifty - three (53) months, with the latest one having expired on 23 June, 2025. The  contractor had been paid a total of Kshs.136,025,070, equivalent to 73% of the con tract  sum.  Physical verification carried out on 12 June, 2025 revealed that the contractor had  abandoned the site while works totalling Kshs. 9,970,090 as per the Bills of Quantities  (BQ’s)   had not been executed. Further, t he contracts and   performance Bon d guarantee  had   expired on 23 June, 2025 and   5 May, 2025 respectively.  Further,   the   treatment   plant   was   located   on   a   donated   piece   of   land   measuring  approximately 2.5 Acres. However, the title deed of the land was not provided for audit  review.  In the c ircumstances, value for money on the expenditure of Kshs.136,025,070 incurred  on the project could not be confirmed.  939.   Stalled Construction and Equipping of Theater at Ainamoi Health Centre  The contract for the construction and equipping of an operating s urgical theatre at  Ainamoi Sub - County Hospital at a cost of Kshs.14,135,859 was to be completed on  4 June, 2020. Review of records revealed that the full contract sum had already been  paid. Further, the contract period had expired and it was ex tended to 19 August, 2022.  However, physical verification of the facility on 17 June, 2025 revealed that the Project  had stalled and the contractor was not at site.  In the circumstances, value for money on the expenditure of Kshs.14,135,859 incurred  on th e project could not be confirmed.

447  940.   Delayed Completion of Modern Market at Sondu  The contract for the construction and completion of modern Sondu   Market at a contract  sum of Kshs.128,945,229 was signed on 12 June, 2019 with a contract period of fifty - two  (52) weeks with effect from 14 August, 2019. Review of the Project Implementation Status  report as at June,2025, indicated that the contractor has   been paid an accumulated  amount of Kshs.107,665,976 or 72% of the contract sum with works certified at 90%. No  budgetary provisions on the remaining works were provided for during the year under  review.  Physical verification of the project carried out on   17 June, 2025 revealed that the contract  period had expired and several works were yet to be completed. However, the contractor  was on site but works were progressing at a slow pace and without an addendum or  approved extension to the original contract.  In the circumstances, value for money for the expenditure of Kshs.107,665,976 already  spent on the project could not be confirmed.  941.   Delayed Completion of Kapkures Water Supply Project  The contract for the rehabilitation and construction of Kapkur es Water Supply project at  a contract sum of Kshs.87,417,116 was signed on 30 May, 2019 for a contract period of  twelve (12) months from the date of signing the contract. Review of records revealed that  the completion date was extended to 17 February, 2023 . However, the status report as  at June, 2025 indicated that the progress of works certified stood at 85% and additional  works originally not in the Bills of Quantities (BQ’s) including, fencing, construction of new  gravity main from intake to treatment wo rks and completion of pipe fittings on twin  treatment works were yet to be completed.  Further, the contractor had been paid a cumulative amount of Kshs.63,713,770 to date  inclusive of consultancy services amount of Kshs.23,348,579 and variation works amo unt  of Kshs.2,500,000 paid via payment certificate No. 2 and which was not approved by the  Evaluation Committee before it was submitted to the Accounting Officer for approval. In  addition, the performance bond guarantee provided had expired.  In the circu mstances, value for money on the expenditure amounting to Kshs.63,713,770  incurred on the project could not be confirmed.  942.   Lack of Risk Management Policy  The County Executive had no approved Risk Management Policy. This was contrary to  Regulation   158(1)   of   the   Public   Finance   Management   (County   Governments)  Regulations, 2015 which requires that the Accounting Officer ensure that the county  government entity develops risk management strategies, which include fraud prevention  mechanism and a system of risk m anagement and internal control that builds robust  business operations.

448  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  REPORT ON EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROLS, RISK MANAGEMENT  AND GOVERNANCE  943.   U nderstaffing of Internal Audit   Department  Review of the documents provided for audit revealed that the Directorate of Internal Audit  and Risk Management had six (6) staff out of an approved thirty - eight (38) staff  establishment. This was an indication of inadequate staff in the Departm ent.  Further, the Directorate lacked an approved budget and workplan. In addition, there was  no Internal Audit Charter and evidence of risk management reports undertaken in  the year.  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of internal contro ls, risk management and  governance could not be confirmed.  944.   Lack of Audit Committee  Review of the governance structure in place revealed that the County Executive did not  have an Internal Audit Committee in place. This was contrary to the provisions of S ection  155(5)   of   the   Public   Finance   Management   Act,   2012   which   requires   a   County  Government entity to establish an internal audit committee whose composition and  functions are to be prescribed by the regulations.  In the circumstances, effectiveness and o versight of internal controls and governance  could not be confirmed.  945.   Weaknesses in Access to Government Opportunities Controls  Review of procurement records revealed that a supplier was contracted to supply, deliver  and   install   assorted   furniture   in   new   Hospital   facilities   at   a   contract   price   of  Kshs.2,840,700. The contract was signed on 19 February, 2024 two (2) months after  evaluation of tenders was approved on 20 January, 2024. The tender was reserved for  Access to Government Opportunities   ( AGPO) (wome n). However, the AGPO Certificate  provided by the supplier related to a different firm. Further, the contract for the supply of  medical   equipment   for   Londiani   Sub - County   Hospital   at   a   contract   price   of  Kshs.2,064,000 was reserved for AGPO (groups) but the   AGPO Certificate provided by  the supplier belonged to a different firm.  In   the   circumstances,   the   effectiveness   of   controls   on   Access   to   Government  Procurement Opportunities could not be confirmed.
