469  COUNTY EXECUTIVE   OF   KAKAMEGA   –   NO.37  REPORT ON THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS  Basis for Qualified   Opinion  991.   Unsupported Prior Year Adjustment  The   statement   of   changes   in   net   assets   reflects   net   assets   balance   of  Kshs.1,095,201,214 as at 30 June, 2025. However, the balance includes prio r year  adjustment   of   Kshs.675,934,192   described   as   difference   between   receivables   and  payables for financial year 2023/2024, which has not been supported by relevant  documentation and explanation for its inclusion in the financial statements.  In   the   circu mstances,   the   accuracy   and   completeness   of   net   assets   balance   of  Kshs.1,095,201,214 could not be confirmed.  992.   Unsupported Working Capital Adjustments  The statement of cash flows reflects net cash flows from operating activities amounting  to Kshs.1,441,072,822 as disclosed in Note 22 to the financial statements. However, Note  22 to the financial statements on cash generated from operations includes an un explained  working   capital   adjustment   amount   of   Kshs.675,934,192   described   as   prior   year  adjustment (difference between receivables and payables for financial year 2023/2024).  However, the journal entries, nature of adjustment, workings and supporting docum ents  were not provided for audit review.  Further, the statement indicates increase in payables balance of Kshs.77,894,425.  However, recalculation of the change reflects an increase of Kshs.810,799,158 resulting  in a variance of Kshs.732,904,733 described   as pending bills for acquisition of assets  under the workings for the increase in payables but the reason for the exclusion of the  amount in the changes in payables was unjustified and the analysis of the amount and  supporting documents were not provided   for audit review.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the net cash flows from  operating activities amount of Kshs.1,441,072,822 could not be confirmed.  993.   Unsupported Outstanding Imprests  The statement of financial position and as disc losed in Note 15 to the financial statements  reflects receivables from exchange transactions balance of Kshs.21,753,905, which  includes outstanding imprests amount of Kshs.18,325,045. However, Management did  not maintain an updated imprests register indica ting details of payees and amounts,  imprest warrant number, date of issue, due date and date of surrender. Further, no  explanation was provided for the failure to have the imprests recovered or surrendered  as at 30 June, 2025.

470  In the circumstances, the a ccuracy, existence and occurrence of the outstanding imprests  balance of Kshs.18,325,045 could not be confirmed.  Emphasis of Matter  994.   Budgetary Control and Performance  T h e   s t a t e m en t   o f   c o m pa r i s o n   o f   b ud g e t   an d   a c t u a l   a m o un t s   r e f l e c t s   f ina l   r e c e ip t s   bu d ge t  a n d   a c t ua l   o n   c o m pa r a bl e   b a s i s   t o t all i n g Ks h s. 16,172,021,545   a n d   Ks h s. 11,857,449,274  r e s pe c t i v e l y,   r e s ul t i n g   i n   un d e r - f und i n g   o f Ks h s. 4,314,572,271 o r   27 %   o f   t h e   bu d ge t .  However,   t h e   Coun t y   Ex e c u t i ve   s p en t   an amount of   Ks h s. 11,913,264,879   a gain st   actual  receipts o f   Ks h s. 11,857,449,274   r e s u l t in g   to   over - utilization   o f   Ks h s. 55,815,605.  T he   unde r - f un d in g   a ff e c t e d   t h e   pla n ne d   a c t i v i t i e s of the County Executive   an d   may have  i m pa c t e d   nega t i v el y   o n s e rv i ce   de l i v e ry   t o   t h e   public.  My opinion is not   modified in respect of this matter.  Other Matter  995.   Unresolved Prior Year matters  In the audit report of the previous year, several issues were raised under Report on  Financial Statements and Report on Lawfulness and Effectiveness in the Use of Public  Resource as listed at the end of this report.   However, the Management has not resolved  the issues or given any explanation for the delay in resolving the twenty eight (28) issues  as shown at the end of this report.  Other Information  996.   There were no material issues relating to Other Information.  REPORT   ON   LAWFULNESS   AND   EFFECTIVENESS   IN   THE   USE   OF   PUBLIC  RESOURCES  Basis for Conclusion  997.   Long Outstanding Trade and Other Payables  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 19 to the financial statements  reflects a balance of Kshs.2,514,353,9 24 in respect of trade and other payables.   Included  in the balance are trade payables amounting to Kshs.1,723,816,990, out which an amount  of Kshs.61,390,555 relates to long outstanding balances that have remained unpaid for  periods between two (2) and   eight (8) years from 2017 to 2023 . Management did not  explain why the long outstanding trade payables had not been paid as a first charge. This  was contrary to Section 41 (2) of the Public Finance Management (County Governments)

471  Regulations, 2015 which pro vides that debt service payments shall be a first charge on  the County Revenue Fund and the Accounting Officer shall ensure this is done to the  extent possible that the County Government does not default on debt obligations.  In the circumstances, Manageme nt was in breach of the law.  998.   Non - Compliance with the Law on Staff Ethnic Composition  Review of personnel records revealed that the County Executive had six thousand, six  hundred and eighty - eight (6,688) employees out of whom six thousand, two hundred an d  ninety - one (6,291) members of staff or 94% were from the same ethnic community. This  was contrary to Section 7(1) and (2) of the National Cohesion and Integration Act, 2008  which requires that all public offices shall seek to represent the diversity of t he people of  Kenya in employment of staff and that no public institution shall have more than one - third  of its staff establishment from the same ethnic community.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  999.   Non - Compliance with the Persons   with Disabilities Act, 2025  Review of personnel records revealed that out of six thousand, six hundred and eighty -  eight (6,688) employees, only ninety - four (94) or 1% of the positions in the County  Executive were held by persons with   disabilities. This was contrary to Section 5(1)(e) of  the Persons with Disabilities Act, 2025 which provides that every County Government  shall promote the inclusion of persons with disabilities in the County public service by  putting in place measures to   ensure that at least five per centum of the employment  positions are filled by persons with disabilities.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1000.   Non - Compliance with Fiscal Responsibility Principles on Wages  The statement of financial   performance reflects revenue totalling Kshs. 13,708,952,618  and   compensation   of   employees’   payments   totalling   Kshs.6,671,517,508 .   The  compensation of employees’ payments constitutes forty - nine per cent (49%) of the total  revenue of the County Executive for   the year under review. This was contrary to  Regulation   25(1)(b)   of   the   Public   Finance   Management   (County   Governments)  Regulations, 2015 which provides that the employees costs should not exceed 35% of  the County Executive total revenue.  In the circumstan ces, Management was in breach of the law.  1001.   Non - Compliance with the One - Third Rule of the Basic Salary  Review of the personnel records revealed that four hundred and sixty - seven (467)  employees had net pay that was less than one - third of their respective basic salaries.  This was   contrary to Section 19(3) of the Employment Act, 2007 which stipulates that

472  wit hout prejudice to any right of recovery of any debt due and notwithstanding the  provisions of any other written law, the total amount of all deductions made by an  employer from the wages of his employee at any one time shall not exceed two - thirds of  such w ages.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1002.   Irregularities in Procurement for Cleaning and Garbage Collection Services  The County Executive incurred an expenditure of Kshs.35,475,246 for provision of  cleaning and garbage collection   services across various County Municipalities. Review  of procurement files revealed that Management entered into framework contracts with  various firms for provision of the services between 1 January, 2023 and 3 April, 2023 with  total contract amounting to   Kshs.405,512,329 for periods between two (2) and three (3)  years. However, tender advertisement, bid documents and other procurement documents  revealed that Management did not specify intention to establish a framework agreement  and the contract period in   relation to the procurement of the services.  This was contrary to Regulation 102 (1) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal  Regulations, 2020 which provides that a procuring entity may enter into a framework  agreement through open tender using an   invitation to tender which shall specify that the  procuring entity intends to establish a framework agreement, the number of suppliers or  contractors which shall not be less than seven alternative vendors and the duration of the  framework agreement which s hall not exceed three years.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1003.   Non - Compliance with the Provisions of the Public Finance Management  Regulations, 2022  The Public Finance Management (Public Investment Management) Regulations, 2022,  came to effect in the financial year 2024/2025 for all County Governments which required  implementation   and   appointment   of   various   committees,   project   implementation  oversights , ensure that all contracts signed by the procuring entities are uploaded in the  Public Investment Management Information System, prepare project completion reports  and submit them to the County Treasury in standard templates.  However, no documentary evi dence was provided for audit on implementation of these  regulations.   Management did not provide explanations for the failure to implement the  regulations as provided for in the Ninth Schedule on implementation of Public Finance  Management (Public Investme nt Management) Regulations, 2022.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the regulations.

473  1004.   Irregular   Payment   of Subscriptions  Review of records revealed that County Executive incurred an expenditure amounting to  Kshs.3,000,000 paid to the Co uncil of Governors for devolution conference registration  expenses. However, the expenditure incurred had not been provided for in the annual  budget and estimates for the year under review. This was contrary to Section 37 of  Intergovernmental Relations Act , 2012 which provides that the operational expenses in  respect of the structures and institutions established in the Act shall be provided for in the  annual estimates of the revenue and expenditure of the National Government to cater for  the Summit, the Co uncil of County Governors, the Technical Committee, Secretariat and  the sectoral working group established by the Technical Committee and the sectoral  working groups established by the Council.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1005.   Irregular   Expenditure on Other Government Entities Projects  The County Executive awarded a contract to a local construction company for the design  and supervision of the construction of an office block and chambers for the Kakamega  County Assembly at a contract sum of Kshs.67,272,728. The County Executive paid  cons ultancy fees amounting to Kshs.24,000,000 to the contractor during the year under  review. However, Management did not provide explanation and supporting documents  authorizing the County Executive to procure the services on behalf of the County  Assembly.  Further,   the   County   Executive   entered   into   a   contract   for   the   construction   and  improvement of Mukumu Girls’ High School sports grounds at a contract price of  Kshs.5,037,060. However, the institution did not fall under the devolved unit but was fully  under   the regulation and control of the National Government.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1006.   Use of Asbestos for Roofing of Residential Houses  Review of the County Executive records revealed that the County Executive owned one  hundred and forty - four (144) residential houses. Audit inspection revealed that one  hundred and twenty - four (124) houses were roofed with asbestos and Management did  not pr ovide a plan to replace the roofs. This was contrary to the Government of Kenya  ban on the use of asbestos in the year 2006 due to its carcinogenic health risks.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law and the failure to replace the  asb estos roofs raises serious environmental and health hazard to the public.  1007.   Non - Compliance   with   the   Law   on   Procurement   Reservations   for  Disadvantaged Groups  The County Executive planned to procure works, goods and services for the year under  review   totall ing   Kshs.3,784,315,989.   Management   set   aside   an   amount   of  Kshs.907,935,830 or twenty four percent (24%) of the planned procurement expenditure

474  for disadvantaged groups. This was contrary to Section 157(5) of the Public Procurement  and Asset Disposal Act, 2 015 which requires an Accounting Officer to reserve at least  thirty per cent to the disadvantaged groups in the procurement budget.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1008.   Un - Utilized Public Participation Web Portal  The County Execut ive entered into a contract for the development of an automated  County   public   participation   web   portal   on   28   March,   2024   at   a   contract   sum   of  Kshs.4,719,000   for   a   contract   period   of   six   (6)   months.   Review   of   the   project  implementation report and the portal   revealed that the project was completed and handed  over but had not been put to use to date. This was contrary to Section 149(1) of the Public  Finance Management Act, 2012 which provides that an Accounting Officer is accountable  for ensuring that the reso urces of the entity for which the officer is designated are used in  a way that is lawful and authorized and effective, efficient, economical and transparent.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1009.   Project   Implementation   Status  1009.1.   Department for Health Services  The Department for Health Services commenced to implement various projects some  dating back from the financial year 2021/2022 amounting to Kshs.7,002,023,807. Projects  amounting to Kshs.50,341,490 were completed and in use   in the year under audit,  projects amounting to Kshs.101,177,176 were completed but had not been put to use  with some dating back to the financial year 2021/2022, while projects amounting to  Kshs.6,850,505,141 had stalled with no ongoing works at the time   of audit. Review of the  project   implementation   status   further   revealed   that   out   of   the   expenditure  Kshs.7,002,023,807 on initiated projects, a total of Kshs.3,301,036,240 had been settled.  The   projects   were   at   various   stages   of   project   execution/completion   leaving   an  outstanding balance of Kshs.3,700,987,567 unpaid. Management, in the fiscal strategy  and plan did not indicate how the projects will be financed in the short and long - term. In  addition, prioritization of projects has not been clearly defined, w hich may lead to further  delays in project completion.  In the circumstances, value for money may not have been realized from the delayed  projects.  1009.2.   Proposed Construction of Maternity Block at Muhaka Health Centre  The Department for Health services awarde d a contract for the construction of maternity  block at Muhaka Health Center at a contract sum of Kshs.29,074,980 on 10 March, 2024.  The construction works were to be completed within twenty - four (24) months from the  contract signing date. However, field   inspection carried out on 26 June, 2025 revealed  that the project had stalled at the foundation level, trenches were dug and left open and

475  no works done by the contractor for a period exceeding one year. The contractor was not  on site at the time of audit.   Review of contract file revealed that the County Attorney had  on 17 October, 2024 advised the Health Services Department to terminate the contract  and   provided   grounds   and   procedure   of   termination.   No   action   in   relation   to  recommendation by the County Att orney on contract termination by the Department has  been implemented.  In the circumstances, value for money may not have been realized from the project.  1009.3.   Delayed   Completion of the Level 4 Hospital at Shamakhubu, Shinyalu  Sub -   County  The   Department   for   He alth   Services   awarded   a   contract   for   the   construction   of  Shamakhubu Level 4 Hospital in Shinyalu   Sub - County   at a revised contract sum of  Kshs.229,139,694.   The   contractor   received   an   advance   payment   amounting   to  Kshs.40,000,000 as per Certificate No.1, which was to be recovered progressively from  the subsequent certified works. Review of the advance recovery rev ealed that an amount  of Kshs.23,474,301 was recovered from Certificates numbers 3, 4 and 5. No further  recoveries   were   made   from   Certificates numbers   6   to   10   as required   leaving   an  outstanding balance of Kshs.16,525,699 that remained unaccounted for to dat e. Field  verification carried out on 30 June, 2025 revealed that the project was 85% complete and  the contractor had abandoned the site in the year 2021, with both internal and external  works finishing incomplete.  In the circumstances, value for money may   not have been realized from the delayed  project.  1009.4.   Delayed Construction of Open - air Markets  The Department for Trade awarded contracts to six (6) contractors on 24 March, 2022 for  construction of six (6) open air markets across various trading centers wi thin the County  at a total contract sum of Kshs.173,465,242. The contracts specified a c ompletion   period  of one hundred and four (104) weeks from the date of signing. However, as at the time of  audit, an amount of Kshs.52,186,215 or 30% of the total contra ct sum had already been  paid to the contractors with the contractual period having already lapsed and the overall  projects implementation at approximately 30% and completion of the   projects was behind  schedule by approximately one (1) year and six (6) mont hs.  In the circumstances, value for money for the expenditure of Kshs.52,186,215 spent on  the projects could not be confirmed.  1009.5.   Delayed   Completion   of   Augmentation   of   Navakholo   Water   Supply  Project  The   Department   for Water,   Environment,   Natural   Resources   and   Climate   Change  awarded a contract on 21 March, 2022 for the augmentation of Navakholo water supply

476  project in Navakholo Sub - county at a contract sum of Kshs.4,906,225. The augmentation  works were   to be completed within twenty - four (24) weeks from the date of contract  signing. At the time of the audit, the contractor had been paid a sum of Kshs.2,745,836  or 56% of the total contract sum. Field inspection conducted on 13 June, 2025 revealed  that the   project was incomplete and the contractor was not on site and a number of key  activities including plastering of water tank, construction of the sanitation facility, fencing  of borehole and completion of the solar site had not been undertaken.  In the ci rcumstances, value for money for the expenditure of Kshs.2,745,836 incurred on  the project could not be confirmed.  1009.6.   Delayed Construction of Khabukoshe   -   Harambee Water Project  The   Department   for Water,   Environment,   Natural   Resources   and   Climate   Change  awa rded a contract for the construction of a water storage tank, booster and pump house  at a contract sum of Kshs.13,801,322 on 8 June, 2023. The construction works were to  be completed within six (6) months from the date of signing. Field inspection carried   out  on 13 June, 2025 revealed that the project was incomplete and the contractor was not on  site with key works including laying of water pipes, painting of the masonry tank and  construction of pump house yet to be done. Verification of payment details rev ealed that  no payment had been made to the contractor as at the time of audit.  In the circumstances, the delay in implementation of the project may impact negatively  on service delivery to the public.  1009.7.   Delayed Renovations   of County Government Houses in Ma lava  The County Executive awarded a contract for renovation works of ten (10) one - bedroom  self - contained   County   Government   houses   in   Malava   town   at   a   contract   sum   of  Kshs.9,075,675 with an expected completion date of 31 August, 2023. Review of the  Projec t Implementation Status Report and audit inspection conducted in May, 2025  revealed that the renovation works were at initial stage although the contractor was not  on site.  In the circumstances, the delay in implementation of the project may impact negati vely  on service delivery to the public.  1009.8.   Delayed   Upgrading   of   Mahiakalo -   Nyayo   Tea   Zone - Shikulu   Market  Roads  The Department for Roads, Public Works and Energy awarded a contract for the upgrade  to bitumen standards of the Mahiakalo - Nyayo Tea Zone - Shikul u Market Road at a  contract sum of Kshs.468,229,351. The works were to commence on 10 January, 2024  for twenty - four (24) months and was expected to be completed by 10 December, 2025.  Physical inspection conducted in June, 2025, revealed that the project wa s about 60%  complete with six (6) months to completion period and the project was running behind

477  schedule which may result in delays as the contractor was not on site as at the time of  audit.  In the circumstances, the delay in project   implementation may impact negatively on  service delivery to the public.  1009.9.   Delayed   Upgrade   to   Bitumen   Standard   of   Mumias   -   Matawa   –  Indangalasia Road  The Department for Roads, Public Works and Energy awarded a contract for the upgrade  to bitumen standards o f the Mumias   -   Matawa   -   Indangalasia Road at a contract sum of  Kshs.599,527,614. The works were to commence on 12 January, 2024 for twenty - four  (24) months and was expected to be completed by 12 December, 2025. Physical  inspection carried out in June, 2025 , revealed that the project was only about 40%  complete despite less than six (6) months remaining to completion date.  Further, the contractor was not on site as at the time of audit. The project may have stalled  due to non - payment of certified works and   may lead to project completion delays and  possible cost escalation to complete the works.  In the circumstances, the delay in implementation of the project may impact negatively  on service delivery to the public.  1009.10.   Construction of a Box Culvert at Tamanon i  The County Executive entered into a contract for the construction of a box culvert and  approaches (1.5Km) at Tamanoni at a contract sum of Kshs.7,888,428. The works were  scheduled to commence on 27 May, 2024 for a duration of six (6) months with expect ed  completion date of 28 November, 2024. However, physical inspection conducted in June,  2025, revealed that the project was about 60% complete with project completion time  delayed by seven (7) months. The delays in implementation of the project may lead t o  cost escalation.  In the circumstances, value for money for the project could not be confirmed.  1009.11.   Poor Construction of Drainage Structures and Improvement of Roads  The Department for Public Works, Roads, Transport and Energy awarded contracts for  maintenance of Sichirai P.A.G   -   Munyulu Junction - Ebwambwa Road (3KM) at a contract  sum of Kshs.4,711,278, Daisy Junction   -   Iwatingu loops Roads (1.4KM) at a contract sum  of   Kshs.2,117,551   and   Mayoni   -   Weteba   Road   (2.2KM)   at   a   contract   sum   of  Kshs.2,961,700. The project duration was scheduled for six (6) months period from 01  February, 2024 to 02 July, 2024 with all the payments fully made during the year under  review. However , it was observed that the drainage works was poorly done with no road  culverts installed.   As a result, in some road sections of the road were washed away  shortly after project completion.

478  In the circumstances, value for money for the expenditure of Ksh s.9,790,529 incurred on  the road projects could not be confirmed.  1009.12.   Stalled Education Projects  Review of the Department for Education Project Implementation Status Reports and audit  inspections carried out on 23   June, 2025 revealed that ten (10) projects awarded in the  previous two (2) financial years at a total contract sum of Kshs. 77,193,724   were stalled  and contractors were not on site. Further, eighteen (18) Early Childhood Education  Development (ECDE) classro om projects awarded between 15 December, 2021 and 25  January, 2024 with a contract sum of Kshs. 85,627,664   were incomplete and their  respective contracts had lapsed on various dates.  In the circumstances, value for money for the stalled and incomplete pro jects could not  be confirmed.  1009.13.   Overpayment on the Construction of Kipkaren Stock Ring  The County Executive awarded a contract for the construction of Kipkaren Stock Ring on  19   October, 2023 at a contract sum of Kshs.14,622,461 with a contract period of si xteen  (16) weeks from the commencement date. Review of the project file and physical  inspection   out   on   25   June,   2025   revealed   that   out   of   the   total   contract   sum   of  Kshs.14,622,461, an amount of Kshs.7,104,164 or 49% of the contract value had already  been a pproved for payment to the contractor. This was more than actual progress, which  was assessed at only 10% completion. The variance resulted in an overpayment of  Kshs.5,549,926. Further, despite the overpayment, the contractor was not on site as at  the time   of audit and the contract period had already lapsed.  In the circumstances, value for money for the expenditure incurred of Kshs.7,104,169 on  the project could not be confirmed.  1009.14.   Overpayment of Shiatsala Market Project  The   Department   for   Trade,   Industria lization   and   Tourism   awarded   a   contract   on  24 March, 2022 to construct an open - air market at a contract sum of Kshs.38,005,230.  Review of the project bill of quantities revealed the estimated cost to the slab/ sub -  structure level amounted   to Kshs.4,850,370.   However, the contractor had been paid a  total sum of Kshs.11,499,203 resulting in an overpayment of Kshs.6,648,833 for works  that were not done. The contractor subsequently abandoned the site with the contract  period having long lapsed   and the project stalled at the slab/sub - structure level.  In the circumstances, value for money for the expenditure of Kshs.11,499,204 incurred  on the project could not be confirmed.  1009.15.   Stalled Kakamega County Aggregation and Industrial Park Project  The Department for Trade, Industrialization and Tourism entered into a two (2) year  contract for the construction of County Aggregation and Industrial Park at a contract sum

479  of Kshs.481,255,920 on 20 September, 2023. The contractor raised an invoice for  pa yment totalling Kshs.140,004,640 on 22 December, 2023 against an interim payment  certificate   for   works   completed   and   approved   by   the   Inspection   and   Acceptance  Committee. Field inspection carried out on 24   June, 2025 revealed that the project had  stalled due to non - payment for the certified works.  In the circumstances,   the   value for money for the expenditure of Kshs.140,004,640 on  the project could not be confirmed.  1010.   Non - Remittance of Statutory Deductions  Review of the payroll records provided r evealed that County Executive made statutory  deductions in relation LAPFUND, LAPTRUST, Housing Levy and Higher Education  Loans   Board   (HELB)   during   the   year   amounting   to   Kshs.675,901,362.   However,  Management did not provide evidence to confirm remittance of   the deductions to various  statutory bodies. This was contrary to Section 19(4) of the Employment Act, 2007 which  requires that an employer who deducts an amount from an employee’s remuneration  shall   pay   the   amount   deducted   in   accordance   with   the   time   peri od   and   other  requirements specified in the law, agreement court order or arbitration as the case may  be the County Executive risks incurring avoidable costs in respect of interest and  penalties.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1011.   Non - Compliance with the Facilities Improvement Financing Act, 2023  The Department for Health through Kakamega County Health Services Fund collected an  amount of Kshs.873,502,133 from sixteen (16) health facilities and deposited the amount  into a commerc ial bank account held at the Department for Health. However, the  Department remitted an amount of Kshs.788,383,867 to sixteen (16) health facilities and  retained a balance of Kshs.85,118,266. This was contrary to Section 5(1) and (2) of the  Facilities Impr ovement Financing Act, 2023 which provides that there shall be retention  of all monies raised or received by, or on behalf of all public health facilities and there  shall be opened a facility   improvement   financing account for each public health facility  in to which all monies shall be paid into.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1012.   Delay in the Winding up of Kakamega County Public Funds  1012.1.   Kakamega County Agricultural Input Fund  Review of the closure of the Kakamega County Agricultural Input Fund revealed that the  County Assembly Committee for Finance and Economic Planning issued a report dated  27 June, 2024, recommending the winding up of the Fund since it was unsustainable as  pe r the requirement of the Public Finance Management Act, 2012. The last audited

480  financial statements of the Fund for the year ended 30 June, 2024 indicated a cash and  cash equivalents balance of Kshs.859,364 held in three (3) commercial bank accounts  and cu rrent portion of long - term receivables from exchange transactions balance of  Kshs.7,816,487.  Further, the County Executive Committee Member for Finance, Economic Planning and  ICT   vide   letter   ref   CGK/TPR/AD/1/57/VOL.II/48   dated   11   July,   2024   instructed   a  c ommercial bank to close one account and transfer the funds to Kakamega County  Revenue Collection Account. However, there were no documentary evidence that the  three   bank   accounts   were   closed   and   funds   transferred   to   the   County   Revenue  F und. Further, the documentary evidence for the transfer of receivables to County  Executive   of   Kakamega   was   not   provided   for   audit   review.   This   was   contrary   to  Regulation 19 (a) and (c) of the Kakamega County Agricultural Input Fund Amendment  Regulations, 2 019 which requires upon winding up of the Fund the administrator of the  Fund to pay any amount remaining in the Fund into the County Exchequer Account; and  that all assets of the Fund shall be taken over by the County Government.  In addition, there was n o documentary evidence for closure of the Fund since the final  report after winding up the Fund was not submitted to the Auditor - General for audit and  the County Assembly as required.  1012.2.   Kakamega County Maternal Child Health and Family Planning Fund  Rev iew of the closure of the Kakamega County Maternal Child Health and Family  Planning Fund revealed that the Kakamega County Maternal Child Health and Family  Planning Act, 2017 (Revised 2021) did not contain the procedure for winding - up the Fund.  This was   co ntrary to Regulation   198 of   the   Public Finance   Management   (County  Governments) Regulations, 2015, which requires that the County Executive Committee  Member shall provide for the management, operation and winding up procedure in the  guidelines for establish ing each Fund which shall be in accordance with the Act and the  Regulations.  Further, the County Assembly Committee for Finance and Economic Planning report  dated 25 June, 2024 recommended the winding - up of the Fund by closure of the financial  year 2023/ 2024 since it was not a going concern. The last audited financial statements of  the Fund for the financial year ended 30 June, 2024 reflected cash and cash equivalents  balance of Kshs.1,794,969 held in a commercial bank, accounts receivables balance of  Ksh s.362,800, and property, plant and equipment balance of Kshs.3,564,469. However,  there was no documentary evidence provided for audit review to confirm that cash was  transferred to the County Revenue Fund and assets transferred to County Executive of  Kakam ega. This was contrary to Section 116 (6) (a) and (b) of the Public Finance  Management Act, 2012 which requires that on the winding up of a County public fund, the  administrator of the fund shall pay any amount remaining in the fund into the County  Exchequ er Account; and the County Executive Committee Member for finance shall, with  the approval of the County Assembly, pay any deficit in the fund from the County  Exchequer Account.

481  In addition, there was no documentary evidence for closure of the Fund since   the final  report after winding up the Fund, was not submitted to the Auditor - General for audit and  the County Assembly as required.  1012.3.   Kakamega County Small Scale Trade Development Fund  The Kakamega County Small Scale Trade Development Fund was established   in 2015  under the Small - Scale Trade Regulations, 2015 to support Small Scale Traders through  issuance of low interest loans. The County Assembly Committee for Finance and  Economic Planning report dated 5 August, 2024 recommended the winding up of the  Fund   since it was dormant and was not receiving transfers from the county executive,  and the County Treasury to write - off non recovered loans totalling Kshs.40,645,683 as at  31 March, 2024 in accordance with Section 150 of the Public Finance Management Act,  20 12. However, there was no documentation to confirm that the outstanding loans  balance was irrecoverable and due for written - off as required by Regulation 150 (1) and  (2) of the Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015, which  require s that an Accounting Officer may only write off losses owed to the state if he or  she is satisfied that all reasonable steps have been taken to recover the loss and the loss  is irrecoverable; or he or she is convinced that recovery of the losses would be  u neconomical; and it would be to the advantage of the County Government entity to effect  a settlement of its claim or to waive the claim. Further, an Accounting Officer shall ensure  that all losses written off are done in accordance with the Act, the Regula tions or any  other relevant legislation.  Further, the last audited financial statements of the Fund for the financial year ended 30  June, 2024 indicated a cash and cash equivalents balance of Kshs.354,482, and long -  term receivables balance of Kshs.40,531, 045. However, there was no indication that the  monies were transferred to the County Revenue Fund as required. This was contrary to  Regulation 22(a) of the Kakamega County Small Scale Trade Development Fund  Regulations, 2017 which provides that the County   Executive Member may wind up the  Fund with the approval of the County Assembly and upon winding - up, the administrator  shall pay any amount remaining in the Fund into the County Exchequer Account.  In addition, there was no documentary evidence for closure   of the Fund since the final  report after winding up the Fund was not submitted to the Auditor - General and the County  Assembly as required. Additionally, the financial statements for the period in existence  before closure were not submitted for audit.  The   winding of the above three (3) Funds was contrary to Regulation 199 (2) of the Public  Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 on winding up of a  County Public Fund which requires that the final report after winding up the Fund be  submitt ed to the Auditor - General for audit and the County Assembly.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

482  REPORT ON EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROLS, RISK MANAGEMENT  AND GOVERNANCE  Basis for Conclusion  1013.   Internal Control   Weaknesses in Information Communication Technology  Environment  Review   of   the   County   Executive’s   Information   Communication   Technology   (ICT)  environment revealed that the County Executive does not have an approved ICT policy  and a Strategic Plan to   guide governance, management and development of its ICT  resources. Further, during the year under review, there was no ICT Steering Committee  to assist in the development of ICT policy framework to enable the County realize its long -  term ICT strategic goal s.  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of the County Executive’s ICT internal control  mechanisms could not be confirmed. 484  COUNTY EXECUTIVE OF VIHIGA   –   NO.38  REPORT ON THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS  Basis for Qualified   Opinion  1014.   Failure to Capitalize Property, Plant and Equipment  The   statement   of   financial   performance   statements   reflects   an   amount   of  Kshs.1,432,268,408 in respect of use of goods and service s as disclosed in Note 8 to the  financial statements. Included in the expenditure is an amount of Kshs . 307,636,974  incurred on rehabilitation of civil works and   an amount of Kshs . 303 ,085,6 35 incurred on  constructions of civil works, all totalling Kshs.610,722 ,609.   However, review of the  financial statements revealed that the two (2) expenditure items were not capitalized in  accordance with the IPSAS 33 on transition to Accrual Basis of Acco unting.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the expenditure amounting to  Kshs.610,722,609 included in the use of goods and services and not capitalized could  not be confirmed.  1015.   Unsupported Software License Renewal  The   statement   of   fin ancial   performance   statements   reflects   an   amount   of  Kshs.1,432,268,408 in respect of use of goods and services as disclosed in Note 8 to the  financial statements. Included in the amount was an expenditure of Kshs.33,974,444 in  relation   to   office   and   genera l   supplies   and   services   out   of   which,   a   balance   of  Kshs.3,200,040 was incurred on software license renewal. However, key supporting  documents   such   as   needs   assessment   report,   activation   records   or   license   user  allocation to confirm which users or machines   received the secondary licenses, delivery  reports/service completion certificate to confirm that the services were received, tested  and accepted and evidence of system use or outputs tied to the renewed licenses to show  that the system was in active use an d valid contract were not provided for audit.  Further, there was no approval by the Accounting Officer for use of the direct procurement  method and documentary evidence to indicate that Management reported the direct  procurement to the Authority within fou rteen (14) days after the notification of the award  of the contract since the value exceeded Kshs.500,000 threshold.  In the circumstances, the accuracy, completeness and regularity of the   expenditure on  license renewal amounting to Kshs.3,200,040 could n ot be confirmed.  1016.   Unconfirmed Depreciation and Amortization Expense s  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 10 to the financial  statements reflects an amount of Kshs.15,898,111 in respect of depreciation of property,  plant and equipment and amortization of the intangible assets. However, the depreci ation  charge and amortization were based on a draft policy that was yet to be approved by the

485  County Assembly and Management has not given reasons for the delay in approval of  the Policy.  In   the   circumstances,   the   accuracy   and   completeness   of   the   deprecia tion   and  amortization amount of Kshs.15,898,111 could not be confirmed.  1017.   Receivables from Non - Exchange Transactions  The statement of financial position reflects a balance of Kshs.10,865,170 in respect of  receivables from non - exchange transactions as disclo sed in Note 13 to the financial  statements. However, the following unsatisfactory matters were observed.  1017.1.   Unsupported and Long Outstanding Salary Advances  Included in the balance are salary advances amounting to Kshs.1,865,170 out of which  an amount of Ks hs.1,775,438 were advances made in the years 2015 and 2017 to ten  (10) members of staff. The staff members included four (4) former staff of the County  Executive, one (1) current member of staff, one (1) former deceased member of staff,  three (3) current s itting MCAs and one (1) former Member of County Assembly (MCA).  Management explained that a recovery of Kshs.85,168 from two (2) officers had been  made. However, no evidence in form of pay slips was provided for audit. Further, no  reconciliation was provid ed for audit indicating the movement of the opening balance of  Kshs.1,950,338 and the closing balance of Kshs.1,865,170.  1017.2.   Recoverability of Amount Due from the County Assembly  Included in the balance is an amount of Kshs.9,000,000 in respect of transfers due from  the County Assembly. However, review of receivables’ records revealed that the County  Executive   transferred   an   amount   of   Kshs.38,000,000   to   the   County   Assembly   on  25   February,   2021   and   Kshs.6,000,000   on   23   November,   2021   all   totalling  Kshs.44,000,000, in respect of funds paid from deposit and retention account to bridge a  shortfall in the County Assembly’s Car Loan and Mortgage Account. However, an amount  o f Kshs.35,000,000 had been refunded as at 30 June, 2025 leaving a balance of  Kshs.9,000,000. Further, Management did not make any provision for bad and doubtful  debts in the financial statements.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the   r eceivables from non -  exchange transactions   balance of Kshs. 10,865,170   could not be confirmed.  Emphasis of Matter  1018.   Budgetary Control and Performance  The statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts reflects final receipts budget  and   actual   on   comparable   basis   amounts   of   Kshs.6,390,648,472   and  Kshs.5,751,275,738 respectively, resulting in under - funding of Kshs.639,372,734 or 10%  of the budget. H owever, the County Executive spent an amount of Kshs.5,459,386,518

486  against   actual   receipts   of   Kshs.5,751,275,738   resulting   in   under - absorption   of  Kshs.291,889,220.  The under - funding affected the planned activities of the County Executive and may have  imp acted negatively on service delivery to the public.  My opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.  Other Matter  1019.   Unresolved Prior Year Matters  In the previous year’s audit report, several issues were raised under the Report on  Financial Statements, Lawfulness and Effectiveness in Use of Public Resources, and  Effectiveness of Internal Controls, Risk Management and Governance. Review of the  status   during the audit of the   County Executive   in the current year revealed that thirty - two  (32) matters listed at the end of this report remained unresolved as at 30 June, 2025.  Other Information  1020.   There were no material issues relating to Other Information.  REPORT   ON   LAWFULNESS   AND   EFFECTIVENESS   IN   THE   USE   OF   PUBLIC  RESOURCES  Basis for Conclusion  1021.   Non - Compliance with the Law on   Fiscal Responsibility Principles on Wages  The County Executive incurred   employees’ costs amounting to   Kshs.2,790,128,784   or  53% of the total receipts amount of Kshs.5,298,479,710 which exceeded the set limit of  thirty - five percent (35%). This was   contrary to Regulation 25(1)(a) and (b) of the Public  Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which requires that the  County Executive Committee Member with the approval of the County Assembly shall set  a limit on the County Government's   expenditure on wages and benefits for its public  officers pursuant to Section 107(2) of the Act and the limit set under paragraph (a) above,  shall not exceed thirty - five percent (35%) of the County Government's total revenue.  In the circumstances, Manageme nt was in breach of the law.  1022.   Non - Compliance with the Law on Staff Ethnic Diversity  The total number of employees during the year was three thousand, two hundred and  seventy - two (3,272), out of which three thousand and eight - nine (3,089) or 94% of the  to tal number were from the dominant ethnic community in the County. This was contrary  to Section 7(1) and (2) of the National Cohesion and Integration Act, 2008 which states  that, “all public offices shall seek to represent the diversity of the people of Ken ya in

487  employment of staff and that no public institution shall have more than one third of its staff  establishment from the same ethnic community”.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1023.   Lack of Annual Recruitment Plan  The County E xecutive recruited two hundred and ninety - eight (298) officers in the year  under   review.   However,   the   County   Public   Service   Board   did   not   have   Annual  Recruitment Plan to guide the recruitments. Further, no evidence was provided to confirm  that budgetary av ailability was sought before recruitments were made. This was contrary  to   Section 59(1) (g) of the County Governments Act ,   2012   which requires the County  Public Service Board of a County to facilitate the development of coherent, integrated  human resource planning and budgeting for personnel emoluments in the County.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1024.   Non - Compliance with the One - Third Rule on Basic Salary  Review of the staff payroll for the month of June, 2025, revealed that the net salaries for  fifty - six (56) officers were less than one third of their respective basic salaries.   This was  contrary to   Section 19(3) of the Employment Act, 2007 which stipulates that without  prejudice to any right of recovery of any debt due and notwithstanding the provisions of  any other written law, the total amount of all deductions made by an employer from the  wages of   his employee at any one time shall not exceed two - thirds of such wages.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1025.   Non - Adherence to Climate Change and Financing Requirements  Review of the Climate Change and Financing of the County Execu tive for the year under  review   revealed   the following   unsatisfactory matters:  (i)   There was inadequate Integration of Climate Change Action Plan into County  Strategies as most Departments did not capture environmental sustainability or  green economy clearly as required. Further, the County Executive lacked a  comprehensive Climate Risk R egister   and a fully functional warning system   across  departments despite having a participatory climate risk assessment report. The  risk   register   would   enable   the   County   to   have   real - time,   accessible   and  community - responsive early warning system.  (ii)   There wa s no   clear value for money metrices on climate change. No   documented  cost benefit analysis or benchmarking report were provided for audit to determine  the economic, efficiency or environmental effectiveness of the projects undertaken  out of the total amoun t of Kshs.253,700,000 allocated in the budget.   Further, there  was   lack   of   Greenhouse   Gas   Emissions   (GHG)   Tracking   and   Adaptation

488  Outcomes Reporting System   and Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV)  systems   hence non - compliance with national and globa l obligations.  (iii)   There   was   no   evidence   of   sustainability   measures,   maintenance   budgets,  monitoring and evaluation post funding of the completed projects or institutional  frameworks to support continued functionality after the end of initial funding.  (iv)   There was no evidence of benefit - sharing agreements or community development  contracts, particularly for projects situated on community or public land that is, in  the case of carbon - related or natural resource - based interventions — such as  afforestation,   ref orestation,   or   water   conservation   structures   there   was   no  Community Development Agreements (CDAs) provided for audit, as required  under the Climate Change (Carbon Markets) Regulations, 2024.   Further,   there  were no monitoring tools or mechanisms to track wh ether agreed - upon project  benefits   such   as water   access,   improved ecosystems,   or livelihood   support  actually reached the targeted beneficiaries or communities .  (v)   Five (5)   project s   out of the sixteen   (16) climate - related projects with potential  environmental   impacts   such   as   irrigation   infrastructure   lacked   National  Environment   Management   Authority   (NEMA)   licenses   and   certificates.  Additionally, there were delayed exchequer disbursements hence the Fund’s  activities as planned in the Annual Work Plan were not c arried out as per the Paris  Agreement. This points to the   risk that the County Executive will not achieve its  targets as highlighted in the   Vihiga   County Climate Change Action Plan 202 3 -  2027. Further, this would have a negative effect on the Country’s abil ity to attain  the Sustainable Development Goal Number 13 on Climate Action.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1026.   Delayed Construction of Hospital Plaza  Review of procurement records provided for audit revealed that the County Executive  entered into an agreement with a firm for the construction of Hospital Plaza and Referral  Hospital at a contract sum of Kshs.395,172,568 on May, 2021.The project was to be  completed within a period of three (3) years. The project was for construction of a six (6)  floor Hospital Plaza from foundation to completion including installation of two (2)   lifts,  terrazzo on ramp and stairs, installation of solar water piping system,   gypsum ceiling,  aluminum   windows and doors, nurse call system wiring and equipment’s, oxygen and  vacuum equipment, electrical and mechanical fittings, external works including laying of  cabro at parking, generator installation, general painting works, flo or tiling and roofing and  concrete gutters.  The project status report indicated that the total works certified to date amounted to  Kshs.223,271,130, representing 56% of total cost as per interim payment certificate  no.10.   However, th e contract agreement had already expired in May, 2024 and there  was no evidence of request for renewal from the contractor or availability of a current  contract. Hence the contractor was in breach of the contract. The last site meeting

489  by the Project Management Team was held in May, 2024, indicating that no other meeting  had been held since expiry of the contract agreement.  Further, physical inspection in the month of June, 2025 revealed that the main structure  had been done to complet ion including exterior painting works, roofing and concrete  gutters. The interior works were on - going and the contractor was on site doing installation  of the second lift, tiling was partly done from first floor to 6th floor, terrazzo done on ramp  and stai rs, water tanks installed, gypsum ceiling works ongoing and wiring ongoing and  painting and skimming was ongoing. However, some other works were yet to start  including, external works, mechanical fitting and generator installation.  In addition, the projec t was behind schedule with a total of thirteen (13) months having  elapsed from the completion date of May, 2024. The   delay in completion of the project  increases the risk of cost escalation.  In the circumstances, value for money for the expenditure of Kshs.223,271,130 already  incurred on the project and full completion could not be confirmed.  1027.   Delay in Construction of County Aggregation and Industrial Park  The Department for Commerce, Tourism   and Cooperatives awarded a contract to a  company   at   a   contract   sum   of   Kshs.496,028,151   for   the   construction   of   County  Aggregation   and   Industrial   Park   as   indicated   on   the   letter   of   award   dated  23 August, 2023. The projec t was to be completed within nine (9)   months;   effective  26 September, 2023 as indicated in the contract agreement dated 29 September, 2023.  However, the following unsatisfactory matters were observed:  (i)   There was no communication from the Project M anagement Team to the  contractor on non - performance of the contract as required by the agreement  signed on 29 September, 2023.  (ii)   The contractor provided an updated performance bond dated 25 March, 2025  expiring on 26 March, 2027 from an insurance agency whi ch Management had  not confirmed its authenticity.  (iii)   A total of Kshs.52,038,575 had been paid to the contractor being valuation of  three (3) certificates.  However, physical inspection carried out in June, 2025 revealed that the contractor was  not actively o n site as the materials on site did not indicate any major works ongoing  hence the project had stalled. Further, the steel framework had been done on two (2)  warehouses and walling done a quarter way on two (2) walls only. In addition, the  foundation wall   had been done on two (2) warehouses awaiting framework installation.  The other warehouse trenches had been dug out but no works had been done as they  had started filling up.

490  In   the   circumstances,   value   for   money   for   the   expenditure   of   Kshs.52,038,575  on the construction of the County Aggregation and Industrial Park could not be confirmed.  1028.   Unsatisfactory Construction of Bumira   Early Childhood Development  Education   Classroom  The Department for Education and Vocational Training awarded a contract for the  construction of Bumira Early Childhood Development Education (ECDE) Classroom at a  contract sum of Kshs.1,775,752 on 21 Novemb er, 2024 for a period of three (3) months.  The contract was for construction of the main structure from foundation, walling, roofing,  plastering and general painting works. Physical inspection of the project carried out in  June, 2025 revealed that the cont ractor had already completed the required works as per  the Bill of quantities. However, the contractor did not use the recommended natural  stones for walling and instead mixed them with substandard molded soil that had already  started peeling off two (2) m onths after completion of the project and the floor had visible  cracks even before the project was put to use, an indication that the works done were  sub - standard.  In the circumstances, value for money incurred on the construction of the classrooms  could   not be confirmed.  1029.   Inconsistency of Carriageways on Construction of Access Roads  The County Executive carried out several road   maintenance   projects within the County.  Physical inspection conducted in June, 2025 revealed that significant inconsistencies  co ncerning the width/carriageway of access roads were ranging between 3.0 to 3.5  meters. However, the Bills of Quantities (BQs) for roads did not specify carriageway width  which according to National Construction Authority (NCA) should be 4.5 meters.   This wa s  contrary to Regulation 149 (1)(a) and (b) of   the   Public Finance Management (County  Governments)   Regulations,   2015   which   provides   that   an   Accounting   Officer   is  accountable to the County Assembly for ensuring that the resources of the entity for which  the   officer is designated are used in a way that is lawful and authorized and effective,  efficient, economical and transparent.  In the circumstances,   Management was in breach of the law.  1030.   Hire of Road Maintenance Equipment  The County Executive awarded a tend er at a contract sum of Kshs.90,769,560 for hire of  four (4) tipper trucks, one excavator, motor grader and single drum roller respectively, a  renewable   one   (1)   year   contract.   The   contract   agreement   was   signed   on  23 December, 2024 and an amount of Kshs.11,346,195 had been paid to the contractor  as at the time of audit.  The Department for Transport and Infrastructure purchases murram from various quarry  points from which the hired tracks were loaded and taken to t he various roads under the  Programme. However, the following   unsatisfactory matters   were noted:

491  (i)   An approved work plan with specification of activities on roads done was not  provided for audit;  (ii)   The Department for Transport and Infrastructure did not   maintain registers both  at the quarry point (Emmaloba Quarry, Luanda South) and at the various roads.  In the absence of the registers, it was not possible to ascertain whether all  murram picked was utilized for the intended roads;  (iii)   The roads done under the   programme did not have sign boards indicating  required information such as client, supervising engineer and year of funding  and  (iv)   The hired equipment were not labelled with stickers for the County Executive  for identification.  This was contrary to   Regulat ion 149(1) of the Public Finance Management (County  Governments) Regulations 2015 which requires an Accounting Officer is accountable to  the County Assembly to ensure that the resources of the entity for which the officer is  designated are used in a way th at is lawful and authorized; and effective, efficient,  economical and transparent.  In the circumstances,   Management was in breach of the law.  1031.   Irregularities in the Registration of Persons with Disabilities and Approvals  of Tax Exemptions  R eview of files   for staff registered under Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) revealed that  files for thirty (30) members were incomplete as they lacked the necessary documentation  such as disabilities cards, KRA Tax Exemption Certificates and Medical Assessment  Reports. T his was contrary to Section 35(1)(a) of the Persons with Disabilities Act, 2025  which provides that   in order to facilitate access by persons with disabilities to the services  set out under this part, the Council shall register on a continuous basis   person with  disabilities, to whom it shall issue disabilities identification cards in such form as it may  determine.  In the circumstances,   Management was in breach of law.  1032.   Failure to Prepare and Submit Financial Sta tements for Sabatia   Level 4  Sub - County Hospital  The financial statements Sabatia Sub - County Hospital for the year ended 30 June, 2025  and prior years were not submitted to the Auditor - General as required. This was contrary  to Section 164(4)(a) of the Public Finance Manageme nt Act, 2012 and Section 47(1) of  the Public Audit Act, 2015 which provide that within three (3) months after the end of each  financial year, the accounting officer for an entity shall submit the entity’s financial  statements to the Auditor - General.

492  In t he circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1033.   Long Outstanding Trade and Other Payables Balance  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 16 to the financial statements  reflects a balance of Kshs.1,710,935,139 in respect of tr ade and other payables. The  balance   includes   trade   payables   amounting   to   Kshs.1,480,433,982   comprising   of  Kshs.973,405,663 or 65% for the previous financial years’ and Kshs.507,028,283 or 35%  for the year under review. However, the County Executive risks i ncurring additional losses  in form of interest and penalties arising from continued delay in the settlement of the  payables. Further, failure to settle debts during the year in which they relate distorts the  financial statements and adversely affects the b udgetary provisions for the subsequent  year as they form a first charge.   This was contrary to Regulation 41(2) of the Public  Finance Management (County Governments) Regulation, 2015, which requires that debt  service payments shall be a first c harge on the County Revenue Fund and the Accounting  Officer shall ensure this is done to the   extent   possible that the County Government does  not default on debt obligation.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  REPORT ON   EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROLS, RISK MANAGEMENT  AND GOVERNANCE  Basis for Conclusion  1034.   Weaknesses in Revenue Collection Management System  Review of procurement and payment records revealed that the County Executive had  made payments to a vendor to the level of 89% of the contract sum of Kshs.58,777,600  for the supply of a Revenue Automation System. However, review of the Revenue  Collection   M anagement   System   records and documents   revealed that key deliverables  such as full system automation, system handover, integration with other County systems  (such as the IFMIS, HRIS, HMIS, GIS, G - PAY) training of end - users and security  configuration   such a s   firewall installation remained incomplete. The vendor continues to  host   the   County's   revenue   data   on   their   cloud   infrastructure,   limiting   the   County  Executive’s control and ownership of its data.  Further,   the   earlier   technical   recommendations   such   as   the   implementation   of  multi - filter functionalities to allow the generation of detailed analytical reports across  sub - categories of revenue streams, has not been addressed by the service   provider.  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of the internal controls and reliability of the  Revenue Collection Management System could not be confirmed.  1035.   Lack of a Risk Management Policy  Review   of   the   internal   controls   of   the   County   Executive   revea led   that   the   Risk  Management Policy had   not been developed and there were no fraud prevention  mechanisms put in place. Further, Operational and Disaster Recovery Plans were also

493  not provided. This was contrary to Regulation 158(1) of the Public Finance Man agement  (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 that require the Accounting Officer to develop  risk management strategies, which include fraud prevention mechanism and a system of  risk management and internal control that builds robust business operations.  In the circumstances, Management’s ability to identify risks, rank them and allocate  adequate resources to mitigate them   could not be confirmed.  1036.   Lack of Follow - Ups on Internal Audit Recommendations  Review   of the County Executive’s Internal Audit Director ate   Reports   revealed that  follow - up on internal audit recommendations was not consistently conducted. As a result,  there was no assurance that Management action plans developed in response to audit  findings had been effectively implement ed.  In   the   circumstances,   the   effectiveness   of   assessment   of   internal   controls,   risk  management and governance could not be confirmed.
