495  COUNTY EXECUTIVE   OF BUNGOMA   –   NO.39  REPORT ON THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS  Basis for Qualified   Opinion  1037.   Unsupported   Property, Plant and Equipment Opening Balance  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 15 to the financial statements  reflects an opening balance as at 1 July, 2024 for   property, plant and equipment   of  Kshs.509,803,798. The balance includes land at a cost of Kshs.6,064,000, motor  v ehicles valued at Kshs.15,987,626, equipment and other machinery of Kshs.7,003,250,  furniture   and   fittings   of   Kshs.19,693,515,   computers   and   ICT   equipment   of  Kshs.13,973,860 and work - in - progress amounting to Kshs.447,081,547. However, the  balances were not   supported by an updated non - current asset register.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of property, plant and equipment  opening balance of Kshs.509,803,798 could not be confirmed.  1038.   Unsupported   Trade and Other Payables Balance  The   statem ent   of   financial   position   reflects   trade   and   payables   balance   of  Kshs.4,469,304,080 as disclosed in Note 16 to the financial statements. Included in the  balance is trade payables amounting to Kshs.2,386,947,335. However, the supporting  ledgers did not incl ude details such as invoice dates and invoice numbers.  Further, the balance includes   an amount of Kshs.32,407,357   due to The   Kenya Power  and Lighting Company’s   (KPLC) for   electricity bills which was at variance with an amount  of Kshs.42,717,024 reflected in the records of the   KPLC . The resultant variance of  Kshs.10,309,667 was not reconciled.  In   addition,   the   statement   of   financial   position   reflects   an   opening   balance   of  Kshs.3,774,932,718 in respect   of   trade and other payables as disclosed in Note 16 to the  financial statements.   However, the circularization of suppliers and a reconciliation of  obtained statements to the County Executive’s records to ensure completeness was not  provided for audit review.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the trade and other payables  balance of Kshs.4,469,304,080 could not be confirmed.  1039.   Unsupported Staff Medical Insurance Costs  The statement of financial performance reflects use of goods and services expenditure  amounting   to   Kshs.4,155,572,191   which,   as   disclosed   in   Note   9   to   the   financial  statements includes insurance costs amounting to   Kshs. 231,258,275 .   Review   of the  contract document s   revealed that the County Executive engaged   an   insurance broker for

496  provision of staff medical insurance cover for two (2) years starting 16 February, 2023 at  a contract sum of Kshs.599,721,288 with a prem ium amounting to Kshs.299,860,644 per  year, for which an amount of Kshs.200,000,000 was paid during the year under review.  However, Management   did not provide documents indicating the full details of the policy  including the list of names of employees cove red and the dependants of each employee.  Further , the number and value of claims honoured or rejected by the insurance company  and   the details of the total payments paid in respect to this contract was not provided for  audit.  In addition , the   insurance cover for staff for a period from February to June, 2025 was not  provided thereby exposing them to risk of not having medical attention by health facilities.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the staff medical insurance cost s  amounting to Kshs.231,258,275 could not be confirmed.  1040.   Long Outstanding Imprests  The statement of financial position reflects an amount of Kshs.152,692,172 in respect of  receivables   from   exchange   transactions   as   disclosed   in   Note   13   to   the   financial  s tatements. Included in the amount is a balance of Kshs.25,332,790 in respect of  outstanding   imprests   balance.   Management   indicated   that   imprests   amounting   to  Kshs.7,681,650 was under investigation by Ethics and Anti - Corruption Commission  (EACC),   Kshs. 6,114 ,580   was   held   by   o fficers   who   exited   the   service   and  Kshs.12,173,160 was submitted for recovery. However, no explanation was provided for  failure to comply with   Regulation 93(5) of the of the   Public Finance Management (County  Governments) Regulations, 2015   which provides that   a holder of a temporary imprest  shall account or surrender the imprest within seven (7) working days after returning to  duty station.  In the circumstances, the accuracy , completeness   and regularity   of the outstanding  imprests amounting to Kshs. 25,332,790 could not be confirmed.  Emphasis of Matter  1041.   Budgetary Control and Performance  The statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts reflects revenue final budget  and   actual   on   comparable   basis   amounts   of   Kshs.13,633,044,511   and  Kshs.11,188,343,410 respectively   resulting in   under - funding of Kshs.2,444,701,101 or  18%   of   the   budget.   However ,   the   County   Executive   spent   an   amount   of  Kshs.10,928,162,004 against   actual receipts   of Kshs. 11,188,343,410   resulting   in   under -  utilization   of Kshs. 268,181,406 or 2% of the actual receipts.  The under - funding affected the planned activities of the County Executive and may have  impacted negatively on service delivery to the public.

497  My opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.  Other Matter  1042.   Unresolved Prior Year Matters  In the previous year audit, several issues were raised under Report on the Financial  Statements, Report on Lawfulness and Effectiveness in the Use of Public Resources and  Report   on   Effectiveness   of   Internal   Controls,   Risk   Management   and   Governance.  However ,   twenty - eight (28) issues were   not satisfactorily addressed and therefore remain  unresolved as listed at the end of this report.  Other Information  1043.   There were no material issues relating to Other Information.  REPORT   ON   LAWFULNESS   AND   EFFECTIVENESS   IN   THE   USE   OF   PUBLIC  RESOURCES  Basis for Conclusion  1044.   Non - Compliance with   the   Fiscal Responsibility Principles   on Wages  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 8 to the financial  statements reflects an expenditure of Kshs.5,983,157,896 in respect to employee costs  which   represents   53%   of   the   total   revenue   for   the   year   amounting   to  Kshs.11,383,133,843 . This was contrary to Regulation 25(1)(b) of the Public Finance  Management   (County   Governments)   Regulations,   2015   which   provides   that   total  expenditure on the wage bill for County Governments should not exceed thirty - five (35)  percent of the County Government’s total revenue.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1045.   Non - Compliance with the Law on Staff Ethnic C omposition  Review of personnel records for newly employed staff revealed that out of six hundred  and forty - two (642) employees employed during the financial year, five hundred and forty -  four (544) or approximately 85% were from one ethnic community.   This   was contrary to  Section   65(1) of the County Government Act, 2012 which stipulates that at least Thirty  percent (30%) of vacant posts at entry level are filled by candidates who are from the  dominant ethnic community in the County.  In the circumstances, M anagement was in breach of the law.  1046.   Employees on   Irregular   Long Probation   Period  Review of   personnel records   for the month of June, 2025 indicated that six hundred and  ninety - four (694) employees   were   serving on probation for long periods of up to twenty

498  (20) years.   Management did not explain the reasons for not absorbing these staff to the  p ermanent and pension able terms. This was contrary to Section 42(2) of the Employment  Act, 2007 which provides that a probationary period shall not be more than six months  but it may be extended for a further period of not more than six months with the agreement  of the employe e  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1047.   Recruitment Without Approved Staff Establishment  Review of the June, 2025 payroll revealed that the County Executive paid seven thousand  and eighty - five (7,085) employees through the Human Res ource Integrated System  (HRIS). Out of the employees, six hundred and forty - two (642) were recruited during the  year under review. However, the recruitment was done without an approved staff  establishment to guide the filling of the positions. Available in formation revealed that the  Bungoma County Public Service Board staff establishment was developed and approved  for implementation in May, 2025 by the County Public Service Board. However, the staff  establishment provided had not been approved by the County   Cabinet.  Further, the County Executive did not have an approved staff establishment at the  beginning of the financial year under review and therefore the optimal staffing levels for  all cadre of staff had not been established. Management did not explain   the mechanism  it relied upon to identify existence of the vacancies filled. This was contrary to Section 5 (f)  of the County Governments Act, 2012 which provides that a County Government shall be  responsible for establishing and staffing its public service   as contemplated under Article  235 of the Constitution.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1048.   Non - Compliance with the Persons with Disabilities Act, 2025  Review of   personnel   records revealed that the County Executive had a staff population  of seven thousand, one hundred and sixteen (7,116) as at June, 2025   out of whom , only  ninety   (90)   employees   representing   1.26%   of   the   population   were   persons   with  disabilit ies .   This was con trary to Section 5(1)(e) of the People with Disabilities Act, 2025  which states that ‘every county government shall promote the inclusion of persons with  disabilities   in the county public service by putting in place measures to ensure that at least  five pe r centum of the employment positions are filled by persons with   disabilities .  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law .  1049.   Non - Compliance with   the   One - Third Rule on Basic Salary  Review of the staff payroll revealed that some employees’ salary deductions exceeded  two - thirds (2/3) of their basic salary in eleven (11) months during the year.   This was  contrary to Section 19(3) of the Employment Act, 2007 which stipulates that without

499  prejudice to any right of recovery of any debt due and notwithstanding the provisions of  any other written law, the total amount of all deductions made by an employer from the  wages of his employee at any one time shall not exceed two - thirds of such wages.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1050.   Irregular   Employment of Staff on Contract Without Gratuity Provision  The   County Executive employed five hundred and sixty - six (566) employees and seventy  (70) employees in the Departments for H ealth and Agriculture respectively. However, it  was observed that the staff were engaged on contract without gratuity provision. This was  contrary to Paragraph D . 32(2) of the Bungoma County Human Resource Policy and  procedures Manual, 2024 which provides t hat all officers who are on contract are eligible  for gratuity.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the   human resources manual .  1051.   Failure to Provide Monthly Progress Reports of all Procurement Contracts  Review of various project   records   revealed that important information was missing in the  contracts signed which included commencement dates, completion dates and duration of  the contract. The   P roject   I mplementation   T eam also failed to provide   M onthly   P rogr ess  R eports of all the procurement contracts. This was contrary to Section 152 of the Public  Procurement   and   Asset   Disposal   Act,   2015   and   Regulation   140(2)   of   the   Public  Procurement and Asset Disposal Regulations, 2020 which provide s   that   the Head of  Procu rement   function   shall   prepare   a   monthly   progress   report   of   all   procurement  contracts and submit the same to the Accounting Officer   and   shall include contract  description; contract number; value of contract; commencement date; current status; the  amount of   money paid; and the expected completion date.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the   law .  1052.   Incomplete Project Implementation Status Report  The County Executive did not provide a detailed   P roject   I mplementation   S tatus   R eport  with   details such as t ender number, financial year of award of contract, name of  contractor,   project   details,   commencement   date,   proposed   completion   date,   actual  completion date, name of supervising   e ngineer, contract sum, total payments and  percentage completi on . Therefore, it was not possible to ascertain the number of projects  approved for implementation, completed,   in progress, not started and stalled.  In   the   circumstances,   the   effectiveness   of   projects’   implementation   could   not   be  confirmed.  1053.   Irregular Pay ment   of   Subscriptions to   Lake Region Economic Block  The County Executive paid an amount of Kshs.3,500,000 to Lake Region Economic Bloc  for subscriptions for the year under review. However, Management did not provide any

500  document indicating that the entity   was   recognized by the law. Further, the agreement for  Lake Region Economic Bloc provides that the financial statements will be audited by the  Auditor - General, however, the Economic Bloc did not submit financial statement s for  audit.   This was contrary to Section 37 of the Intergovernmental Relations Act, 2012 which  provides   that the operational expenses in respect of the structures and institutions  established in the Act shall be provided for in the annual estimates of the   revenue and  expenditure of the National Government.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of law.  1054.   Irregularities in the   Distribution of Fertilizer  The County Executive awarded a contract to a local company on 17 December, 2024 at  a contract   sum of Kshs.50,452,200 for the supply of planting and top - dressing fertilizers  to the forty - five (45) Wards.   T he County Executive awarded a contract to a local firm on  18 February, 2025 at a sum of Kshs.56,250,000 for the supply of planting and top -  dressin g fertilizers   and   made payment on 22 March, 2025 amounting to Kshs.26,000,000  and t he fertilizer was delivered in the financial year 2024/2025.   Further, r eview of  Bungoma County Finance Act, 2023 indicated that the subsidized fertilizer was to be sold  at K shs.2,000 per bag for planting fertilizer and top - dressing fertilizer. However, no  supporting documents were provided for audit to confirm that the fertilizer was sold at the  recommended price of Kshs.2,000 per bag or distributed to the farmers free of cha rge.  In the circumstances,   value for money for the expenditure on purchase and distribution  of fertilizer could not be confirmed .  1055.   Unsatisfactory Renovation of Cattle Dips  The County Executive awarded a contract to a local company at a contract sum of  Kshs.2,915,954 for the renovation of two cattle dips at Maraka and Namwela Wards.  However, the cattle dips were not functional for almost one (1) year, the wood   fence   from  the   entry point to exit point were worn out and the structures were not strong enough to  handle   cattle , the surrounding fence was not existing, vandalism of the wooden posts and  the cemented floors were cracked   with overgrown grass .  In the circumstances, value for money   for the expenditure on the cattle dips could not  be confirmed .  1056.   Irregularities in the   Construction of Masinde Muliro Stadium  The County Executive awarded a contract for construction of Masinde Muliro Stadium to  a local   company on 26 April, 2019 at a contract sum of Kshs.679,386,376 which was later  revised to an amount of Kshs.807,464,800. The initial completion date was 14 June, 2021  but was revised four times and the last revised completion date was 16 December, 2025.  Review of payments records revealed that the Company was paid   an amount of  Kshs.39,711,882 as the final payment for   various   Certificate Numbers which had been  partially paid. However, the current status of the project could not be established as

501  Management   did not provide information on site instructions, schedule of outstanding  works, and the title deed for the land on which the stadium is built.  Further, a udit inspection conducted on 23 July, 2025 revealed that the works had stalled  for more than one   (1) year and the contractor was not on site   and t he external fence that  was built had structural defects. A section of the fence facing the VIP entrance was  bending outwards thereby forming a huge crack on the floor between the fence and the  adjacent groun d. No explanation was provided for the defects. In addition, some officers  had already moved in and occupied the office block even before completion of the project  and hand over for occupation.  In the circumstances, value for money   spent on the project c ould not be confirmed .  1057.   Unutilized Completed   High - Altitude Training Centre  The County Executive awarded a contract for construction of High - Altitude Training  Centre to a local company on 16 November, 2023 at a contract sum of   Kshs.30,980,230.  During the year under review, the company was paid an amount of Kshs.11,558,042 .  However, a lthough the project was completed and handed over to   the County Executive  it   had not been opened for use   and   the land ownership documents were not p rovided for  audit review.  In the circumstances, value for money   for   the   expenditure on the project could not be  confirmed .  1058.   Delayed Completion of Chwele Vocational Training Centre  The County Executive through the Department for Education awarded a contract for  erection and completion of Chwele Vocation Training Centre at a contract sum of  Kshs.30,337,295 on 7 May, 2020 for a project duration of twenty - six (26) weeks or six (6)  month s. The commencement date was 14 May, 2020 and the completion date was  14 October, 2020. During the year under review, the County Executive paid   an amount  of   Kshs.5,000,000. However, the audit verification revealed that the project had stalled  and   Management did not provide the measurement sheets to confirm the value of works  done.  Further ,   information   provided   revealed   that   the   contract   was   terminated   on  26 September, 2023 after the contractor abandoned the site for   over nine (9) months.  There was no evidence that due process was followed in the termination process. This  was   contrary   to   Regulation   141   of   the   Public   Procurement   and   Asset   Disposal  Regulations, 2020 which provides for the process of contract termination.  In the circumstances,   value for money for the expenditure on the project could not be  confirmed .  1059.   Delayed Completion of Governor’s Residence  The County Executive awarded a   contract   for construction of Governor’s residence at a  contract sum of Kshs.40,120,900 on 27 June, 2023. The contract period was fifty - two (52)

502  weeks from 14 August, 2023 and the expected completion date was 13 August, 2024.  Payments amounting to Kshs.17,473,250 w ere made during the year under review to the  contractor. However, audit inspection conducted on 15 July, 2025 revealed that the  project was incomplete and the last   P roject   S tatus   R eport indicated 55% completion and  minimal work was ongoing. However, the su bstructure and superstructure works, and  formwork for a staircase and suspended floor slab had been done. Further, hoarding  works were indicated to have been done but during the site visit only the front side of the  site had   been done   increase   the   possibil ity of unauthorized access.  In addition, there was no evidence provided to confirm whether the contractor had sought  for extension of the contract period or a default notice issued to the contractor by the  County Executive for failure to comply with the   contract.  In the circumstances, value for money may not have been realized from the project.  1060.   Stalled Construction of the Deputy Governor’s Residence  The County Executive awarded a contract for the construction of the Deputy Governor’s  residence   at   a   con tract   sum   of   Kshs.35,980,200.   The   contract   was   awarded   on  27 June, 2023 for a contract period of fifty - two (52) weeks from 14 August, 2023 to  1 3 August, 2024. The contract period had since lapsed and no payment has been made  to   date. Audit inspection conducted on 15 July, 2025 revealed that only site clearance  and excavation of foundation trenches and securing of the site through hoarding had been  done.   However , no work was ongoing at the time of inspection and the contractor ha d  abandoned the site.  Further, the   P roject   I mplementation   S tatus   R eport was not provided and there was no  evidence provided to confirm whether the contractor had sought for extension of the  contract period or a default notice issued to the contractor by the County Executive for  breach of contract. In addition , the land ow nership documents were not provided for audit.  In the circumstances, value for money may not have been realized from the stalled  project.  1061.   Stalled Construction of County Aggregation and Industrial Park  The County Executive awarded a contract for the construction of County Aggregation and  Industrial Park at a contract sum of Kshs.474,153,714 on 28 August, 2023 for a period of  twenty - four   (24) months with an expected completion date of 28 September, 2025.   The  scope of work included boundary fence, access road and parking, foot paths around the  building, storm water drainage, septic tank, borehole, ablution block, power and pump  houses,   office   block,   warehouses,   cold   storage   rooms,   civil   works,   electrical   an d  mechanical works. During the year under review, the contractor was paid amounts of  Kshs.37,430,000 and Kshs.40,000,000 for Certificate No. 2 and 3 respectively. The  cumulative payments as at 30 June, 2025 amounted to Kshs.168,448,114. However, the  audit   could not establish the current status of the project since Management did not

503  provide information on the project status or contract data, schedule of outstanding works  and title deed for the land.  Further, a udit inspection conducted on 2   July, 2025 revea led that the contractor was not  on site and no work was ongoing.   In addition , the works on the warehousing had been  done up to basement level only and the walling of the offices were done up to the first  floor.  In the circumstances, value for money   for   th e expenditure of Kshs.168,448,114 spent on  the project   could not be confirmed .  1062.   Construction of Kanduyi   -   Sang’alo Junction Road to Dual Carriage  The County Executive entered into a contract for construction   of Kanduyi   -   Sang’alo  Junction Road to Dual Carriage (C33)   on 27 December, 2018 at a contract sum of  Kshs.1,382,442,975.   The road has a length of 6.7 Kilometers. The contract period  recorded was for   twenty - four   (24) months and was expected to be completed on  2 2 October, 2021. The objective of the contract was to construct and expand the road   to  d ual   c arriage way.   The scope of the works included preliminaries and general works, site  clearance, earth works, excavation and filling of structures,   culverts and drain age works,  passage of traffic, natural material subbase and base, graded crushed   –   subbase and  base, bituminous service treatment and surface dressings, bituminous mix bases, binder  courses and wearing courses, concrete works (Box Culvert and closed lined   drain), road  furniture,   sexually   transmitted   diseases   and   HIV/AIDS   prevention   awareness   and  education and street lighting.  Further, t he contract was revised through an addendum dated 3 June, 2022 which  increased the contract sum by an amount of Kshs.191,2 85,204 to Kshs.1,573,728,108.  The revised completion date was 21 July, 2022 and there was no evidence of any further  extension of the contract period. As at the time of audit in the month of July, 2025, the  contractor had been paid a total amount of Kshs.1 ,371,481,891. The status report dated  June, 2025 from the Resident Engineer indicated that the project was 94% complete.  However, the following major works were observed   to   be outstanding;   -  (i)   Under Bill No. 16   –   Bituminous mix bases, a 50mm Asphalt concret e wearing  course had not been done.  (ii)   Under Bill No. 17   –   Concrete works, a Foot Bridge costing Kshs.50,000,000  had not been done.  (iii)   Under Bill No. 20   -   Road Furniture works were still outstanding; Road marking  was done temporarily on the incomplete road.  (iv)   Bill No. 26   –   Street lighting. This was done by another State Agency during the  Madaraka Day celebrations on June, 2024. However, this item which had been  planned to cost Kshs.24,286,000 has not been removed from the Bills of

504  Quantities (BQ). Further, the   street lighting done appear not to comply with the  provisions of the BQ as the lighting was done using concrete posts instead of  steel street lighting round posts.  Audit inspection conducted on 21 July, 2025 revealed the following:  (i)   The road project was incomplete and no work was ongoing as the contractor  was not on site.  (ii)   The road although incomplete was open to motorists and pedestrians which  wa s a risk as it had no foot bridges.  (iii)   The road was not properly drained   as s ome sections   were retaining flood water  already shortened the life of the road.  (iv)   The exit roads at the town   c enter were not served with drainage system linked  to the existing culverts and were likely to empty all the water to the surface of  the dual carriage way thereb y increasing the damage to the road.  In the circumstances, value for money   for   the expenditure of Kshs.1,371,481,891   could  not be confirmed.  1063.   Rehabilitation of Sio/Mayanja/Sihilila and Nandingwa Rivers  The County Executive entered into a contract for   rehabilitation of Sio/Mayanja/Isihilila and  Nandingwa Rivers in South Bukusu, Kimaeti and Bumula wards   on 6 September, 2024  at a contract sum of Kshs. 5,917,200. The rehabilitation involved the   supply of indigenous  tree seedlings, bamboo, grass planting, s ite preparation, protection and maintenance of  the seedlings and was expected to be completed on 6 December, 2024.   The contractor  has been   paid a total of Kshs.2,957,944 on 14 March, 2025.  Audit inspection conducted on 8 July, 2025 revealed that there we re incidences of sand  harvesting which contributed to uprooting of the tree seedlings ,   extensive encroachment  and cultivation of maize crop in the areas where tree seedlings had been planted. Further,  there were cattle grazing along the rivers which have c ontributed to reduced numbers of  surviving seedlings. In addition, there was no proper maintenance of the surviving tree  seedlings.  In the circumstances, value for money   for   the expenditure of Kshs.2,957,944   could not  be confirmed .  1064.   Proposed Erection and   Completion of County Public Service Board Offices  Review of projects records revealed that the County Executive awarded a tender to a  construction company for the erection and completion of County Public Service Board  Offices at a contract sum of Kshs.52,497,283 on 13 April, 2023 and was to be completed

505  a fter   fifty - two   (52) weeks on 12 April, 2024. However, review of the project files revealed  that the County Public Service Board had requested for a change of site for construction  of the office from Ndengelewa Market to plots situated between Ngarisha Sacc o and  Bungoma Law Courts nine (9) months after the contract was signed.  Further, as at the time of the audit, the contract had lapsed and there was no evidence of  extension of the contract duration. Audit inspection conducted on 14 July, 2025 revealed  th at the office block was at first floor slab work, the site lacked enough space for storage  of materials and the project implementation committee had not issued any monthly  progress reports. This was contrary to Regulation 140 (1) of the Public Procurement   and  Asset Disposal Regulations, 2020 which requires the Head of Procurement Function to  prepare a monthly progress report of all procurement contracts and submit the same to  the Accounting Officer in accordance with Section 152 of the Act.  In the circums tances, Management was in breach of the law and value for money on the  project could not be confirmed.  1065.   Delayed   Construction   of   Early   Childhood   Development   Education  Classroom and Pit Latrines in Luuya Bwake Ward  The County Executive through the Department for Education awarded a contract for the  construction of one (1) Early Childhood Development Education (ECDE) classroom and  two (2) door pit latrines at Lwanda PEFA, Luuya, Maanga and Kiboochi Primary Schools  in   Luuya Bwake Ward at a contact sum of Kshs.6,077,470 on 29 June, 2022. The project  was to take twenty - four (24) weeks commencing on 30 June, 2022. Review of records  provided for audit revealed that the contractor was paid an amount of Kshs.865,640 for  certi ficate number 1.   It was further observed that the contract was terminated on  15 December, 2023 for breach of contract after the contractor abandoned the site for one  month without the authority of the Project Manager. However, there was no   evidence that  due process was followed in the termination process. This was contrary to Regulation  141 of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Regulations, 2020 which provides the  procedure for termination of contracts.  Further, audit inspection cond ucted in the month of July, 2025 at Lwanda PEFA Primary  School revealed that no work was ongoing since the contractor had abandoned the site.  The ECDE classroom construction had the sub - structure and walling done up to lintel  level. However, the contractor   did not construct a wall on the right side but relied on the  existing wall of the adjacent classroom contrary to the drawing design which made a  provision   for an   independent classroom and space exist between the old and new the  classroom. The abandoned co nstruction had caused accumulation of water that was  flowing to the existing classroom. The walling thickness done was 150mm instead of  200mm specified in the Bills of Quantities. Further, construction of the two (2) door pit  latrine was not done and no wo rk had started in the other two (2) ECDE Centres.  In the circumstances, value for money on the expenditure of Kshs.865,640 could not be  confirmed.

506  1066.   Delayed Completion of ECDE Classroom and Two (2) Door Pit Latrine at  Lukhome Baptist Primary School  The County Executive through the Department for Education awarded a contract for  erection and completion works for one ECDE classroom and two (2) door pit latrine at  Lukhome Baptist Primary School for a contact sum of Kshs.1,495,570. Review of records  reve aled that the contractor was paid   an amount of   Kshs.1,238,404 for certificate  number 1.  Further, a udit inspection conducted in the month of July, 2025 revealed that the ECDE  classroom was complete and in use. However, the floor was already peeling - of f.   In  addition , the pit latrine was abandoned after excavation was done. As a result, the  excavated pit was filled with rain water and not properly covered thereby posing great  danger to the pupils .   As a result of the stalled latrine construction, the popu lation of about  six hundred (600) pupils were greatly disadvantaged and forced to share the existing six  (6) door pit latrine available which was in a deplorable state.  In the circumstances, value for money on the expenditure of Kshs.1,495,570   could not b e  confirmed .  1067.   Construction of Vocational Training   Centres   without Ownership Documents  The Department for Education contracted a local company for fencing and construction  of one classroom at Ngoli Vocational Training Centre (Craft Centre) at West Bukusu at a  contract sum of Kshs.1,774,200. However, Management did not provide ownership  docum ents   for   the   land   for   the   Training   Centre,   including   title   deeds,   leases,   or  Memorandum of Understanding for use of the parcel of land.  In the circumstances, the ownership status of the land could not be confirmed.  1068.   Failure to Transfer Funds to Kimilili and Bungoma Municipalities  The County Executive did not transfer funds that were budgeted for Bungoma and Kimilili  Municipalities .   Instead,   the funds were spent by the County Executive on behalf of the  two (2) Municipalities. Further, the operations were carried out by the County Executive  through the Departments for Lands, Housing, Urban Areas Development and Physical  Planning, and Road and P ublic Works.   This was contrary to Section 21(1)(a) of the Urban  Areas and Cities Act, 2011 which gives Municipalities executive authority as delegated  by County Executives.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

507  REPORT ON EFFECTIVE NESS OF INTERNAL CONTROLS, RISK MANAGEMENT  AND GOVERNANCE  Basis for Conclusion  1069.   Incomplete   Fixed Assets Register  The statement of financial position reflects property, plant and equipment balance of  Kshs.1,832,761,089 as disclosed in N ote 15 to the   financial statements. The amount  relates to land, motor vehicles, equipment and other machinery, furniture and fittings,  computers and ICT equipment and work in progress. However, Management did not  maintain a proper fixed asset s   register showing the date   of acquisition, name of supplier,  details   of   the   asset,   cost/valuation   amount,   depreciation   amount   for   the   year,  accumulated depreciation and net book value.  In the circumstances, the   effectiveness of   internal controls in the management of assets  could n ot be confirmed .  1070.   Lack of Adequate Repairs and Maintenance of Server Room  The County Executive through the Department for Public Service Management, paid an  amount of Kshs.620,000 for maintenance of server room and LAN at the headquarters.  The payment was a pending bill for completed works of upgrading server room which was  last   done on 19 June, 2023. However, there were no system installed in the facility to  warn on possible fire outbreak.  In the circumstances,   the effectiveness of internal controls   to   ensure   safety of Data and  ICT Systems   could not be confirmed .  1071.   Lack of   Departmental Training Committee and Training Needs Assessments  Review of the training documents provided revealed that various Departments had not  established Departmental Training Committees to manage the training function through  the County Public Servi ce Board. Further, the County Executive had not designed a  training needs assessment manual   and human resource skills inventory   to help in training  projections, needs and nomination of officers on areas of importance.  In the circumstances, the   effectivene ss   of achieving a competent work force may not be  achieved.  1072.   Lack of Serviced Fire Equipment, Fire Assembly Points and Fire Safety Alarm  System  Audit verification carried out on 9 July, 2025 revealed that the firefighting equipment and  facilities including fire extinguishers and fire hose - pipe were not serviced, the assembly  points had not been marked and a fire alarm safety system had not been installed.

508  Further, the firefighting equipment were last serviced on 19 November, 2011 casting  doubt whether the fire equipment w as   still effective.  In the circumstances, Management may not be able to mitigate risks   of   loss of   property,  records and lives in case of fire outbreak.  1073.   Lack   of   an   Approved   Information   Communication   Technology   Policy,  Business Continuity Plans and Disaster Recovery Plan  Review of Information Communication Technology (ICT) governance documents, field  verifications and interviews with management revealed that the County Executive did not  have an approved ICT poli cy.   Whereas the draft policy document had been tabled before  the County Executive Committee, Management did not provide timelines indicating the  action plans which would lead to the approval of the ICT policy and subsequent  submission to the County Assemb ly for approval. Further, ICT equipment were not tagged  for identification . Additionally,   the County Executive did not have   B usiness   C ontinuity   P lan  and   D isaster   R ecovery   P lans in place.  In the circumstances, the   effectiveness of the Internal   Controls in safeguarding ICT  infrastructure and County operation in case of a disaster could not be confirmed .  1074.   Failure to Implement the Recommendations made by the Internal Audit  Function  The Internal Audit Department conducted audit assignments and reported on their  findings. However, there was no evidence that the issues raised were acted upon by  Management.  In the circumstances,   the   effectiveness of the Internal Audit Function   could not be  confirmed .
