529  COUNTY EXECUTIVE OF SIAYA   –   NO.41  REPORT ON THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS  Basis for Qualified   Opinion  1113.   Inaccuracies in Employee Costs  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 9 to the financial  statements reflects an amount of Kshs.2,975,810,506 in respect of employees’ costs.  However, review of monthly payroll summaries revealed employees’ costs amounting to  Kshs. 3,396,136,478, resulting in unreconciled variance of Kshs.420,325,972.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of employees’ costs amounting to  Kshs.2,975,810,506 could not be confirmed.  1114.   Unapproved and Unr econciled   Salary Arrears Payments  T he statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 9 to the financial  statements reflects an amount of Kshs.2,975,810,506 in respect of employee costs.  Included in these payments were salary arrears amounting to Kshs.99,694,941 which  were paid   to employees across various Departments. However, no evidence of approval  was provided in support of the payments. Further, no reconciliation on staff arrears  schedule payable in each month, the nature of arrears paid and the period the arrears  relate to w as provided for audit. In addition, there was no ageing analysis of staff arrears  to support the expenditure since all salaries were remitted monthly to employees through  the Integrated Payroll and Personnel Database (IPPD) system.  In the circumstances,   the accuracy and regularity of the employee costs amounting to  Kshs.99,694,941 could not be confirmed.  1115.   Unsupported Insurance Costs  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 10 to the financial  statements reflects an amount of Kshs. 2,023,283,907 in respect of use of goods and  services. Included in this amount is insurance costs amounting to Kshs.404,537,414, out  of which an expenditure of Kshs.30,000,000 was paid to an insurance brokerage firm for  provision of staff medical insuranc e cover. Management provided quotations and cover  notes for the financial year 2014/2015 (ten (10) years ago), which indicated that the sum  insured   covered   one   thousand   and   seven   hundred   (1,700)   employees.   However,  documents relating to the policy and the   contract agreement indicating the details of  premium payable, nature of risk covered, extent of coverage and any other services were  not provided for audit. In addition, Management did not provide evidence on how the staff  members were identified and selec ted.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of insurance costs amounting to  Kshs.30,000,000 could not be confirmed.

530  1116.   Irregular Payments to Members of the County Assembly  The statement of financial performance reflects use of goods and services expenditure  amounting   to   Kshs.2,023,283,907   which   as   disclosed   in   Note   10   to   the   financial  statements includes domestic travel and subsistence amount of Kshs.323,767,894.  Review of r ecords revealed payment of cash allowances amounting to Kshs.1,713,600 to  Members of the County Assembly (MCAs) for a consultative meeting in Kisumu regarding  the Siaya County Annual Development Plan. However, these payments which ought to  have been paid b y the County Assembly, were irregularly charged to the County  Executive without.  In the circumstances, the regularity of the domestic travel and subsistence expenditure  amount of Kshs.1,713,600 could not be confirmed.  1117.   Unconfirmed Trade and Other Payables  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 32 to the financial statements  reflects   a balance   of Kshs.1,889,967,165 in   respect of   trade and   other payables.  However, the balance includes an amount of K shs.14,925,862 in respect of provision of  security and cleaning services which was not supported by Local Service Orders (LSOs),  Inspection and Acceptance Reports, job cards for cleaning works done and work  attendance register.  In the circumstances, the   accuracy and completeness of the trade and other payables  balance of Kshs.14,925,862 could not be confirmed.  1118.   Non - Compliance with Transitional   International Public Sector Accounting  Standards   Requirements  Note 2 to Financial Statements on Statement of   Compliance and Basis of Preparation of  the financial statements. Management has taken advantage of the transitional provisions  under   International   Public   Sector   Accounting   Standards   (IPSAS   33).   However,  Management has not indicated the elements of the fina ncial statements that have not  been recognized and the steps being taken towards full compliance with IPSAS Accrual.  In the circumstances, the financial statements presentation and disclosure could not be  confirmed.  1119.   Variance in Transfers from County Revenue Fund  The statement of financial performance reflects an amount of Kshs.6,958,101,730 in  respect of transfers from County Revenue Fund (CRF). However, CRF statement of  financial   performance   reflects   transfers   to   C ounty   Executive   amounting   to  Kshs.6,982,478,853 resulting in unreconciled variance of Kshs.24,377,123.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the transfers from County  Revenue Fund amounting to Kshs.24,377,123 could not be confirmed.

531  1120.   Inaccuracies in Outstanding Imprest   Amounts  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 22 to the financial statements  reflects receivables from exchange transactions balance of Kshs.4,551,674. The balance  relates to temporary imprest due for surrender on or before 30 June, 2024 and   had not  been surrendered by the time of audit.  Further, the statement of financial position reflect a balance of Kshs.4,551,674 while the  imprest register reflected an outstanding imprest amount of Kshs.4,005,674 resulting in  an unreconciled variance of   Kshs.546,000.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the outstanding imprest amount  of Kshs.546,000 could not be confirmed.  1121.   Unexplained Voided Transactions  Review   of   financial   records   revealed   that   two   thousand   three   hundred   and  twenty - three   (2,323)   transactions   in   Integrated   Financial   Management   Information  System (IFMIS) amounting to Kshs.4,081,328,220 were voided. However, no evidenc e  was provided to confirm that the Controller of Budget was informed of the voiding of the  payments so as to make necessary adjustments and approvals.  In the circumstances, completeness and regularity of the voided transactions amounting  to Kshs.4,081,32 8,220 could not be confirmed .  Emphasis of Matter  1122.   Budgetary Control and Performance  The statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts reflects final receipts budget  and   actual   amounts   on   comparable   basis   amounts   of   Kshs.9,602,122,988   and  Kshs.7,4 58,918,285 respectively, resulting in an under - funding of Kshs.2,143,204,703 or  22%   of   the   budget.   However,   the   County   Executive   spent   an   amount   of  Kshs.7,486,087,487   against   actual   receipts   of   Kshs.7,458,918,285,   resulting   in  over - utilization   of Kshs.27,169,202.  The under - funding affected the implementation of planned activities and programmes and  may have impacted negatively on service delivery to the public.  My opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.  Other Matter  1123.   Failure to Disburse Climate Change Funds  Review of the programme - based budget revealed that the Climate Change Fund had a  budget estimate of Kshs.137,000,000 under grant from The National Government for  Financing Locall - Led Climate Action (FLLoCA). However, the Fund did not receive any  grants from The National Treasury   during the year under review.

532  1124.   Unresolved Prior Year Matters  In the previous year audit report, several issues were raised under the Report on Financial  Statements, Lawfulness and Effectiveness in Use of Public Resources, and Effectiveness  of   Internal Controls, Risk Management and Governance. Review of the status during in  2024/2025 revealed that thirty (30) issues listed at the end of this report remained  unresolved as at 30 June, 2025.  Other Information  1125.   Ther e were no material issues relating to Other Information.  REPORT   ON   LAWFULNESS   AND   EFFECTIVENESS   IN   THE   USE   OF   PUBLIC  RESOURCES  Basis for Conclusion  1126.   Failure to Operationalize Climate Change Regulations  The statement of financial performance and as dis closed in Note 13 to the financial  statements reflects an amount of Kshs.301,184,243 in respect of other grants and  subsidies which includes an amount of Kshs.132,573,505 in respect of Climate Change  Fund. The Siaya County Climate Change Fund was enacted t hrough an Act of County  Assembly on 28 October, 2021. However, Management was yet to operationalize the  regulations.   This was contrary to Section 31 of the Siaya County Climate Change Act,  2021, which states that ‘’the County Executive Committee Member fo r the time being  responsible for climate change affairs shall in consultation with the steering committee  and, with the approval of the County Assembly make Regulations for the better carrying  into effect the provisions of this Act’’.  In the   circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1127.   Non - Compliance with   Persons with Disabilities Act, 2025  Review of payroll records revealed that the County Executive had two thousand eight  hundred and sixty - five (2,865) employees as at 30 May, 2025,   out of whom only sixteen  (16) employees or 0.56% were persons with disabilities. This was contrary to Section  5(1)(e) of the Persons with disabilities Act, 2025 which provides that every county  government shall promote the inclusion of persons with disabil ities in the county public  service by putting in place measures to ensure that at least five per centum of the  employment positions are filled by persons with disabilities.  Further, physical inspection of County Executive’s infrastructure carried out in Ju ne, 2025  revealed that most of the Departmental offices did not have suitable ramps, accessible  toilets and lifts. This was contrary to Section 5(1) of the Persons with Disabilities Act, 2025  on provision and modification of facilities in the work place as   may reasonably be required  to accommodate persons with disabilities.

533  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1128.   Non - Compliance with the Law on Staff Ethnic Composition  Review of the County Executive’s payroll records indicated that out   of two thousand seven  hundred and ninety - four (2,794) employees, two thousand five hundred and four (2,504)  or approximately 90% of the total number were from the dominant ethnic community in  the County. This was contrary to Section 7(1) and (2) of the Na tional Cohesion and  Integration Act, 2008 which provides that no one community should hold more than thirty  percent (30%) of the positions. Although Management indicated that majority of the  County employees were inherited from the defunct Local Authority   who were mainly from  one (1) ethnic community, no effort has been taken to address the issue.”  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1129.   Non - Compliance   With the Law on Affirmative Action  Review of procurement and payment records and other relevant supporting documents  revealed that   Management did not allocate at least 30% of its annual procurement budget  to enterprises   owned by youth, women and persons with disabilities. This was contrary to  Regulation 149 of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Regulations, 2020 which  states   that   “a n   Accounting   Officer   of   a   procuring   entity   shall,   when   processing  procurement under   Section 157(5) of the Act, allocate at   least thirty percent (30%)   of its  annual procurement budget for the   purposes of procuring goods, works and services from  enterprises   owned by youth, women and persons with disabilities”.  In the circumstances, Managem ent was in breach of the law.  1130.   Non - Compliant with the Public Procurement and Disposal Act, 2015  Review of procurement records revealed that County Executive contracted a firm to  supply   and   deliver   computers   and   its   accessories   for   the   Integrated   Revenue  Management System under framework contract arrangements at a contract sum of  Kshs.20,536,439 .   However,   no   evidence   was   provided   for   audit   to   show   that  Management prepared an annual value for money assessment to determine whether the  terms in the Framework   Agreement remained competitive. This was contrary to   Section  114   (2)   of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015 which states that ‘’t he  maximum term for the framework agreement shall be three years and,   for agreements  exceeding one year, a val ue for money assessment undertaken   annually to determine  whether the terms designated in the framework agreement   remain competitive ’’ .  Further, no evidence was provided to indicate that the Accounting Officer reported the  contracts awarded to Public Procu rement Regulatory Authority as required in Section  138(2) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015.  In the circumstances, value for money on the expenditure amounting to   Kshs.20,536,439  could not be confirmed.

534  1131.   Delay in Construction   of Siaya County Aggregation and Industrial Park  The County Executive through the Department for Trade, Cooperatives, Investment and  Industries awarded a tender for the construction of County Aggregation and Industrial  Park to a loc al firm at a cost of Kshs.483,688,922 in September, 2023. This project was  to be co - funded by the County Executive and the National Government through the  Department for Trade and Industrialization shared equally. However, review of the  project’s cashbook   revealed that the National Government had made a transfer of only  Kshs.62,500,000 as at 30 March, 2025 leaving a balance of Kshs.179,344,461 or 74% of  the share for funding.  Further, schedule one (1) of the framework required that the Industrial Park shou ld have  a minimum area of ten (10) hectares, accessible to major transport facilities with clear  status of ownership and that the Industrial Park should have basic facilities such as roads,  electricity, water and sewerage. However, the identified location   of the project lacked the  required facilities.  In addition, review of the Project Progress Report dated 9 September, 2024, revealed  that the overall project completion was at 12%. Therefore, the project was behind  schedule since forty - eight (48) weeks had   lapsed against the initial approved contract  period of eighty (80) weeks translating to 60% of the initial contract period. Management  did not provide any evidence to explain the delays in completion. Physical inspection  carried out in October, 2025 revea led that the contractor was not on site and the project  had stalled.  In the circumstances, value for money for the expenditure of Kshs.62,500,000 incurred  on the project could not be confirmed.  1132.   Delay in Construction of Early Childhood Development Education Block at  Maranyona Primary School  Review of procurement records revealed that during the 2022/2023 financial year, the  County Executive awarded a contract for construction of Early Childhood D evelopment  Education   (ECDE)   Block   at   Maranyona   Primary   School   at   a   contract   sum   of  Kshs.4,134,669 for a period of twelve (12) weeks commencing May, 2023. However,  physical inspection carried out in July, 2025 revealed that the contract was yet to be  comple ted over twenty - five (25) months from the contract date.  Further, works relating to painting, tiling, glass fixing and construction of latrine were  incomplete despite the expiry of the project duration and no evidence was provided for  audit in respect of   the extension of the project period. This was contrary to Section 139  (2) (a) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015 which requires an  Accounting Officer of a procuring entity to approve extension of contract period on the  recommendation o f an evaluation committee and be justified by the tenderer.  In the circumstances, value for money for the expenditure amount of Kshs.4,134,669  could not be confirmed.

535  1133.   Irregular   Tender   Variation   of   the   completion   of   Early   Childhood  Development Education   (ECDE) Classrooms at Nyandheho Primary School  Management through the Department for Education entered into a contract for the  proposed at a total cost amounting to Kshs.2,985,462. Review of supporting documents  revealed that Management varied the   project by an amount of Kshs.265,542. However,  there was no evidence to indicate that the cost variation was evaluated and approved.  This was contrary to Section 139(1) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act,  2015 which provides that an amendment   or a variation to a contract resulting from a  procurement proceeding is effective only if the variation or amendment has been  approved in writing by the respective tender awarding authority within a procuring entity.  In the circumstances, Management was i n breach of the law.  1134.   Stalled Completion of Early Childhood Development Education Block at  Nyabera Primary School  The   County   Executive   engaged a   company for the   proposed completion of   Early  Childhood Development Education (ECDE)   Block at Nyabera Primary School at a  contract sum of Kshs.4,307,957. The project commenced on 9 March, 2022 and was  scheduled for completion in June, 2022 with a project period of twelve (12) weeks. Review  of pr ocurement records revealed that the contractor had requested for an extension which  was granted on 21 December, 2023 for a period of three (3) weeks. However, as at July,  2025 the project had stalled with the delay exceeding the original contract period by  seventeen (17) months. The contractor was not on site, and the project location was in a  state of neglect. No evidence was provided on measures being taken to complete the  project.  In the circumstances, the value for money on the funds spent on the projec t could not be  confirmed.  1135.   Failure to Install Medical Equipment  Review of procurement records revealed that County Executive through the Department  for Health awarded a tender to a company to supply, deliver and install medical equipment  at Siaya Hospita l Theatre Complex at a cost of Kshs.22,974,650 in January, 2025. Stores  records revealed that the equipment was delivered and received in the stores on 6  February, 2025. Review of payment records indicated that the County Executive had paid  the contractor   an amount of Kshs.20,477,338 or 89% of the contract sum. However,  physical inspection carried out in October, 2025 revealed that the medical equipment was  yet to be installed and commissioned eight (8) months after delivery with some of them  stored in the   open and unsecured spaces exposing them to dust, moisture and physical  deterioration.  In the circumstances, value for money on the expenditure amounting to Kshs.20,477,338  could not be confirmed.

536  1136.   Unutilized County Facilities  The County Executive awarded a contract for proposed construction of maternity block at  Malunga Dispensary   at a cost of Kshs.4,400,000. However, physical inspection in July,  2025 revealed that the facility was complete but not in use.  Further, Management   through the Department for Environment, Water, and Natural  Resources awarded a contract   to drill and equip two (2) boreholes in Ligose Primary and  Ligala Dispensary at a contract cost of Kshs.5,819,100.   However, physical inspection  carried out in July, 2 025 revealed that the borehole at Ligose Primary School was non -  operational due to vandalism while the borehole at Ligala Primary School had evidence  of piping leakages and corroded steel rails supporting the overhead tank as a result of  poor paint works p osing structural integrity risks.  In addition,   Management awarded a contract for drilling and equipping of a borehole at  Yenga. However, physical inspection of the project in October, 2025 revealed that the  borehole was not functional due to lack of water   from the elevated storage tank to the  outlet tank. The paint works on the steel rails supporting the elevated tank were poorly  done, thus exposing them to corrosion.  In the circumstances, value for money for the expenditure amounting to Kshs.10,219,100  c ould not be confirmed.  1137.   Irregular   Payment of Allowances  Review of the Integrated Payroll and Personnel Database (IPPD) and Government  Human Resource Information System (GHRIS) records revealed that several officers  were overpaid house allowances amounting to Kshs.22,331,251 in excess of their  approved   job   grade   entitlement   as   prescribed   by   the   Salaries   and   Renumeration  Commission.   Further,   payroll   records   revealed   that   medical   personnel   were   paid  emergency call allowances at rates exceeding those approved by the salaries and  Renumeration   Commission   (SRC) circula r Ref: SRC/TS/CGOVT/3/61 Vol.III/(136) dated  14 September, 2016 which states that ‘’emergency call allowance is payable at the rate  Kshs.30,000’’. No evidence was provided to confirm that the staff were either medical  doctors, dentists or pharmacists deplo yed in the County hospitals as stipulated by the  SRC Circular on health workers allowances.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1138.   Non - Adherence to Approved Staff Establishment  Review of the County staff establishment revealed that Management approved three (3)  and one (1) staff in respect of Job Groups A and B respectively. However, review of the  May, 2025 GHRIS payroll data revealed that the County had two hundred and seventy -  s ix (276) employees in Job Group A and fifteen (15) employees in Job Group B, resulting  in   excess   staff   by   two   hundred   and   seventy - three   (273)   and   fourteen   (14)   staff  respectively.

537  Further audit review   of the Integrated Payroll and Personnel Database (IPP D) records for  the month of June, 2025, revealed that job designations for sixteen (16) officers were not  defined in the database. This was contrary to Section B.3 of the County Public Service  Human Resource Manual, 2013 which provides that all appointment s and designations  must be based on an approved staff establishment and any creation or re - designation of  positions must be authorized by the Board in accordance with the existing organizational  structure and mandates.  In the circumstances, Management wa s in breach of the law.  1139.   Employees   Without   Personal Numbers  Review of payroll records and Departmental returns revealed that a total of four hundred  and forty - nine (449) employees   did not have personal numbers assigned to them.   No  explanation was provided why personal numbers were not issued. This was contrary to  P art 3.1 (vi) of the Payroll Management Policy for the Public Service, 2024, which states  that “all public service employees whose salaries are paid from the consolidated fund  shall be issued with a Unified Payroll Number (UPN)”. UPN is a unique identifier   for public  service employees that track employment history across public service organizations from  entry to exit.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1140.   Unsupported   Recruitment   of Employees  Review of the human resource records and co rrespondences maintained by the Siaya  County Public Service Board revealed that six hundred and eight (608) employees were  appointed between 7 January and 10 February, 2025. However, supporting documents  such as advertisements, shortlisting records, interv iew minutes, and appointment letters  were not provided for audit. Management explained that the records of the County Public  Service Board were submitted to the Ethics and Anti - Corruption Commission (EACC), as  per the copy of inventory dated 24 September,   2025.  In the circumstances, the regularity in recruitment of new employees could not be  confirmed.  1141.   Failure   to Provide Staff   Appointment   and Posting Documents  Review of sampled personnel records revealed that the County Executive appointed  nineteen (19) health officers. However,   appointment and deployment letters of twelve (12)  officers were not provided for audit. Further, another sample of personnel files of s ix (6)  health officers requested for audit were not provided. This was contrary to Section 9(1)(e)  of the Public Audit Act, 2015 which states that ‘’without prejudice to the powers given  under the Constitution and this Act and for the purposes of carrying   out his or her duties  effectively, the Auditor - General, or an officer authorized for the purpose of this Act, shall  have powers of unrestricted access to all books, records, returns, reports, electronic or  otherwise and other documents of entities listed u nder Article 229(4) of the Constitution’’.

538  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1142.   Irregularities in the Construction of Modern Early Childhood Development  Education Centre in Bondo Sub - County  The County Executive entered into a contract for the construction of a modern Early  Childhood Development Education (ECDE) Centre in Bondo Sub - C ounty. Review of  payment records and documents revealed that Management made an advance payment  amounting to Kshs.10,931,825 or 20% of the contract sum in accordance with the special  conditions   of   the   contract.   However,   the   justification   on   the   Payment,   Pr oject  Implementation Status Report and details of the mobilization of plant, equipment and  materials to the site were not provided for audit.  Physical   inspection   conducted   in   July   and   October,   2025   revealed   unauthorized  alterations in the construction incl uding use of steel nails instead of U - bolt cups for fixing  galvanized corrugated iron sheets, alterations in window installations and rafters in roof  trusses were spaced 4.4 meters apart instead of the two (2) meters specified in the Bills  of Quantities. N o documentary evidence for approval of the changes by the Accounting  Officer was provided to justify these changes. This was contrary to   Section 151 2(a) and  (b) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015 which provides that the  Accounting Offi cer shall be responsible for monitoring the performance of the contractor,  to ensure that all delivery or performance obligations are met or appropriate action taken  by the procuring entity in the event of obligations not being met; ensure that there is ri ght  quality and within the time frame, where required.  In the circumstances, value for money for the expenditure amounting to Kshs.10,931,825  could not be confirmed and Management was in breach of the law.  1143.   Delayed Supply, Delivery, Installation and Commis sioning of Mortuary Cold -  Room Plant  Review   of   procurement   records   revealed   that   the   County   Executive   contracted   a  company for the supply, delivery, installation and commissioning of a mortuary cold - room  plant at Bondo Sub - County Hospital at a contract sum   of Kshs.54,685,880. The contract  was awarded on 4 April, 2024 for a period of twelve (12) weeks with an expected  completion date of   27 June, 2024. However, as at the time of the audit in October, 2025,  the cold room plant had not been installed. This wa s contrary to Section 151 2(a) and (b)  of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act 2015, which requires the implementing  team to monitor contract performance and ensure that all required milestones are properly  maintained. Further, although the Contra ctor was on site, the contract period had lapsed,  no extension had been requested and granted. This was contrary to Section 139(2) of the  Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015 which requires approval of contract  extensions by the Accounting Offic er.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

539  1144.   Non - Compliance with Fiscal Responsibility Principles on Wages  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 9 to the financial  statements reflects employees’ amounting   to Kshs.2,975,810,507 representing 43% of  the total receipts amount of Kshs.6,958,101,730. This was contrary to Regulation 25(1)(a)  and (b) of the Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015  which requires that the County Government’s   expenditure on wages and benefits for its  public officers shall not exceed 35% of the County Government’s total revenue.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1145.   Non - Compliance with Fiscal Responsibility Principles on Debt  The statement of financial position reflects total liabilities totalling   Kshs.1,891,436,239  representing 27% of the total revenue amount of Kshs.6,958,101,730. This was contrary  to   Regulation   25(1)(d)   of   Public   Finance   Management   (County   Governments)  Regulations, 2015 which provides that the County public debt shall never exce ed twenty  (20%) percent of the County Governments total revenue at any one time.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1146.   Long Outstanding Trade and Other Payables  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 32 to the   financial statements  reflects trade and other payables balance of Kshs.1,889,967,165. Review of pending bills  schedule revealed that bills totalling Kshs.184,615,904 were brought forward from prior  years. However, pending payables dating back to ten (10) y ears have not been settled  and no reason has been provided for the failure to pay the bills. This was contrary to  Regulation 41(2) of the Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations,  2015 which states that ‘’debt service payments shall be a   first charge on the County  Revenue Fund and the Accounting Officer shall ensure this is done to the extent possible  that the county government does not default on debt obligations’’. Further, failure to settle  bills during the year to which they relate dis torts the financial statements and adversely  affects the budgetary provisions for the subsequent years as they form a first charge.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  REPORT ON EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROLS, RISK MANAGEMENT  A ND GOVERNANCE  Basis for Conclusion  1147.   Weaknesses in the   Legal   Department  The   County   Executive   paid   legal   fees   totalling   Kshs.25,505,473   to   various   firms  representing the County Executive in various legal disputes and court cases. Review of  legal documents and expenditures records provided for audit revealed   that the County  Executive did not have a substantive County Attorn ey during the year under review.

540  Further, the Office of the County Attorney had an approved staff establishment of twenty -  two (22) legal officers out of whom only five (5) legal officers were in place representing  22% of the approved capacity. This was con trary to Section 4 (1 and 2) of the County  Attorney Act, 2020 that requires County Governments to establish an Office of the County  Attorney which will consist of County Attorney, County Solicitor and such other number  of legal counsels.  In   addition, review of a payment amounting to Kshs.2,100,000 on a court case of 2014  revealed that a judgment had been made in favor of a dismissal of a County Executive  Member on 19 January, 2017 as compensation for twelve (12) months’ salary together  with 3 1% gratuity for the period served. In a letter dated 22 February, 2022 Management  was advised to pay Kshs.9,083,062 which included accumulated interest. However, a  report from the Legal Department indicated that the County Executive still owed balance  of K shs.4,829,862 as at 30 June, 2025. The delay to clear the claim may expose the  County Executive to further avoidable expenditure.  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of the legal Department in carrying out its  mandate could not be confirmed.  1148.   Weakness es in Internal Audit Function  Review of the Internal Audit Function and governance revealed that the County Executive  had an Internal Audit Function in place with a total staff of twelve (12) officers including  five (5) support staff instead of the approv ed staff establishment of nineteen (19) technical  officers resulting in understaffing by seven (7) officers. Further, the staff were not  members of professional bodies such as Institute of Certified Public Accountants of Kenya  and Institute of Internal Aud itors but were accountants seconded from the Finance  Department. Information obtained from the Management indicated that the officers  carrying out duties of the internal audit were employed as ward administrators and  deployed to the Unit casting doubt on t he effectiveness of the internal audit function.  In addition, review of the programme - based budget revealed that the Department’s  budget was reduced from Kshs.11,539,329 to Kshs.8,139,329. This allocation included  Kshs.3,006,620 to the Audit Committee.  Further, the Internal Audit Function submitted to Management four (4) audit reports on  various Departments and sections outlining the recommendations to be implemented by  the Management. However, Management did not provide evidence on the implementation  of   the audit recommendations.  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of the Internal Audit Function and risk governance  of the County could not be confirmed.  1149.   Weakness in Information Communication Technology Internal Control  Management did not have an approved Information Commutation Technology (ICT)  Strategic   Plan   for   governance   and   management   of   Information   Communication  Technology ((ICT) resources. In addition, there was no evidence of an ICT steering  committee in place to   assist in the development of ICT Policy framework to enable

541  Management   realize   long - term   ICT   strategic   goals.   There   was   also   no   formal,  documentation to confirm that emergency procedures had been tested. Further, there  was no evidence of disaster recovery   plans inform of backups stored in a secure off - site  location to allow for business continuity in the event of an unforeseen disaster(s).  In the circumstances, effectiveness on the ICT controls and governance could not be  confirmed.  1150.   Irregular Double Payme nt of Salary  Review of the Integrated Payroll and Personnel Data (IPPD) records and manual payrolls  at the Siaya County Referral Hospital revealed that a staff member was paid both as a  casual and a permanent and pensionable employee. This resulted in double payment to  the officer.  In the circumstances, effectiveness in internal controls in management of payroll could  not be confirmed.  1151.   Lack of Human Resource Plans and Policies  Review of human resources records revealed that the County Executive lacked   a n Annual  Rec ruitment Plan , Career Progression Guidelines and Human Resource   Plans. It was  therefore not possible to confirm the appropriateness of the current staffing level   for  achieving the County Executive’s strategic objectives.  In the circumstances, the existence of an effective control mechanisms on human  resource management could not be confirmed.

543  COUNTY EXECUTIVE OF   KISUMU   –   NO.42  REPORT ON THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS  Basis for Qualified   Opinion  1152.   Non - Compliance with International Public Sector Accounting Standards  Reporting Requirements  Management did not disclose in Note 2 to the financial statements on statement of  Complian ce and Basis of Preparation of the specific transitional provisions applied or  steps   taken   towards   full   compliance   with   International   Public   Sector   Accounting  Standards (IPSAS) accrual. Further, Management did not indicate the elements of the  financial sta tements that had not been recognized as a result of taking advantage of the  transitional provisions outlined in IPSAS 33.  In the circumstances, the disclosure and fair presentation of the financial statements  could not be confirmed.  1153.   Inaccuracies in the F inancial Statements  The statement of financial performance reflects an amount of Kshs.9,100,755,678 in  respect of transfers from the County Revenue Fund (CRF), while the CRF financial  statements reflects an amount of Kshs.9,290,898,968 resulting in unreconciled and  unexplaine d variance of Kshs.190,143,290. Further,   the statement of cash flows under  cashflows from investing activities, reflects an amount of Kshs.388,118,718 relating to  purchase of property, plant and equipment, while the statement of comparison of budget  and ac tual amounts reflects an amount of Kshs.376,231,334 for the same component  resulting in unreconciled variance of Kshs.11,887,384.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the financial statements could  not be confirmed.  1154.   Lack of Land Ownershi p Documents  The statement of financial position reflects property, plant and equipment balance of  Kshs.393,322,516 as disclosed in Note 15 to the financial statements. Included in the  property, plant and equipment balance is addition to assets amount of Kshs.19,000,00 0  paid for acquisition of a ten (10) acre piece of land. However, the title deed for the land  was not provided for audit to confirm the ownership status.  In   the circumstances, the ownership of property, plant and equipment balance of  Kshs.19,000,000 coul d not be confirmed.  1155.   Unsupported Trade and Other Payables  The statement of financial position reflects a balance of Kshs.5,944,565,373 in respect of  trade and other payables as disclosed in Note 17 to the financial statements. Included in

544  the balance is an   amount of Kshs.4,074,201,380 in respect of verified pending bills out of  which a balance of Kshs.1,240,781,349 has been outstanding for over three (3) years  while an amount of Kshs.301,930,175 was outstanding for between two (2) and three (3)  years. Howev er, the ageing analysis and supporting records for payables amounting to  Kshs.1,870,363,993 were not provided for audit.  Further, review of the supporting schedule provided for audit revealed that payments  totalling Kshs.112,161,062 paid during the year w ere not listed or disclosed as part of the  pending bills in the audited financial statements for the previous years.  In the circumstances, the accuracy, completeness, and obligation of trade and other  payables balance of Kshs.1,870,563,993 could not be co nfirmed.  1156.   Unsupported Customers Deposits  The statement of financial position reflects a balance of Kshs.46,149,043 in respect of  refundable deposits and prepayments as disclosed in Note 18 to the financial statements.  However, supporting ledgers provided for audit reflected a balance of Kshs.42,3 13,576  resulting in unreconciled variance of Kshs.3,835,467.  In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of refundable deposits and  prepayments balance of Kshs.46,149,043 could not be confirmed.  Emphasis of Matter  1157.   Budgetary Control and Performance  The statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts (recurrent and development  combined)   reflects   final   receipts   budget   and   actual   on   comparable   basis   of  Kshs.14,214,711,871 and Kshs.9,241,631,511 respectively, resulting in an under - funding  of Kshs.4,973,080,360 or 35% of the budget. However, the County Executive spent  Kshs.8,569,136,546 against actual receipts of Ks hs.9,241,631,511 resulting in under  expenditure of Kshs.672,494,965 or 7 % of the accrual receipts.  The under - funding affected the planned activities and may have impacted negatively on  service delivery to the public.  My opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.  Other Matter  1158.   Unresolved Prior Year Matters  In the previous year’s audit report, several issues were raised under the Report on  Financial Statements, Lawfulness and Effectiveness in Use of Public Resources, and  Effectiveness of Internal Control s, Risk Management and Governance. Review of the  status during audit of the County Executive in 2024/2025 revealed that thirty - nine (39)  matters listed at the end of this report remained unresolved as at 30 June, 2025.

545  Other Information  1159.   There were no material issues relating to other information.  REPORT   ON   LAWFULNESS   AND   EFFECTIVENESS   IN   THE   USE   OF   PUBLIC  RESOURCES  Basis for Conclusion  1160.   Procurement Process Undertaken after Cut - off Date  The statements of   financial position and as disclosed in   Note 17 to the financial  statements reflects trade and other payables balance of Kshs.5,944,565,373. Included in  the balance is   an amount of   Kshs.4,074,201,380 payables to third parties. Review of the  procurement documents and payment vouchers revealed tha t the County Executive,  through the Department of Water, Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resources,  initiated the procurement of several water projects after the 31 May, 2025 cut - off date.  However, explanation and documentation provided by Manageme nt did not demonstrate  justification or explanations warranting deviation from approved procurement timelines .  This was in contravention of The National Treasury Guidelines on implementation of  2024/2025 budget which required that no new procurement activi ties were to be initiated  beyond the set cut - off date of 31 May, 2025 of the financial year to allow for proper  financial closure and absorption planning within the fiscal year.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1161.   Irregular   Procur ement   Process   on   Purchase   of   Computers   and   Other  Equipment  The statement of financial position reflects property, plant, and equipment balance of  Kshs.393,322,516 as disclosed in Note 15 to the financial statements. The balance  represents additions made d uring the year, excluding historical assets. Included in the  balance are computers and related equipment amounting to Kshs.27,160,611.   The  amount included Kshs.2,977,500 paid to a company that was prequalified under provision  of construction and other civi l works and had a framework agreement to supply general  office supplies but was irregularly invited to bid and awarded a contract to supply  computers, while two hundred and seventy - seven (277) companies prequalified under  the category of computer supply we re denied an opportunity to bid and compete fairly.  This was contrary to Article 227(1) of the Constitution of Kenya 2010, that states when a  state organ or any other public entity contracts for goods or services, it shall do so in  accordance with a system   that is fair, equitable, transparent, competitive and cost -  effective.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

546  1162.   Irregular Award of Contracts  Note 8 to the financial statements reflects expenditure on use of goods and   services  amounting to Kshs.2,374,381,143, out of which Kshs.795,722,748 relates to repair and  maintenance of access roads and other roads. Review of procurement records for  selected projects revealed material irregularities in the procurement and tender ev aluation  processes as outlined below;  1162.1.   Award of Contract to an Unqualified Bidder  A   firm   was   awarded   a   contract   amouting   to   Kshs.3,939,447   for   the   opening   and  maintenance   of   the   Glory - SDA - Baba   Selina - Kobaso - Kodeny   Corner   Access   Road.  Review of the procurement file revealed that tender evaluation was conducted on 31 May,  2024 and the following irregularities were noted:  1162.1.1.   Ove r - scoring at Technical Evaluation  Under the general experience criterion, the successful bidder was awarded sixteen (16)  marks, exceeding the maximum allowable score of thirteen (13) marks. Further, based  on the documentation provided, the bidder was only   eligible for four (4) marks under this  criterion.  1162.1.2.   Improper Assessment of Financial Capability  Under the financial capability criterion, the bidder was awarded nine (9) marks for  submission of certified audited financial statements. However, the financia l statements  submitted were incomplete and related to irrelevant financial years (2018 and 2019)  instead of the required recent years (2021, 2022, and 2023).  As a result of the inflated technical scores, the bidder attained a total of sixty - one (61)  mark s, thereby qualifying for financial evaluation and ultimately being awarded the tender.  However,   had   the   evaluation   been   conducted   in   accordance   with   the   tender  requirements, the bidder would have scored forty (40) marks, which was insufficient to  qualify   for progression to the financial evaluation stage.  1162.2.   Non - Compliance with Tender Requirements  A   company   was   awarded   a   contract   for   the   improvement   of   Kokumu - Naki - Pap  Ndege   -   Korona Road at a contract sum of Kshs.4,993,986 on 14 March, 2025. Review  of the procurement file revealed that the procurement method used was request for  quotations.   Three   (3)   tenderers   were   invited   to   bid   and   they   all   responded   and  consequently the c ompany was deemed the most responsive. However, review of the  tender documents revealed that a ll bidders were required to attach a copy of single  business permit/trading license. It was noted that the winning bidder attached a single  business permit belong ing to another business entity. Based on the above, the bidder  should have been disqualified at preliminary evaluation stage and excluded from further  consideration.

547  Further, a t technical evaluation, the bidder was awarded fifty - five (55) marks out of a  m aximum of seventy 70 marks. Review of the tender documents revealed that the bidder  failed to provide evidence of meeting the required parameters. For example; eight (8)  marks were awarded for general experience proof by attaching copies of reference  lette rs/LPOs and or contracts of four (4) such assignments carried out by the bidder for  public and private sector organizations. Further, under specific experience in similar  works,   twelve   (12)   marks   were   awarded   without   demonstrating   or   providing   any  supporti ng documentation. Further, on financial capability six (6) marks were awarded for  attaching certified audited accounts for the last three financial years. However, these  accounts were not provided for audit.  1162.3.   Improvement of Nyamasaria Bridge   -   Kasaoke Access Road  A local contractor was awarded a contract for the improvement of Nyamasaria bridge   -  Kasaoke access road at a contract price of Kshs.3,470,723 on 21 June, 2024. Physical  inspection during the audit on 23 July, 2025 revealed that the co ntractor installed a total  of twenty - eight (28) culverts which were in four (4) different locations. Approximately one  (1) year and one month after the project completion the following were observed;  The head walls, wing wall, aprons and the surround of t he culverts had deteriorated with  some   culverts already   blocked   and   structural   components   did   not   meet   standard  specifications with visible cracks already evident. Additionally, the concrete on some  culverts   was   clearly   visible   indicating   deficiencies   in   b ackfilling,   gravelling   and  compacting works, which contributed to development of substantial potholes. Further,  after the third culvert, it was noted that a ditch had been dug across the road rendering it  impassable and most sections of the road exhibited   rough patches and large potholes,  indicating poor workmanship.  1162.4.   Failure to Prepare and Maintain a Roads Infrastructure Register  The County Executive did not maintain a roads infrastructure register as required by The  National Treasury Guidelines issued on July, 2020 in respect of asset and liability  management reporting registers and templates. The roads infrastructure register sho uld  include   details   such   as   road   description,   road   ID,   length   in   kilometers,   date   of  commissioning, type of road, mode of funding, useful life, and cost.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of Law and value for money on the  expenditure incurre d on the projects could not be confirmed.  1163.   Non - Compliance with Gender Representation Requirements in the County  Executive Committee  Article 179(2) of the Constitution of Kenya provides that the County Executive Committee  (CEC) shall consist of the   Governor, Deputy Governor, and members appointed by the  Governor with the approval of the County Assembly. Review of the composition of the  County Executive Committee revealed that it comprised of twelve (12) members, of whom  three (3) were female and nine   (9) were male. As a result ,   more than two - thirds of the  appointed members were of the same gender, contrary to the constitutional principle of

548  affirmative action as outlined under Article 27(8) which stipulates that not more than two -  thirds of the members   of any appointive body shall be of the same gender.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1164.   Non - Compliance with National Cohesion and Integration Act, 2008  Review of human resource records as at 30 May, 2025 revealed that out of a tot al of four  thousand, eight hundred and thirty - four (4,834) employees four thousand, two hundred  and fifty - three (4,253) representing 88% of employees in the County Executive were from  the dominant ethnic community, in the County contrary to the provisions   of Section 7(2)  of the National Cohesion and Integration Act, 2008. This section requires that no public  institution shall have more than one - third of its staff from the same ethnic community.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the   law.  1165.   Non - Compliance with the Persons with Disabilities Act, 2025  Review of the payroll records and staff bio data for the year under review revealed that  the total number of employees as at 31 March, 2025 stood at four thousand, eight hundred  and   thirty - f our   (4,834).   Out   of   this   number,   only   sixty - nine   (69)   employees   were  categorized   as   persons   with   disabilities,   constituting   1.4%   which   was   below   the  recommended level of 5% under Section 5(1e) of the Persons with Disabilities Act, 2025  which requires Count y Governments to promote inclusion of persons with disabilities in  County Public Service by putting in place measures that ensure that at least five (5%) of  the employment positions are filled by person with disabilities.  In the circumstances, Management   breached the law.  1166.   Failure to Develop and Maintain Skills Inventory and Succession Plan  The County Executive did not maintain a skills inventory for all its employees in the  respective departments for the purpose of identifying the available and the   required skills  to guide training and succession management. This was contrary to Section 11.14 of the  County Government of Kisumu Human Resource and Procedures Manual that requires  authorized Officers to develop, analyze, update and maintain a comprehensi ve skills  inventory for all staff in their respective departments for purposes of identifying the  available and required skills.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the County Human Resource and  Procedures Manual.  1167.   Non - Compliance   with   Fiscal   Responsibility   Principles   on   Allocation   to  County Assembly  Review of approved budget for County Executive revealed that the County Assembly was  allocated Kshs.1,108,619,656 for both recurrent and development expenditure. The total  revenue   of   the   County   Executive   was   Kshs.9,080,593,167.   Review   of   the   County  Revenue   Fund statement of financial performance for the year ended 30 June, 2025

549  revealed transfer to County Assembly of Kshs.1,055,601,131. However, this amount  exceeded   the   ceiling   of   Kshs.635,641,522   by   Kshs.419,959,609.   This   allocation  represents approximatel y 12% of the total revenue contrary to Regulation 25(1)(f) of the  Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which sets the  funding to County Assembly at a maximum of 7% of the total revenues of the County  Government.  In the circums tances, Management was in breach of the law.  1168.   Irregular Wages to Casuals  Review of manual payrolls revealed that during the year under review, wages amounting  to Kshs.23,848,817 was paid to Casuals.  However, approved   staff   establishment   showing   deficiency   of   staff   to   be   filled   by  temporary employees and formal request by the   user departments to engage temporary  employees and evidence of authorization by the County Public Services Board to the  departments to recruit temporary employees were not provided for audit .  Further, records in respect of how temporary   employees were hired, the work for which  they were hired for, criteria for their recruitment, terms and conditions of services and  master rolls showing attendance of the temporary workers were also not provided for  audit.  In the circumstances, the regular ity and value for money on wages amounting to  Kshs.22,848,817 paid to casuals could not be confirmed.  1169.   Non - Compliance with Law on Fiscal Responsibility Principle on Wages  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 7 to the financi al  statements reflects expenditure totalling Kshs.5 ,748,210,378   in respect of employee  costs.   The   amount   represents   approximately   63 %   of   the   total   revenue   of  Kshs. 9,080,593,167 . This was contrary to Regulation 25(1)(a) and (b) of the Public  Finance Managem ent (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which provides that the  County Executive Committee member with the approval of the County Assembly shall set  a limit on the County Government expenditure on wages and benefits for its public officers  and that the   limit set shall not exceed thirty - five (35) per cent of the County Government’s  total revenue.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.  1170.   Unremitted Statutory Deductions  The statement of financial position reflects a balance of Kshs.5,838,359,852 in respect of  employees’   benefits obligations and as disclosed in Note 20 to the financial statements.  However, this amount includes Kshs.5,075,728,885 in respect of unremitted co ntributions  to the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) comprising of outstanding balance of  Kshs.4,808,421,118, penalties of Kshs.256,259,007 and May and June, 2025 NSSF

550  contributions of Kshs.11,048,760. This was contrary to Section 27(1) of the National  Social   Security   Fund   Act,   2013   which   states   that   if   any   contribution   for   which   a  contributing employer is required to pay to the Fund is not paid within one month after the  end of the month in which the last day of the contribution period to which it falls , a sum  equal to five per cent of the amount of that contribution shall be added to the contribution  for each month or part of a month that the amount due remains unpaid, and any such  additional amount shall be recoverable at the same time and in the same   manner as the  contribution to which it is added.  Further, review of pension documents provided for audit revealed that the County  Executive owed an amount of Kshs.611,244,643 to four (4) pension funds which comprise  of principle outstanding contributions   amounting to Kshs.135,956,307, interest amount of  Kshs.419,476,604 and arrears of Kshs.1,582,854. This was in contravention of Section  19(4) of the Employment Act, 2007, which states that an employer who deducts an  amount from an employee’s remuneration in   accordance with subsection (1)(a), (f), (g)  and (h) of the Act shall pay the amount so deducted in accordance with the time period  and other requirements specified in the law, agreement, court order or arbitration as the  case may be.  In the circumstances , Management was in breach of the law.  1171.   Avoidable Legal Costs  The statement of financial performance reflects use of goods and services expenditure  amounting   to   Kshs.2,374,381,143   which   includes   other   operating   expenses   of  Kshs.163,703,661 out of which Kshs.5,000,000, was paid to a law firm. The payment was  for legal   dues for certified amount of debt, interests, retention and costs for a case  between the County Executive and a construction company. The court made a decree in  favour of the contractor for undertaking construction of a hawkers ’   market but the payment  cer tificates were not fully honoured prompting the contractor to move to court. According  to the court decree, the final payment certificate amount was Kshs.5,260,020. Other  claims to be paid were interest on payment certificate, full payment of retention amo unt,  Interest on retention amount, and general damages totalling Kshs.21,016,710.  Review of the court ruling confirmed that the County Executive will eventually spend more  than Kshs.20,000,000 which could have been avoided by complying with the contract  agreements and terms of reference. The high legal costs were incurred as a result of   poor  contract management and conflict resolution by the County Executive.  In the circumstances, value for money on the expenditure could not be confirmed.  1172.   Expenses Incurred on Behalf of Self - Reporting Entities  The statement of financial performance and as disclosed in Note 9 to the financial  statements   reflects   transfers to other government entities balance of Kshs.565,341,363 .  Included in the amount is an amount of Kshs.206,585,822 being payments related to the  City   of   Kisumu   and   Kshs.29,923,120   made   on   behalf   of   Lakefront   Development  Corporation. Review of payments records revealed that the County Executive incurred

551  direct payments on behalf of self - reporting entities instead of transferring all the funds to  th e   entities   account.   This   was   contrary   to   Regulation   83(1)   of   Public   Finance  Management (County Governments) Regulations ,   2015, which states that the County  Treasury   shall   be   responsible   for   establishing   sound   cash   management   systems,  procedures   and   process es,   to   ensure   efficient   and   effective   banking   and   cash  management   practices   ensuring   payments,   including   transfers   to   other   levels   of  government and county - government entities are made when due for efficient, effective  and economical programme delivery and   the county government’s normal terms for  account.  In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law .  1173.   Poor Workmanship on Construction of Pap Konam Agricultural Training  Centre Phase I Project  The statement of financial position and as disclosed in Note 15 to the financial statements  reflect property, plant, and equipment balance of Kshs.393,322,516. The amount includes  the proposed completion of the Pap Konam Agricultural Training Centre Phase   I project,  which was awarded to a local firm at a contract sum of Kshs.9,976,826, out of which  Kshs.8,485,449 was paid on 10 July, 2025. However, site inspection conducted on 29  September, 2025 revealed visible cracks in the two lecture halls, and sections   of the soft  board ceiling had started to wear out and detach from the roof, posing a risk of falling.  In the circumstances, value for money on the expenditure could not be confirmed.  1174.   Irregularities in Procurement and Implementation of Projects  During the year under review, the County Executive awarded contracts amounting to  Kshs13,950,508.   However,   c ontract   for   construction   of   staff   quarters   at   Oriang  Dispensary   was awarded to a local company at a contract price of Kshs.2,198,870. The  contract a greement was signed on 24 February, 2025. However, the technical evaluation  committee recommended the contractor despite the fact that bids submitted were not  responsive as the key mandatory documents used were for another bidder. Further, no  previous work   experience was provided in form of LPOs and award letters.  Further, t he Contract for construction of Muhoroni Mortuary Phase 1 was signed on  7 April, 2025 between a local company and the County Executive at a contract sum of  Kshs.3,995,640.   However, the contractor had abandoned the site, and the project  implementation status report indicated that only 30% of work had   been done.  In addition, t he contract for completion and equipping of a theatre at Gita   was signed on  7 February, 2025 between the County Executive and a local company. However, the  Inspection and Acceptance Committee rejected the anaesthetic machine since it did not  meet the required specifications provided in the tender document.  In the   circumstances, value for money spent on the projects could not be confirmed.

552  REPORT ON EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROLS, RISK MANAGEMENT  AND GOVERNANC E  Basis for Conclusion  1175.   Lack of Annual Recruitment Plans  The County Executive recruited two hundred and one (201) employees during the year  under review. However, review of the recruitment process revealed that the respective  departments did not have an approved annual recruitment plans to guide the hiring  proce ss. Further, no evidence was provided to demonstrate that budgetary approval or  funding confirmation was sought prior to the recruitment. This reflects lack of proper  planning and budgeting procedures.  In   the   circumstances,   the   effectiveness   of   internal   controls   on   human   resource  management could not be confirmed.  1176.   Understaffing in Internal Audit Department  Review of the approved staff establishment for the Internal Audit Department revealed  that the Department was supposed to have seventeen (17 ) officers headed by a Director  of Internal Audit. However, the Department had six (6) officers and one administrative  staff. Shortage of staff in the department may have resulted to reduced oversight.  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of   internal controls, risk management and overall  governance could not be confirmed.  1177.   Internal Controls Weaknesses in Payroll Management  Review of payroll records for the month of June, 2025 revealed that thirty - six (36)  employees were overpaid and the Count y Executive later started making recoveries for  the   overpayments.   As   at   30   June,   2025   the   unrecovered   balance   amounted   to  Kshs.5,485,450. Reasons as to how these salary overpayments occurred were not  provided and therefore it was not possible to confirm ex istence of internal controls in the  management of the payroll data. This contravenes Section 149(1) of the Public Finance  Management Act, 2012 which imposes on an Accounting Officer of a county government  entity the responsibility of ensuring that the reso urces of the entity for which the officer is  designated are used in a way that is lawful and authorized, effective, efficient, economical  and transparent. Further, Regulation 120(3) of the Public Finance Management (County  Governments) Regulations 2015 req uires the Accounting Officer to certify the correctness  of the payroll at least once every month .  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of internal controls over payroll management  could not be confirmed.  1178.   Discrepancies between the   Integrated   Personnel   Payroll Data  Comparison of staff lists submitted by various Chief Officers with the   Integrated   Personnel  Payroll Data   (IPPD) and manual staff registers revealed that there were eighty - five (85)

553  employees who appeared in the IPPD records but were not included in the lists provided  by the Chief Officers. This may indicate that the County Executive paid salaries to  individu als who did not offer services to the County Executive.  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of internal controls on payrall management could  not be confirmed.  1179.   Failure to Update the Fixed Assets Register  Included in the statement of financial position is property, plant, and equipment with an  opening balance as at 1 July, 2024 of Kshs.1,134,368,973. During the year under review  newly acquired assets amounted to Kshs.417,976,865. However, Management did not  maintain an updated assets register. The asset register lacked key information such as  tag number, make and model, original location, current location, purchase amount,  depreciation   rate,   annual   depreciation,   accumulated   depreciation,   net   book   value,  resp onsible officer, and asset condition. It was therefore not possible to confirm the  existence, ownership, and value of assets owned by the County Executive.  Further, it was not possible to establish the location of the assets and the individual staff  memb ers to whom the assets were assigned. This was contrary to Regulation 136(1) of  the Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015, which states  that the Accounting Officer shall be responsible for maintaining a register of assets under  h is or her control or possession as prescribed by the relevant laws.  In the circumstances, the effectiveness of internal controls over fixed assets  management could not be confirmed.  1180.   Uncollected Rent Arrears  Review of payroll record for the month of   June, 2025 revealed that five (5) employees  had rent arrears amounting to Kshs.298,800. Management did not provide reasons why  rent was not deducted from their salaries on monthly basis leading to rent arrears. Further,  the Internal Audit Unit in its repor t dated 7 March, 2024, reported that there were County  employees who were paying rent that was below the market rate. In addition, other staff  occupied County houses and were also earning house allowances yet rent was not  deducted from their monthly earnin gs. Management did not provide responses to the  issue, and no evidence of the action taken to recover the uncollected rent was provided  for audit. The County Executive may have lost revenue as a result of under - charging and  non - deducted rent from County St aff Salaries.  In the circumstances, effectiveness of internal controls and procedures in rent deduction  and remittance could not be confirmed.
